variants.functional_evidence: Minigene assays (pcDNA3.1 and pcMINI-N) in HEK293T and HeLa cells showed complete skipping of exon 8 (c.478_549del), predicting in-frame loss of 24 amino acids (p.Pro161_Gly184del) in the triple-helical domain.
evidence_quotes: A novel heterozygous point variant in the intron 8 splice donor site of COL4A2 (c.549 + 5G > A; NM_001846.4) was identified in the proband (II-1; Fig. 2a) by PCR-based Sanger sequencing (Fig. 2b).
Analysis of the DNA from his parents (I-1 and I-2) was normal, showing that the variant might be de novo in the proband (paternity/maternity testing was not performed).
Fetal brain MRI at 34 weeks confirmed the left subdural hemorrhage and lateral displacement of the cerebrum (Fig. 1a).
Subsequent follow-ups revealed significant developmental delay and cognitive impairment.
Therefore, this novel splice-site variant is considered pathogenic.
variants.notes: Both parents tested negative but paternity/maternity not confirmed and authors say 'might be de novo', so counted as de novo assumed. Transcript NM_001846.4 stated in results; Table 2 uses ENST00000360467.7. Protein consequence is inferred from minigene, not patient RNA.

Five additional rare variants found in both cases and controls (Supplementary Table 3, not legibly parsed) were not extracted. variants.phenotype_details: Sporadic intracerebral hemorrhage in 4 US (GOCHA/ERICH) cases: 2 lobar and 2 nonlobar ICH; ages not individually stated. Also found in 2 ICH-free LBC controls, one with self-reported hypertension and myocardial infarction (not counted as probands).
variants.functional_evidence: In silico molecular dynamics modelling predicted 14.9-35.1% shortening of the alpha1alpha1alpha2(IV) structure and a collagen stability calculator predicted a 2.2°C reduction in Tm; no wet-lab work.
evidence_quotes: rs138269346COL4A1 was present in 4 ICH cases (2 lobar and 2 nonlobar ICH cases) and rs201716258COL4A2 was observed in another 2 ICH cases (1 lobar and 1 nonlobar ICH case).
Turning to the population-based LBC cohort, we identified 2 ICH-free controls who carry the minor allele of rs138269346COL4A1 but no carriers for rs201716258COL4A2.

Rs138269346COL4A1 was deemed pathogenic due to its annotation across multiple prediction tools: moderate by SnpEff, deleterious by SIFT, probably damaging by PolyPhen, and probably damaging by LoFtool.
We detected 2 patients with ICH who carry the minor allele of rs201716258COL4A2 but no carriers for rs138269346COL4A1.
variants.notes: Rare-variant case-control sequencing study; carriers found by screening, no family/segregation data, so n_families=0 and inheritance unknown. n_tested = 2,133 US (1,055 cases/1,078 controls) + 192 LINCHPIN cases + 1,189 LBC controls = 3,514; affected denominator is 1,247 ICH cases. n_total_carriers=6 counts only study-sequenced carriers (4 cases + 2 unaffected controls); additional carriers in UK Biobank (1 of 276 proxy ICH cases; 33 with vascular/heart problems among 137,766) and 5 in Geno2MP are not individual-level. Paper also writes the variant as 'COL4A1I100T' in thermal stability text, apparently a typo. Nominal association with nonlobar ICH p=0.054. Incomplete penetrance evident (present in controls/biobank).

variants.phenotype_details: Sporadic ICH in 2 US cases (1 lobar, 1 nonlobar) and 2 Scottish LINCHPIN cases (nonlobar ICH, lentiform epicenter, low small vessel disease score; 1 male, 1 female, aged 85 and 73 at ICH; no history of ischemic stroke).
variants.functional_evidence: In silico molecular dynamics modelling predicted 15.7% shortening of the triple-helical structure and a collagen stability calculator predicted a 2.1-3.1°C increase in Tm; no wet-lab work.
evidence_quotes: rs138269346COL4A1 was present in 4 ICH cases (2 lobar and 2 nonlobar ICH cases) and rs201716258COL4A2 was observed in another 2 ICH cases (1 lobar and 1 nonlobar ICH case).
For rs201716258, both individuals developed nonlobar ICH in the right ventricle (ICH epicenter was lentiform) with a low small vessel disease score.
The ages of patients (1 male, 1 female) were 85 and 73 at the time of ICH, and there was no history of ischemic stroke.

Both variants were considered pathogenic based on minor allele frequency (<0.00035 in European populations), predicted functional impact (deleterious or probably damaging), and in silico modeling studies (substantially altered physical length and thermal stability of collagen).
variants.notes: Carriers found by case-control screening; no family or parental data. n_tested=3,514 total sequenced (1,247 ICH cases). SIFT tolerated, PolyPhen benign, CADD 4.7 per authors. Not associated with ICH subtypes (p>0.12). Also 6 carriers in Geno2MP and 63 UKB carriers with vascular/heart problems (not individual-level, not counted). Figure 2 caption writes 'rs20176258', apparently a typo.

extraction.extraction_notes: Rare-variant targeted sequencing case-control study of sporadic ICH (GOCHA/ERICH US cohort, LINCHPIN Scottish cases, LBC controls), plus lookups in UK Biobank and Geno2MP. Only the two rare candidate variants found exclusively in cases (in the discovery set) were extracted. Previously reported COL4A2 variants rs117412802, rs62621875 and rs201105747 were detected in both cases and controls and analyzed only for association; not extracted. The 39 annotated functional variants are listed only in Dryad tables e-2 to e-5 (not provided). Tables 1-3 had captions only, no rows. Carrier phenotypes beyond ICH were not reported for study participants.

Microarray SNP/CNV study of two Turkish families with Chiari malformation type I (4 affected, 7 unaffected). The only COL4A1/COL4A2 variants reported are common dbSNP polymorphisms on a genotyping array: COL4A1 rs9521687 (C/A, 5'UTR), described as 'significantly associated with CMI', and seven intronic COL4A2 SNPs (rs73619284, rs8001070, rs9555689, rs7317178, rs12323265, rs9515209, rs4517640). These are association-type common SNPs, not candidate pathogenic variants characterised in specific individuals. The paper does not assign genotypes per individual and gives no HGVS, so no variant records were created. The supplementary CNV table contains no CNV at the 13q34 COL4A1/COL4A2 locus beyond broad LOH regions spanning 13q33.2-q34.

variants.phenotype_details: Three unrelated patients (aged 73, 71, 56) with late-onset cognitive decline (onset 65, 64, 55 y); Fazekas 3 WMH, lacunes, microbleeds, enlarged basal ganglia PVS/status cribrosum (marked in patients 1 and 2, mild in patient 3); patient 1 ischaemic pontine stroke at 65; patient 2 old deep lenticular macrohaemorrhage on MRI; patients 2 and 3 history of depression, apathy, anosognosia; patient 3 frontal behavioural disturbance, recent small deep infarcts, prior episodes of macroscopic haematuria. No cataract/glaucoma/retinal tortuosity reported; no muscle involvement.
evidence_quotes: Patients 1, 2, and 3 carried the same NM_001845.6:c.1420G>A, p.(Gly474Arg) variant.

Comparison with exact Fisher's test showed a significant enrichment for this variant in the of 5600 adult patients addressed in our lab for panel sequencing of genes involved in monogenic cSVDs (3/5600) as compared to gnomAD controls (p = 0.016; odds ratio 5.84; 95% CI 1.18–17.76).

Although the family histories appeared noteworthy because of the repeated occurrence of psychiatric disorders across generations, DNA samples and brain MRI data from family members were unavailable, precluding co‐segregation analyses and limiting the conclusions that could be drawn from these familial observations.
An old, deep, lenticular haemorrhage was observed in patient 2 (arrowhead).
Renal function and urinalysis were normal, although previous episodes of macroscopic haematuria were reported.
variants.notes: Variant present in gnomAD v4.1.0 in 74/806973 individuals (rs752346924). No family members tested; inheritance unknown. Haematuria in patient 3 was historical (Table 1 'Yes'). n_tested = 5600 lab panel pool from which 3 carriers were drawn.

variants.phenotype_details: 71-year-old woman; recurrent major depressive episodes since mid-20s, type 1 bipolar disorder diagnosed at 64; name-memory difficulty for 5 years (cognitive complaint onset 65); moderate executive dysfunction; Fazekas 3 confluent WMH, status cribrosum in lenticular nuclei, deep and lobar microbleeds; moderate chronic renal failure (attributed to nephroangiosclerosis), right renal cysts; retinal arterial tortuosity; chronic diarrhoea; hypertension from 60. Strong family history of suicide/mood disorders.
evidence_quotes: Patient 4 carried a distinct variant: NM_001845.6: c.1457G>A, p.(Gly486Glu), which was absent from the gnomAD v4.1.0 database.
Moderate renal failure (creatinine clearance of 40 mL/min) was found without any proteinuria or haematuria, and several cysts were detected on the right kidney by ultrasound examination.
Ophthalmological examination revealed tortuosity of the retinal arteries.
These two variants were considered likely pathogenic (ACMG class IV) because they involved glycine residues in the triple helical domain of COL4A1 [].
variants.notes: Renal failure was clinically attributed to nephroangiosclerosis, but renal cysts were also present. n_tested not explicitly stated for this variant (likely from the same 5600-patient lab pool, but not stated). No relatives tested.

extraction.extraction_notes: Case series of four unrelated French patients identified by an 8-gene cSVD panel. Pedigrees in Figure 1 show family histories only; no relatives genotyped, so inheritance is unknown for all. UK Biobank p.(Gly332Arg) mentioned only as cited literature and not extracted.

Case-control allele-frequency association study of whole exome sequencing data from 184 unrelated hemiplegic migraine patients, compared with gnomAD Non-Finnish European frequencies by chi-square test. The only COL4A1/COL4A2 variants reported are polymorphisms with rsIDs, cohort MAFs and p-values. These are COL4A1 p.Pro54Leu (c.161C>T, NM_001845.5, rs34004222), found in 4 patients with MAF 0.01 vs gnomAD NFE 0.004205 (chi-square p=0.049). They also include COL4A2 p.Glu1123Gly (c.3368A>G, NM_001846.3, rs117412802), found in 8 patients with MAF 0.022 vs 0.01267 (p=0.121, not significant). No individual-level phenotype, inheritance or family data are given; clinical data beyond the HM diagnosis are stated to be limited. Per the extraction rules, association-study SNPs were not recorded as variant-level evidence. No functional work was done. The COL4A1 p.Pro54Leu variant is noted as previously reported in an optic nerve hypoplasia case and in an ICH association study; these are cited, not new individuals.

variants.notes: Protein change is inconsistently written: p.Glu326Ser in abstract/results/figure legends, but p.G326S in Table 2 and p.Gly326Ser in the Discussion; c.976G>A is at the first base of codon 326, consistent with Gly>Ser. Transcript NM_001303110.2 is a non-canonical COL4A1 transcript, so numbering may differ from NM_001845. Inheritance recorded as inherited based on stated autosomal dominant co-segregation across generations II-IV, but the paper does not explicitly state which parent carries the variant and the pedigree figure was not provided; total carrier count not stated. Keratoconus placed under 'ocular' (corneal disease); it is not a typical COL4A1 phenotype. n_tested=4 reflects four KC families/probands studied (124 individuals total sequenced/genotyped including 100 controls in whom the variant was absent).

extraction.extraction_notes: Paper reports four variants in four keratoconus families; only the COL4A1 variant (family 3) is extracted. PLOD1, COL1A1 and COL5A2 variants omitted as out of scope. Supplementary Table S1 (co-segregating loci) and pedigree figure referenced but not provided. Variant absent in 100 healthy controls. No functional work beyond in silico 3D modelling.

variants.phenotype_details: Man in his early twenties with drug-resistant epilepsy; developed multiple (12) intracerebral hemorrhages in stereo-EEG electrode trajectories within days of implantation, and a lumbar intradural hemorrhage after a diagnostic spinal tap; mild right leg weakness; full recovery. Heavy oral nicotine pouch use. Coagulation studies normal. Carrier mother described as unremarkable/seemingly healthy.
variants.reported_classification: variant of unknown clinical significance class 3 according to the American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics (ACMG)
evidence_quotes: However, we identified a heterozygous mutation c.4698G>T, p.(Trp1566Cys) in COL4A2 (NM_001846.4) encoding a collagen type‐IV alpha‐2 chain, which was inherited from his unremarkable mother.
In detail, there were 12 hemorrhages (>5 mm) affecting 26/172 electrode contacts (15%) on 8/17 electrodes (47%), all ICHs were in the trajectories of the depth electrodes.

Due to pain in both dorsal thighs, a lumbar spine MRI was performed on the twelfth postoperative day and revealed an intradural hemorrhage in an early subacute phase, compatible with the previously performed first lumbar puncture on postoperative Day 2.

First, the pure association of a genetic variant—to date classified as a variant of unknown clinical significance class 3 according to the American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics (ACMG)—does not prove any causative role.
variants.notes: Variant in NC1 domain (non-glycine missense). Hemorrhages were procedure-provoked (SEEG implantation, lumbar puncture). Epilepsy listed under 'other' though WES found no epilepsy gene variant and authors do not attribute epilepsy to the COL4A2 variant. Absent from gnomAD v4. Carrier mother asymptomatic.

variants.phenotype_details: Boy aged 2.5 years, born preterm at 35 weeks (1.7 kg) with an eventful perinatal period. He had global developmental delay, mainly motor, and epileptic spasms from 1 year of age that became drug-refractory and needed polypharmacy and a ketogenic diet. Examination showed microcephaly (HC 42 cm), nystagmus, squint and spastic quadriplegia. EEG showed multifocal epileptiform discharges. MRI showed periventricular white matter hyperintensities, periventricular and porencephalic cysts, old intraventricular hemorrhages, white matter volume loss and a dysplastic corpus callosum. CT showed calcifications in the periventricular white matter and basal ganglia. There were no cataracts, renal ultrasound was normal, echocardiography was normal, and there was no significant family history.
evidence_quotes: The molecular genetic evaluation was later confirmed with a heterozygous mutation of the COL4A1 gene on exon 37 (variant - p.Gly1050Ala) with an autosomal dominant inheritance pattern.
This was classified as a variant of uncertain significance.
MRI Brain and Sanger sequencing were recommended to the parents, after having been screened for renal cysts and cataracts.
There was no significant family history.
Our case had intraventricular hemorrhages as well as porencephalic cysts and periventricular white matter gliosis.
variants.notes: Only protein notation is given (exon 37), with no c. notation or transcript. The variant was found by whole genome sequencing. Parental testing was recommended but not reported, so inheritance is unknown. The phrase 'autosomal dominant inheritance' refers to the inheritance pattern, not to a carrier parent. n_tested is set to 1 because this is a single-patient report.

variants.functional_evidence: Adenoviral overexpression of the Col4a2 c.1838G>T mutant in LPS-stimulated rat CTX-TNA cells and primary astrocytes increased GFAP, iNOS, COX-2, IL-1β, IL-6 and TNF-α and JAK2/STAT3 phosphorylation, and these effects were reversed by the JAK/STAT inhibitor WP1066.
evidence_quotes: 7 | Chr13: 111117813 | COL4A2 | c.1838G>T | p.G613V | Missense | Heterozygous | Mother | NM_001846.4 | Uncertain significance | N
In our study, we identified a child with epilepsy who carried the same Col4a2 mutation as his mother.
In the family history, only patient 7's mother had moderate mental retardation without epilepsy.
7 | 3 y 4 m, M | 10 m | ES | None | Severe→Severe | H→Multifocal | WG→N | TPMVPAPLEVCZPCLBKDTCZ | TCZ | Uncontrolled
variants.notes: The authors classify this variant as VUS yet describe it as showing incomplete penetrance. The functional work used the rat Col4a2 construct in rat cells.

variants.phenotype_details: Patient 8, male, 18 y: epileptic spasms with onset at 9 months; moderate developmental delay improving to mild; EEG multifocal then normal; MRI normal; seizure-free for 16 y.
evidence_quotes: 8 | Chr13: 111156194 | COL4A2 | c.4139G>A | p.G1380D | Missense | Heterozygous | De novo | NM_001846.4 | Likely pathogenic | N
8 | 18 y, M | 9 m | ES | None | Moderate→Mild | Multifocal→N | N→N | P | P | Controlled; Seizure-free for 16 y

extraction.extraction_notes: This is a retrospective series of 8 unrelated patients with 'Col4a2-related infantile epileptic spasm syndrome' from a single centre; the denominator is the 8 patients sequenced by trio WES. Patients with significant brain structural abnormalities were excluded, so none had a classic cerebrovascular COL4A2 phenotype. De novo calls are counted as confirmed because the paper describes trio WES with Sanger confirmation of parental origin. Several variants are non-glycine (P383L, R179H, R579C), and the pathogenic link to COL4A2 is the authors' interpretation. The MRI abbreviation 'WG' and the other table abbreviations are not defined. Functional work covered only c.1838G>T, in rat astrocytes.

variants.phenotype_details: 12-year-old Han-Chinese girl with intermittent dizziness for 5 months, mild learning difficulties and inability to concentrate. Brain MRI showed diffuse periventricular leukoencephalopathy, lacunes in bilateral centrum semiovale, periventricles and basal ganglia, and dilated perivascular spaces in bilateral basal ganglia. Head CT showed patchy low-density areas and punctate calcification in bilateral basal ganglia, presumed by the authors to indicate previous microbleeds. MRA/MRV normal; no cerebrovascular events. Ophthalmic examination, urinalysis and renal ultrasound normal. Diagnosed as MRI-defined covert CSVD.
variants.reported_classification: de novo variant; previously reported as a pathogenic variant
evidence_quotes: Interestingly, we found a de novo variant of COL4A1 gene(NM_001845.6 exon33) c.2662G > A (p.Gly888Arg), which had been reported as a pathogenic variant in a patient with porencephaly and leukoencephalopathy as well as cataract and myopathy [].

Further examination of the brain MRI showed diffuse periventricular leukoencephalopathy, lacunes in bilateral centrum semiovale, periventricles, and basal ganglia, and dilated perivascular spaces in bilateral basal ganglia (Fig. 2A–L).
As the father did not carry the COL4A1 variant which was detected in our patient, his intermittent headaches may be caused by other reasons.
Ophthalmic examination was normal, and no abnormality was found in urinalysis, renal and renal arterial and venous ultrasound.
variants.notes: De novo status based on trio whole-exome sequencing; father explicitly stated to be non-carrier, mother's negative result implied by trio design but not separately stated. The variant was previously reported in a different patient (porencephaly, leukoencephalopathy, cataract, myopathy); that earlier patient is not part of this record. 'Other' reflects dizziness and mild learning difficulties.

extraction.extraction_notes: Single case report. The prior report of the same variant in another patient is cited but not counted.

Population cohort association study (SardiNIA, n=6,301) of arterial stiffness/PWV. The only COL4A1-related variant is the common SNP rs3742207 (described as located in/near COL4A1), analysed by genotype frequencies, effect sizes and p-values in gene-environment interaction models. Per instructions, association polymorphisms are not recorded as variant-level evidence; no specific COL4A1/COL4A2 variants are reported in specific affected individuals. Other SNPs (rs1495448 MAGI1, rs7152623 BCL11B) are unrelated to COL4A1/COL4A2.

variants.phenotype_details: Father (44 y): pediatric epilepsy from age 1 (controlled on phenobarbital, later discontinued), chronic migraines, exertional extremity weakness, horizontal diplopia, chronic cough with hemoptysis, bowel incontinence, venous insufficiency, mildly reduced vibratory sense in great toes; brain MRI with confluent asymmetric deep white matter T2/FLAIR hyperintensity involving basal ganglia/caudate (leukoencephalopathy). Daughter (6 y): autism, childhood seizures/pediatric epilepsy, similar brain MRI white matter findings.
variants.reported_classification: variant of uncertain significance (VUS); title: "Novel, Possibly Pathogenic"
evidence_quotes: The patient's daughter, recently diagnosed with autism, underwent genetic testing, revealing a variant of uncertain significance (VUS) in the type IV collagen alpha 1 (COL4A1) gene.
Genetic testing identified a novel COL4A1 gene variant, c.3698G>A (p.Gly1233Glu), in the patient, which was also carried by his daughter.
In both the patient and his daughter, MRI revealed a confluent increased T2/FLAIR signal in the supratentorial deep white matter with basal ganglia involvement.
The mutation c.3698G>A (p.Gly1233Glu) in the COL4A1 gene is not only identified in the patient but also in his daughter, who has autism and pediatric epilepsy.
variants.notes: One family: father (case-report subject) and daughter (first tested, genetic index). Counted as one proband; inheritance recorded as inherited assuming the daughter is the index case, since she carries the father's variant. The father's own inheritance (from his parents) is not reported; if the father is treated as proband, inheritance would be unknown. No transcript stated. Paper erroneously states glycine replaced by 'glutamine' though p.Gly1233Glu is glutamate.

extraction.extraction_notes: Single-family case report; no transcript given; no functional work. Daughter's genetic testing details reported only briefly.

variants.phenotype_details: 35-year-old male with recurrent ischemic strokes mainly in the pons (first pontine infarct with dysarthria ~2 years before presentation, age ~33), dysarthria, dysphagia, right hemiplegia, multifocal lacunes in pons/subcortical/periventricular WM, leukoencephalopathy, multifocal microbleeds in pons, thalamus and basal ganglia; mild cognitive impairment (MoCA 21, MMSE 25) with executive dysfunction; diagnosed as PADMAL. Renal, cardiac ultrasound and retinal vasculature normal. Carrier mother asymptomatic, no cerebrovascular history (declined MRI).
evidence_quotes: Whole exome sequencing was performed using Illumina HiSeq platform and a heterozygous missense mutation in exon 40 of COL4A1 (chr13:110826321, c.3431C>G, p. Thr1144Arg) was found.
The heterozygous mutation c.3431C>G in the exon 40 of COL4A1 was identified in the patient’s mother (Figure 2).
Although the patient’s mother carried this variant, she had no history of cerebrovascular disease, and she declined further MRI scans of the brain.

Brain MRI showed acute cerebral infarcts in the pons and left corona radiata, multiple lacunae in the pons, subcortical white matter (WM) and periventricular WM, multifocal microbleeds in the pons, bilateral thalamus and basal ganglia, and leukoencephalopathy (Figure 1).

Conservation analysis showed that the amino acids at this site were highly conserved across species, suggesting the mutation p. Thr1144Arg may be potentially pathogenic (details can be found in Supplementary material).
variants.notes: Title says 'de novo mutation' but body clearly states the variant was inherited from the asymptomatic mother (father wild type); coded as inherited. Non-glycine missense (Thr) in triple-helical region. In silico predictions conflicting (REVEL 0.237, ClinPred 0.1412, SIFT benign, PolyPhen-2 damaging); authors note ClinVar interpretation is uncertain or benign. Transcript not stated; genomic position chr13:110826321 given (build not stated). 'Other' system reflects mild cognitive impairment.

extraction.extraction_notes: Single case report. Title's 'de novo' conflicts with the body text, which reports maternal inheritance confirmed by Sanger sequencing. Supplementary file only contains a conservation figure caption.

GWAS of retinal vasculometry traits in 52,798 European-ancestry UK Biobank participants (plus 933 South Asian and 1,288 African ancestry participants; EPIC-Norfolk replication). The only COL4A1/COL4A2 variants are common association SNPs. These are rs35131825 (COL4A2, arteriolar tortuosity, p=2e-108), rs9559797 (COL4A2, meta-analysis p=6.76e-151) and an eQTL SNP at chr13:111054111 affecting COL4A1/COL4A2 expression in fibroblasts. None is reported in specific affected individuals as a candidate disease cause, so no variant records were created. The Discussion mentions a previously reported COL4A1 missense mutation causing familial retinal arteriolar tortuosity (Zenteno et al. 2014). That mention is cited only, and this paper reports no new individuals for it. Supplementary tables were filtered (e.g., Table C kept 4 of 121 rows).

variants.phenotype_details: Female; ventriculomegaly detected at 27 weeks gestation; prenatal MRI at 30+3 weeks showed grade III intraventricular hemorrhage; postnatal MRI: severe ventriculomegaly/progressive hydrocephalus (VP shunt at 4 months), multiple hemosiderin deposits in cerebral and cerebellar hemispheres, polymicrogyria (left ventral sylvian, frontal-parietal), partial thalamic fusion, corpus callosum atrophy, septum pellucidum fenestration; bilateral optic nerve hypoplasia/thinning of optic nerve and chiasma (optic atrophy) with visual impairment; drug-resistant focal motor epilepsy from 2.5 months; severe developmental delay, hypotonia. No retinal arterial tortuosity; no gross hematuria (microscopic not tested); echocardiography normal apart from small foramen ovale.
evidence_quotes: We detected a novel, previously unreported heterozygous de novo variant NM_001845.5:c.4688_4711del NP_001836.2:p.(Gln1563_Cys1570del); its presence was confirmed by Sanger sequencing, and segregation analysis (also by Sanger sequencing) showed the variant was absent in either parent.

The finding was confirmed by prenatal MRI at 30 + 3 weeks of gestation (shown in Figure 1A–C) that showed grade III intraventricular hemorrhage (enlargement of lateral ventricles, resulting from subependymal hemorrhage into germinal matrix and choroid plexus bleeding); no other major anomalies were detected.
At the age of 2.5 months, the patient manifested epileptic seizures that remain difficult to control.

Postnatal MRI showed partial thalamic fusion and polymicrogyria, in addition to severe enlargement of lateral ventricles, multiple deposits of hemosiderin in cerebral and cerebellar hemispheres, and thin optic nerve and chiasma.
variants.notes: Single case report; n_tested=1 (single patient tested by WES-based virtual panel of 366 MCD genes). Optic nerve hypoplasia/atrophy placed under 'other' rather than ocular because it is not among the listed ocular features (no cataract, ASD, retinal tortuosity). Paternal grandmother had intracerebral hemorrhage but was not tested; variant is de novo. Authors also call it 'probably pathogenic' in discussion.

extraction.extraction_notes: Single-patient case report with one de novo COL4A1 in-frame deletion in the NC1 domain; parental testing by Sanger confirmed absence in both parents. No functional work performed.

Systematic review and meta-analysis of GWAS for coronary heart disease. The only COL4A1/COL4A2 variants mentioned are the common intronic association SNPs rs11617955 (COL4A1, OR 1.04) and rs11838776 (COL4A2, OR 1.03, 95% CI 1.02-1.04). Both are reported only as pooled effect sizes across cohorts, not in specific individuals, so no variant records were created. The passing mention of patients with COL4A1 mutations having unstable plaques is cited from prior literature and adds no new individuals.

variants.phenotype_details: Patient 1, girl aged 1 y 7 mo: motor development delay, delayed speech and language development, intellectual disability (DQ 38, MI 42); short stature, low weight and head circumference (all -3 SD); fetal lateral ventriculomegaly; history of asphyxia neonatorum and hyperspasmia the day after birth; MRI/CT/X-ray reportedly 'implicated tuberous sclerosis'. Co-occurs with COL4A1 c.2797G>A (p.G933S) in the same patient.
evidence_quotes: A compound heterozygous variant c.2786T>A, p.V929D, and c.2797G>A, p.G933S in COL4A1 was detected in patient 1.
Both variants were de novo, as confirmed by Sanger sequencing (Figure 1A), and absent in the gnomAD and 1000 Genomes Project databases.

According to the ACMG/AMP guidelines, the variant c.2786T>A would be classified as likely pathogenic based on the criteria of PS2 and PM2, while the variant c.2797G>A could be classified as likely pathogenic according to the criteria of PS2, PM2, and PP3.
According to the fetal period examination, “lateral ventriculomegaly” was indicated.
variants.notes: Non-glycine missense in the triple-helical domain. Same patient also carries c.2797G>A (p.G933S); authors call it 'compound heterozygous' although both are de novo, and phase was not determined. Parents tested by trio WES and Sanger; parentage confirmation not described. No cerebrovascular or small-vessel imaging findings reported; the imaging was described as suggesting tuberous sclerosis, so the phenotype attribution to COL4A1 is uncertain. Only in silico predictions, no functional work.

variants.phenotype_details: Patient 1, girl aged 1 y 7 mo: motor development delay, delayed speech and language development, intellectual disability (DQ 38, MI 42); short stature, low weight and head circumference (all -3 SD); fetal lateral ventriculomegaly; history of asphyxia neonatorum and hyperspasmia; MRI/CT/X-ray reportedly 'implicated tuberous sclerosis'. Co-occurs with COL4A1 c.2786T>A (p.V929D).
evidence_quotes: A compound heterozygous variant c.2786T>A, p.V929D, and c.2797G>A, p.G933S in COL4A1 was detected in patient 1.
Both variants were de novo, as confirmed by Sanger sequencing (Figure 1A), and absent in the gnomAD and 1000 Genomes Project databases.

The c.2797G>A mutation results in the protein variant G933S, and the mutation of G in the repeat sequence Gly‐Xaa‐Yaa may affect the triple helix structure, which impairs the stability of the basement membrane structure and causes the disease.
variants.notes: Glycine substitution in Gly-Xaa-Yaa repeat. Same patient carries c.2786T>A (p.V929D); phase not determined despite 'compound heterozygous' wording. Parentage confirmation not described. No cerebrovascular/small-vessel imaging findings reported; imaging described as suggesting tuberous sclerosis.

extraction.extraction_notes: Trio-WES study of 4 unrelated ID patients; only patient 1 carries COL4A1 variants (two de novo missense variants in the same individual). TBR1, CHD7 and TUBA1A variants in patients 2-4 were not extracted. Figure 1 transcription partly illegible but consistent with author text. No functional experiments performed (authors state this as a limitation).

variants.phenotype_details: 2-day-old neonate presenting with seizures, multiple intracranial hemorrhages, and bilateral congenital cataracts.
evidence_quotes: A 2-day-old neonate presented with seizures, multiple intracranial hemorrhages, and bilateral congenital cataracts.
Targeted next-generation sequencing of the collagen type IV alpha 1 chain (COL4A1) gene revealed a heterozygous de novo missense variant (NM_001845.6:c.2291G>A/p.Gly764Asp).
This missense variant adds to the compendium of COL4A1 variants and is associated with a COL4A1-related disorder.
variants.notes: Called de novo in the abstract, but parental testing is not described in the provided text, so it is counted as de novo assumed. Seizures are listed under 'other'. n_tested is set to 1 because this is a single case report.

extraction.extraction_notes: The input is labeled full text, but the body contains only data-availability and competing-interest sections. The actual Data Report content, including the methods, parental testing and clinical details, was not provided, so the extraction rests on the title and abstract. The variant data are hosted at the HGV Database (10.6084/m9.figshare.hgv.3202), which was not provided.

This is a GWAS of CT-measured abdominal adiposity traits in 1,937 Korean men (discovery) and 480 men (replication). Its only COL4A1/COL4A2 variants are common association SNPs: intronic rs4773144 at COL4A1-COL4A2, associated with VAT-adj-BMI (discovery p = 9.25e-6; not replicated, p = 0.6946). The supplementary GWAS tables list further sub-threshold SNPs, including rs9521687 (COL4A1), rs400532 (COL4A2) and rs4773144 (VSR). No variants are reported in specific affected individuals as a candidate cause of disease, so no variant records were created. Table 3 misspells the locus as 'COL4A7-COL4A2'. The supplementary tables were filtered (e.g., kept 4 of 233 rows).

variants.phenotype_details: Male, age of onset 51; periventricular and deep WMH Fazekas grade 3, lacunes present, no cerebral microbleeds; recurrent ischemic stroke (cerebral infarction); severe cognitive dysfunction (MMSE 14, MoCA 7); hypertension; severe family history of stroke. Patient also carried a NOTCH3 variant considered pathogenic.
variants.reported_classification: ACMG: US (uncertain significance); described in text as pathogenic by in silico prediction
evidence_quotes: Finally, we identified a rare heterozygous variant that has never been reported, which was carried by one patient.
This patient exhibited severe cognitive dysfunction, hypertension, recurrent ischemic stroke, and a severe family history of stroke.
One patient carried c.3091C>T (NOTCH3) and c.1937G>C (COL4A1).
We enrolled 182 unrelated patients with CSVD who were admitted to the Department of Neurology, First Affiliated Hospital of Zhengzhou University, from March 2017 to July 2018.
variants.notes: No transcript stated. Co-occurring NOTCH3 variant confounds attribution: the text says the co-carried NOTCH3 variant is c.3091C>T, but Table 2 lists the COL4A1 variant under patient 1 with NOTCH3 c.1261C>T; the clinical data used here are from Table 2 patient 1. Supplementary ACMG table gives the protein change as p.Gly421Ala, conflicting with p.Gly646Ala in main Table 1 and Supplementary Figure 1 (p.G646A). The variant has an rsID (rs532972509) and is present in gnomAD (0.0004), despite being described as novel. Absent in 300 controls. Parental testing was not performed; family history of stroke reported but no family segregation was studied.

extraction.extraction_notes: Targeted sequencing of 7 CSVD genes in 182 sporadic Chinese Han CSVD patients with Fazekas 2-3 WMH. Only one COL4A1 variant was reported, and no COL4A2 variants were reported. NOTCH3 and HTRA1 variants were not extracted because they are outside scope. The text and Table 2 are inconsistent about which NOTCH3 variant co-occurs with the COL4A1 variant, and the protein numbering differs between main Table 1 and the supplementary table.

variants.phenotype_details: Male patient 1000; intracerebral hemorrhage at age 32; later MRI showed confluent white matter lesions, multiple lacunar infarcts and microbleeds; at age 47 cognitive impairment (VCI), gait disturbance and mild depression; no vascular risk factors, no migraine, no hypertension. Positive family history: uncle with cerebral hemorrhage at age 28 (not genotyped).
evidence_quotes: Sanger sequencing of the miR‐29 binding site in the 3′UTR of COL4A1 in 73 VCI patients revealed a novel heterozygous variant c.*36T>A in a patient not included in the WES analysis (Table 1 and Figure S2).
He had intracerebral hemorrhage at 32 years old, and an MRI performed later in life showed confluent white matter lesions, multiple lacunar infarcts, and microbleeds (Table 2).
At the age of 47, cognitive impairment, gait disturbance, and mild depression were observed.

1000 | COL4A1 | c.*36T>A | Het | M | 32 | VCI, gait disturbance, mild depression | Yes | Uncle (cerebral hemorrhage at age 28) | No | No | | ICH at age 32, multiple lacunar infarcts and microbleeds in brain MRI
Furthermore, we were not able to analyze the segregation of the detected variants or CNVs, because samples from family members of the patients were not available.
variants.notes: Variant located in the miR-29 binding site of the COL4A1 3'UTR; found by Sanger screening of 73 Finnish VCI patients (NOTCH3-negative). Segregation not analysed; uncle with cerebral hemorrhage not tested. The paper states 'All variants were classified as being of unknown significance based on ACMG guidelines' in the WES context; Table 1 includes this variant but it is unclear whether that classification explicitly applies to the COL4A1 3'UTR variant, so classification left blank. n_families set to 0 because carrier was found by screening and no family was studied.

extraction.extraction_notes: Only one COL4A1/COL4A2 variant reported (COL4A1 c.*36T>A, 3'UTR, patient 1000). All other variants in the paper are in other genes (HTRA1, TREX1, COLGALT1, PRNP, MTHFR, etc.) and were not extracted. Figure S2 (Sanger chromatogram) referenced but not provided. Denominator: 73 VCI patients screened for the COL4A1 miR-29 binding site out of 326 NOTCH3-negative referrals.

Genetic correlation / cross-trait GWAS analysis using summary statistics (migraine, stroke subtypes, cervical artery dissection). The only COL4A1-related variants are association SNPs (rs650724 as the top joint migraine-all stroke SNV at the COL4A1 locus; rs9521634 and rs2000660 mentioned as index/top SNVs). No specific COL4A1/COL4A2 variants are reported in specific affected individuals, so no records were created.

Case-control association study (232 unstable angina patients, 144 controls) genotyping common polymorphisms by TaqMan. The only COL4A2 variant is the intronic association SNP rs4773144, reported as genotype/allele frequencies with odds ratios and p-values (no significant association with unstable angina). No COL4A1/COL4A2 variants are reported in specific individuals as a candidate cause of disease, so no variant records were created per the exclusion rule for association SNPs.

Case-control association study: 1192 AD patients and 2412 controls (n=3604) screened with an 8-gene targeted panel that included COL4A1. The only COL4A1 variants reported are association variants given with MAF, OR, beta or p-values. Common synonymous variants: rs874203, rs874204, rs16975492, rs1373744. Rare variants: rs747972545 (c.*7C>T, 3'UTR) and rs201481886 (intronic). Variants from the AAO association study: rs9588116, rs645114, rs9521650. No variant is reported in specific individuals as a candidate cause of disease, and per-individual carrier counts are not given for COL4A1. These are association-study variants, so no VariantEvidence records were created. No COL4A2 data. Figure 1 is an LD plot of the common COL4A1 SNPs only.

variants.phenotype_details: Index case (III10, female): chronic lacunar infarcts in the pons, left thalamus and right centrum semiovale found at age 38. She then had recurrent acute lacunar infarcts in the pons and subcortical white matter (2015, 2016, 2019) and subcortical microhemorrhages on SWI at age 43. Skin biopsy EM showed a thickened, stratified vascular basement membrane, endothelial proliferation and luminal stenosis. Brother (III9, carrier): ischemic stroke at age 39, with an acute infarct in the left corona radiata, chronic pontine and subcortical infarcts, and 5 recurrent strokes. Cousin (III8, carrier): microbleeds/hemorrhage reported. In the pedigree, 12 of 18 individuals had clinical and CT/MRI evidence of PADMAL; onset age was 38-52.
evidence_quotes: A novel c.*34G > T variant was detected in the 3′ untranslated region of COL4A1 gene (chr13-110,802,676) by whole-exome sequencing in the index case (III10 in Figs. 4 and 5).
The same variant was also found in index case’s brother and a cousin. The index case’s father (II5) did not carry this mutation (Figs. 4 and 6).
Three additional family members had gene testing and 2 of them were found to have the same heterozygous mutation.
The patient had multiple lacunar infarcts and subcortical microhemorrhage at age 43.
Microbleeds or hemorrhagic stroke were reported in a few patients with PADMAL [, ]. They were observed in two subjects (III8 and III10) in our PADMAL pedigree.
variants.notes: The variant is familial: the brother and a cousin are carriers. The father tested negative and the mother's carrier status was not reported, so the parental origin is not stated and inheritance was set to unknown rather than inherited. No transcript was given; only the genomic position chr13-110,802,676 is stated. Segregation: 12 of 18 pedigree members had clinical/MRI PADMAL, but only 4 individuals were genotyped (3 carriers, 1 non-carrier). n_tested = 4 genotyped family members.

extraction.extraction_notes: This is a single-family case report. The other COL4A1 3'UTR variants (c.*31G>T, c.*32G>T, c.*32G>A, c.*33T>A, c.*35C>A) are cited from prior reports only and no records were created for them. The paper is internally inconsistent about the original PADMAL variants: the introduction lists c.*32G>T twice, while the discussion gives c.*31G>T.

Functional/translational study of Col4a1/a2 hemizygous knockout mice in an elastase-induced AAA model, with human artery proteomics, immunohistochemistry and plasma COL4A1 fragment biomarkers (VIVA trial, 476 AAA cases, 200 controls). No COL4A1/COL4A2 variants are reported in specific individuals. The only human genetic data are an association analysis of 1667 SNPs in the COL4A1/A2 locus in AAA GWAS meta-analysis data (4972 cases, 99,858 controls). The lead SNP, rs7320498 in COL4A2 intron 4, gave p = 6.5e-5 and OR 0.887. This is a common-polymorphism association result and is excluded per instructions. The PubTator 'p.A2K' variant hint is a text-mining artifact from 'COL4A1/A2 in AAA'.

Case-control association study of two common polymorphisms (COL4A1 rs1961495 and COL4A2 rs9521733) in 176 Turkish children with cerebral palsy and 178 matched controls. The results are reported only as genotype and allele frequencies with p-values. No specific variants are linked to specific affected individuals as a candidate cause, so no variant records were created under the association-SNP exclusion rule. The methods section also writes rs196149, which appears to be a typo for rs1961495. There are internal inconsistencies in the paper: the methods text says 276 patients were enrolled while the abstract and tables say 176; the COL4A1 TT genotype count is 11 but is given as 0.6%. The COL4A2 TT genotype and T allele were reported as associated with growth retardation within the CP group (p=0.03 for genotype, p=0.01 for allele).

variants.phenotype_details: Mother (77 y): migraine with aura at younger age, hypertension, mild polyneuropathy; MRI showed WML of a microangiopathic type. Older sister (58 y): migraine with aura earlier in life, hypertension since about age 30, obstructive sleep apnea; MRI showed confluent WMLs in frontal and parietal regions and to a lesser extent posterior temporal, periventricular, pontine and deep cerebellar white matter, sparing U-fibers, with T2-hyperintense foci in basal ganglia and capsula externa; no infarcts or larger hemorrhages; microbleeds not assessable.
evidence_quotes: Analysis of the WGS data for COL4A1, COL4A2, and HTRA1 mutations revealed that the mother and older sister were heterozygous for a novel COL4A1 missense mutation (c.4795 G>A; p.(Ala1599Thr)) (figure 1 and table e-1, links.lww.com/NXG/A415, in the online-only data supplement), whereas the index patient did not carry this mutation.
MRI of the brain showed some WML, but of a microangiopathic type, which was distinct from WML seen in the index patient and the younger sister (figure e-2, links.lww.com/NXG/A415).
She had migraine with aura earlier in life and hypertension since about age 30 years and obstructive sleep apnea syndrome.
Three individuals in the family were analyzed.
COL4A1 mutations have been shown to cause SVD,, and the microangiopathic changes observed in the mother and older sister are consistent with those observed in patients with COL4A1 mutations.
variants.notes: One family; the two carriers are mother and older sister of the NOTCH3 index patient (who does not carry the COL4A1 variant). Counted as one proband/family. The older sister presumably inherited it from the carrier mother, but the mother's own inheritance is unknown, so recorded as inh_unknown. Only 3 family members underwent WGS; other siblings (e.g., brother and another sister with WML/hypertension) were not reported as tested for COL4A1. Transcript not stated. Pathogenicity based only on in silico predictions (data not shown).

extraction.extraction_notes: Paper focuses on a NOTCH3 A1604T variant (not extracted). COL4A1 variant identified by WGS in 3 family members; supplementary table e-1 with family clinical summary was referenced but not provided. No functional work on the COL4A1 variant.

This paper reports a COL4A5 missense variant (c.1844G>C, NM_000495) in a Chinese family with X-linked Alport syndrome. PubTator mapped it to COL4A1 (gene ID 1282), but that mapping is wrong: the variant is in COL4A5. The paper reports no COL4A1 or COL4A2 variants in any individual. COL4A1 appears only as a measured readout: its mRNA and protein expression in transfected podocytes showed no significant change. The supplementary files are administrative (conflict-of-interest forms, data sharing statement, peer review file, MDAR checklist) and contain no variant data.

variants.phenotype_details: Three-generation family. Proband IV-6: in utero ventricular asymmetry, right frontoparietal porencephalic cavity, left hemiparesis evident at ~10 months, language delay, hypermetropia 8.5 D. IV-3: ventriculomegaly in utero, left hemisphere porencephalic cyst, right hemiparesis at ~1 year, seizures, language delay and learning difficulties, hypermetropia 15 D. IV-5: porencephalic cyst of the right lateral ventricle, microcephaly, language delay, intellectual disability (IQ 62), hypermetropia 10 D. Father III-3: severe hypermetropia (7 D), bilateral cataracts, leukoencephalopathy with small asymptomatic white matter lesions. Renal function, CK, urinary sediment, renal ultrasound and cardiac evaluation were normal; no cramps or Raynaud phenomenon.
evidence_quotes: The heterozygous variant c.2228G>T [NM_001845.4(COL4A1):c.2228G>T (p.Gly743Val)] was identified in exon 30 of the COL4A1 gene.
The variant was found in IV-3 and IV-5 and not in asymptomatic relatives (III-4, IV-1, IV-4).
Molecular analysis in the father disclosed a heterozygous variant c.2228G>T (p.Gly743Val) in exon 30 of the COL4A1 gene that segregated with the phenotype.

IV-3 had a left hemisphere porencephalic cyst and the lack of evidence of a left corticospinal tract on tractography (Figures 3E,F), IV-5 had a porencephalic cyst on the right lateral ventricle (Figure 3C), and III-3 had leukoencephalopathy (Figure 3D).
Probands' father had severe hypermetropia and bilateral cataracts.
variants.notes: The proband IV-6 inherited the variant from the carrier father III-3; the father's carrier status is stated in the Introduction. There are 4 carriers: IV-6, IV-3, IV-5 and III-3. The variant was absent in the tested asymptomatic relatives III-4, IV-1 and IV-4. n_tested=1 because COL4A1/COL4A2 panel screening was done in the proband only, followed by targeted family testing. The figure transcription labels the variant p.Gly741Val; the author text consistently says p.Gly743Val, so the author text is used. Hypermetropia is recorded under ocular. Seizures, microcephaly and intellectual disability are recorded under other.

extraction.extraction_notes: Single-family case report. The pedigree (Figure 1) was not transcribed, so the full set of carriers and non-carriers beyond those named in the text cannot be verified. The Figure 2 transcription gives p.Gly741Val, which conflicts with the author text (p.Gly743Val, c.2228G>T); the author text is used. The variant was previously listed in ClinVar (GeneDx SCV000531635.4; Undiagnosed Diseases Network SCV000926981.1), but no prior published phenotype or family is described, so it is not marked as a prior report.

Candidate-gene case-control association study (48 POP cases, 48 controls, Chinese women) of common SNPs in six collagen genes. The COL4A2 variants (rs445348, rs76425569, rs388222, rs2281968, rs74941798) are common polymorphisms (MAF >5%) and are reported only with allele frequencies, odds ratios and p-values. They are not reported as causal variants in specific individuals, so no variant records were created per the association-SNP exclusion rule. No COL4A1 variants were reported. Full SNP list (110 SNPs) is referred to in SDC, which was not provided.

variants.phenotype_details: Homozygous in 2 affected brothers of first-cousin parents. Case 1 (16 y): hemiparesis noticed at 18 months, partial epilepsy from age 1 year, bilateral cataract noticed at 6 months, glaucoma, megalocornea, trabeculodysgenesis, hypoplastic optic discs, retinal venous tortuosity, marfanoid appearance; MRI diffuse periventricular leukoencephalopathy with left ventricular enlargement, small porencephalic cysts, thin corpus callosum. Case 2 (10 y): left hemiparesis noticed at 16 months, preliminary glaucoma findings, MRI diffuse PVL with right mild ventricular enlargement. Normal intellect in both. Heterozygous carriers (both parents, 5 siblings) clinically unaffected with normal MRI, fundus, renal, cardiac and CK evaluations.
variants.reported_classification: predicted to be pathogenic by MutationTaster, PolyPhen2, and Sorting Intolerant From Tolerant
evidence_quotes: WES of the 2 affected brothers and their parents identified a novel homozygous missense variant (NM_001845.5:c.3832G>A; NP_001836.3:p.Gly1278Ser) in exon 43 of COL4A1 (chr13:110169673, GRCh38.p12).
Both affected siblings were homozygous, while both parents were heterozygous for the variant (figure 2).
Both parents and 5 of the siblings (3 boys and 2 girls) were heterozygous for the variant. They did not show any clinical or laboratory signs of small vessel disease.

Brain MRI of patient 1 showed diffuse periventricular leukoencephalopathy (PVL) with left ventricular enlargement, small porencephalic cysts, and thinning of the body part of the corpus callosum (figure 1, C and E).
At age 6 months, bilateral cataract was noticed. He was operated for cataract and glaucoma, and prophylactic glaucoma treatment was started.
variants.notes: Biallelic (homozygous) variant with autosomal recessive inheritance; heterozygous carriers unaffected. The c. notation is inconsistent: abstract says c.3832G>T, Methods/Results/Figure 2 say c.3832G>A; hgvs_c taken from the body text. Proband counted as one family (2 affected homozygous brothers). Total carriers = 2 homozygotes + 2 heterozygous parents + 5 heterozygous siblings. Cohort was 200 consanguineous Turkish families; number of individuals sequenced not stated, so n_tested set to 0.

extraction.extraction_notes: Single consanguineous Turkish family identified within a WES study of 200 consanguineous families; individual-level denominator not given. Variant notation discrepancy (G>T in abstract vs G>A in body). No functional studies performed; only in silico predictions and sequence alignment.

GWAS meta-analysis of quantitative retinal vascular traits (GoDARTS N=1736, ORCADES N=1358; replication LBC1936, Croatia-Korcula, Croatia-Split, Ntotal=1413). The only COL4A2 variants are common association SNPs (rs56399312, rs9515212, rs7991229 and others in Supplementary Table II; previously reported CAD SNPs rs4773144, rs11617955, rs9515203) reported with effect sizes and p-values for retinal arteriolar tortuosity. No rare COL4A1/COL4A2 variants are reported in specific affected individuals, so no variant records were created per the exclusion rule for association polymorphisms. Supplementary PDF rows were filtered (kept subsets), but the content is GWAS statistics only.

This is a genome-wide association meta-analysis (72,147 stroke cases and 823,869 controls from UK Biobank and MEGASTROKE). The only COL4A1 variant is rs9521634, a common intronic (intron 28) polymorphism reported with a risk allele frequency of 36%, OR 1.04 and p = 3.8E-8 for any stroke, with its strongest association in small vessel stroke (OR 1.06). It is an association SNP, not a candidate causal variant in specific affected individuals, so no variant record was created. COL4A2 is mentioned only in reference to common variants from prior studies. The figure transcriptions contain only rsIDs and no additional COL4A1/COL4A2 data.

variants.phenotype_details: Fetus with schizencephaly detected prenatally by fetal ultrasonography and fetal MRI; the authors suggest the onset of damage occurred mid-pregnancy.
evidence_quotes: Here, we report a patient with schizencephaly, detected by fetal ultrasonography and fetal magnetic resonance imaging, with a de novo novel mutation in COL4A1 (c.2645_2646delinsAA, p.Gly882Glu).
Our results suggest that the onset of damage that potentially results in schizencephaly occurs mid-pregnancy.
variants.notes: Dinucleotide delins producing a glycine substitution (Gly882Glu), classified as missense_glycine. Called de novo in the abstract, but no parental testing is described in the available text, so it is counted as assumed de novo. No transcript is stated.

extraction.extraction_notes: The input is labelled full text, but the body contains only database, publisher and contact boilerplate. Effectively only the title and abstract were available, so input_was_abstract_only is set to true. Details of parental testing, the transcript, other phenotypes and the pregnancy outcome were not available.

The only COL4A1/COL4A2 variant studied is the common intronic GWAS SNP rs4773144 in COL4A2 intron 3, plus the LD proxies rs4773143, rs7986871 and rs3809346. The paper analyses it by genotype groups for expression, ChIP allelic imbalance, luciferase and EMSA activity, apoptosis and plaque histology. It also tests association with myocardial infarction in 655 Chinese CHD patients drawn from 1125 angiography patients (G/G OR 2.01). This is an association and functional study of a common polymorphism, not rare variants in specific affected individuals, so no variant records were created, per the rules. The passing mention of a COL4A2 frameshift mutation refers to prior literature and adds no new individuals.

variants.phenotype_details: Autosomal dominant microscopic haematuria (17/20 carriers), proteinuria (7), kidney cysts (11; detectable by ultrasound from age 40), renal impairment (eGFR 31-90 in 14, <30 in 4, ESRD in 3 at ages 63-70); creatinine rising after age 40; hypertension from 35 years in some. Kidney biopsy at 47 years showed thin glomerular basement membranes and lamellation of tubular basement membranes. No muscle cramps or cerebral aneurysms; creatine kinase normal; brain MRI and retinal photography in four affected members showed no cerebral or ocular angiopathy. Tubular proteinuria (elevated RBP or NAG ratios) in some carriers.
variants.reported_classification: novel frameshift mutation; considered responsible for the familial renal disease
evidence_quotes: We identified a novel frameshift mutation, c.4611_4612insG:p.T1537fs, in exon 49 of COL4A1.
We confirmed its presence in 20 family members, 17 with confirmed haematuria, 5 of whom also had stage 4 or 5 chronic kidney disease.

Eleven family members exhibited kidney cysts (55% of those with the mutation), but muscle cramps or cerebral aneurysms were not observed and serum creatine kinase was normal in all individuals tested.

The COL4A1 mutation was confirmed by Sanger sequencing (Figure 1D), and screening across all available samples revealed its presence in all affected individuals participating in the linkage study and in a further eight relatives, seven of whom had one or more of haematuria, cysts or evidence of reduced renal function (eGFR <90 mL/min).
Total family members | 20 | 8
variants.notes: Single Turkish Cypriot kindred with autosomal dominant segregation (LOD 3). Proband's specific parental genotype not explicitly stated; classified as inherited based on multigenerational segregation in the family. Transcript written as 'NM_00185' (likely a typo for NM_001845). n_tested = 28 family members genotyped (20 carriers + 8 non-carriers per Table 1); additionally absent in 63 healthy Turkish Cypriot controls. Only structural modelling (Jmol) of predicted truncation, no wet-lab functional work.

extraction.extraction_notes: Single-family study. Supplementary Video S1 referenced but not provided. Pedigree (Figure 1A) details not transcribed. Whole exome data from four other families with dominant haematuria found no additional COL4A1 variants.

Genome-wide association meta-analysis of white matter hyperintensity volume in 3,670 ischemic stroke patients. The only COL4A2 variant is the common intronic SNP rs9515201, reported as a genome-wide association (meta-analysis p = 6.9 × 10−9). This is an association SNP, not a variant found in specific affected individuals, so no variant records were created. Patients with suspected monogenic causes of stroke were excluded. The supplementary PDF was truncated (1 of 5 sheets not included); that material appears to be cohort descriptions and power calculations, not variant-level data.

This is a MetaboChip association study of prostate volume in 876 biopsy-negative men and 442 men with low-grade prostate cancer from the Nashville Men's Health Study. Its only COL4A1/COL4A2 variant is rs9583484, an intronic COL4A2 SNP (MAF 0.17). That SNP was nominally associated with log prostate volume (meta-analysis beta -0.11, p=1.01x10-5) and did not reach the multiple-testing threshold. This is a common polymorphism association result, not a variant found in specific affected individuals, so no variant records were created.

variants.phenotype_details: 50-year-old female with congenital cataracts, glaucoma, cerebral palsy, and acquired neurogenic bladder. After mild head trauma: confusion, right-sided weakness, multiple diffusion-positive infarcts, contrast-enhancing periventricular white matter, confluent periventricular white matter disease, scattered punctate/deep microhemorrhages, and later new intraventricular hemorrhage. Elevated CSF protein.
variants.reported_classification: previously unreported pathogenic missense substitution; heterozygous putatively pathogenic mutation
evidence_quotes: COL4A1 sequencing was performed, revealing a missense substitution (c.2969G>T; p.Gly990Val; NM_001845) within the triple helical G-X-Y domain, located within the splice acceptor site of exon 36.
A 50-year-old female with a history of congenital cataracts, glaucoma, cerebral palsy, and acquired neurogenic bladder suffered a mild head trauma after a fall from standing height.
Genetic testing was declined by her asymptomatic parents, asymptomatic son, and her sister with MS.
Whether this COL4A1 mutation occurred de novo or is present in asymptomatic family members or her sister with the previous diagnosis of progressive MS remains uncertain.

A repeat brain MRI 5 days later showed an interval increase in the multifocal and periventricular hemorrhagic foci with new intraventricular hemorrhage without any change in white matter hyperintensities (fig. 3).
variants.notes: The authors suggest the variant may be de novo, but parents declined testing and the discussion says de novo status remains uncertain, so it is recorded as inheritance unknown. Splice prediction (Human Splice Finder) suggests exon 36 skipping, with in silico predictions only and no functional assay. The sister with progressive MS was not tested. 'Other' covers cerebral palsy and neurogenic bladder.

extraction.extraction_notes: Single case report. One proband was tested, so n_tested is set to 1. No relatives were genotyped.

Case-control association study (471 CAD patients, 624 controls; 1095 Uygur individuals) genotyping two common COL4A1 tag SNPs (rs605143 and rs565470, MAF >= 0.05) by PCR-RFLP and reporting genotype/allele frequencies, odds ratios and p-values for association with coronary artery disease. These are association polymorphisms, not candidate causal variants in specific individuals, so no variant records were created. rs3742207 (Gln1334His) is mentioned only as prior literature.

The authors sequenced COL4A1 and COL4A2 in 48 individuals from 15 Ecuadorian keratoconus families (23 members of family KTCN-014 plus 25 affected members of other families) and 64 controls. Table 2 lists the identified variants as counts and percentages of carriers by group. Almost all have dbSNP IDs. The missense variants are COL4A1 Val7Leu, Thr555Pro and Gln1334His, and COL4A2 Val192Phe, Arg517Lys, Gly683Ala, Lys701Arg and Pro718Ser. None segregated with disease. Gln1334His (rs3742207) was tested for association with Fisher's exact test (p=0.056 within the family; p=0.17 versus controls). The authors conclude that 'Analysis of COL4A1 and COL4A2 revealed no mutations' and attribute no disease to any variant. COL4A2 Val192Phe (rs62621885) was seen in only one affected individual from the other families, but the authors call it previously reported and benign, and do not present it as causal. Because every variant is reported as a polymorphism with group frequencies or association statistics, no variant-level records were created.

variants.phenotype_details: Thoracic aortic dissection in a 47-year-old patient (age at sampling/surgery).
variants.functional_evidence: Patient iPSC-derived VSMCs showed reduced COL4A2/COL4A1 expression, increased COL1A1/COL3A1, reduced carbachol-induced contraction, increased proliferation, hyperactivated noncanonical ERK1/2 TGF-beta signalling and elevated MMP9, without isogenic correction to attribute effects to the variant.
evidence_quotes: we generated nonintegrative iPSCs from a 47‐year‐old patient with TAD (Figure 1 and Supporting Information: Figure S1).
Sanger sequencing confirmed the COL4A2 R131M (c.392 G > T) mutation in both TAD–iPSCs and the derived SMCs (Figure 4A).
Using a web‐based prediction tool, we found that the COL4A2 R131M mutation is predicted to be harmful (Figure 4B).
For example, in this study, we only included one patient sample carrying the target COL4A2 mutation.
variants.notes: Single patient with whole-exome sequencing; no parental testing or family studied. No transcript stated; p.R131M is located in the 7S domain per authors. hgvs_p expanded from the paper's p.R131M (same residue, not renumbered). Phenotype (aortic dissection) is outside standard COL4A1/2 systems, so classified as 'other'. Authors acknowledge other variants may contribute and that no isogenic control was made. n_tested set to 1 as only this patient was sequenced.

extraction.extraction_notes: iPSC disease-modelling study of one thoracic aortic dissection patient carrying a COL4A2 c.392G>T (p.R131M) variant found by WES among several candidate variants. Paper says iPSCs were generated from 'TAD patients' in places but describes only one patient. A preprint of this work was previously published; no other prior clinical report of this patient is indicated.

variants.phenotype_details: Patient 8, female, diagnosed at age 3.83 y. She had pediatric pulmonary hemorrhage (hemosiderin cells in lavage or gastric fluid), cough and wheezing. She also had fatigue, clubbing, joint hypermobility, joint swelling and skin hyperextensibility, with ground-glass opacities and cysts on chest CT. Other findings were growth retardation, a history of pneumothorax, pleural effusion, pericardial effusion and skeletal developmental abnormalities. Lung pathology showed broken elastic fibers and uneven thickening of the interstitial vessel walls. The authors labeled her subtype as vEDS.
evidence_quotes: 8 | vEDS | COL4A2 | c.4691C > A(p. S1564Y) | NA | P | 0.0000083 | LP | PM1 + PM2 + PP3 + PP4 | C-terminal structure | Affect the proper assembly and maturation of collagen fibers
Patient 8 had a history of pneumothorax, pleural effusion, pericardial effusion, and skeletal developmental abnormalities.

The c.4691 C > A (p. Ser1564Tyr) mutation affects the C-terminal structure of the collagen triple helix trimer, which is essential for the proper assembly and maturation of collagen fibrils (Additional File 2: Supplementary Fig. 3).
Patients 5 and 8 presented with growth retardation.
variants.notes: Inheritance is inferred from the 'P' in the Source column of Table 2. Other rows use M (maternal) and De novo, so 'P' is read as paternal. The father's phenotype is not described. No transcript is given. The only additional analysis is in silico structural prediction (Supplementary Fig. 3), not functional work. No cerebrovascular, small vessel, renal, ocular or muscle phenotypes were reported. 'Early kidney injury markers' were normal (N) for patient 8. n_tested of 8 reflects the eight EDS patients with pulmonary hemorrhage who were sequenced. The total number of EDS patients reviewed is not stated.

extraction.extraction_notes: This is a series of 8 pediatric EDS patients with pulmonary hemorrhage. Only one COL4A1/COL4A2 variant is reported: COL4A2 c.4691C>A in patient 8. The other variants are in COL3A1, COL1A1, COL1A2 and TNXB and were excluded. The authors hypothesize that COL4A2 is a vEDS gene, but they provide no supporting functional data.

Mouse-only functional study of the Col4a1 G1344D allele (Col4a1+/G1344D mice crossed with Tgfbr2 conditional heterozygotes). It examines glaucoma-related phenotypes: anterior segment dysgenesis, iridocorneal adhesions, elevated IOP, optic nerve head excavation and RGC/axon loss. Reducing TGFBR2 partially rescued these phenotypes, and Serpine1 (a TGFβ target) was elevated in mutant anterior segments. No human patients or human COL4A1/COL4A2 variants are reported, so there are no variant-level records. The supplementary files contain only mouse figure legends and a primer list.

Mouse functional study of the Col4a1+/G394V model (Col4a1 G394V). It reports no human patients and no COL4A1/COL4A2 variants in specific human individuals, so no variant records were created. The key finding is age-dependent loss of cerebral artery myogenic tone in 12-month-old mutant mice. This was due to reduced TRPM4 currents from PI3K-mediated PIP2 depletion and was rescued by PI3K or TGF-beta receptor inhibition. Mutant mice also showed spontaneous ICH at 12 months. The Fig. 1 transcription gives the mouse transcript NM_009931.2; it notes the mutated codon was printed as GGT in both rows, a likely figure or transcription artefact.

variants.phenotype_details: Female neonate; prenatal IUGR, microcephaly, ventricular dysmorphism and cerebellar hypoplasia on fetal ultrasound (35 wk); at 7 days MRI: porencephalic areas of hemorrhagic origin (parenchymal hemorrhages), ventriculomegaly, almost complete corpus callosum agenesis, cerebellar hemisphere and vermis hypoplasia, bilateral frontal and temporal lissencephaly; cortical/subcortical periventricular calcifications on CT at 1 month; optic nerve hypoplasia at 5 days; bilateral nuclear cataract at 6 months; left eye glaucoma after cataract surgery; fibrotic pupillary membrane; spastic tetraparesis; seizures from 6 months.
evidence_quotes: The test results were positive for the heterozygous mutation c.2716+2T>C, which affects a consensus sequence for splicing. Both mother and father were negative for mutation.

Porencephalic areas, delimited by hyperintense edges on T2-weighted images and hypointense edges on T1-weighted images, were observed in the cerebral parenchyma, and they were determined to be of hemorrhagic origin.
At 6 months of age an ophthalmological reevaluation identified a nuclear cataract (Fig. 4) that prevented evaluation of the fundus oculi.
At 5 days of age, ophthalmological examination detected marked hypoplasia of the optic nerve at the fundus oculi, while no anomalies of the anterior segment were observed (Fig. 3).
variants.notes: Transcript not stated. Abstract refers to 'COL4A gene' but body specifies COL4A1. Parentage confirmation not explicitly described, but both parents tested negative. Glaucoma developed one week after cataract surgery; authors consider it unlikely surgery-related.

extraction.extraction_notes: Single case report. The variant c.2345G>C is mentioned only in passing from prior literature (mechanism of cataract) and was not extracted.

variants.phenotype_details: A child in the male partner's family was reported as suffering from HANAC syndrome; no specific clinical features or age at onset were given. The male partner (father) was heterozygous, and no phenotype was described for him. In PGD, 12 of 15 embryos (3/3 in cycle 1, 9/12 in cycle 2) carried the variant heterozygously.
variants.reported_classification: pathogenic allele of COL4A1 gene; potential pathogenic COL4A1 allele
evidence_quotes: The family history of the couple in the present study indicated a child, from the family of the male partner, suffering from the HANAC syndrome by acquiring a pathogenic allele of COL4A1 gene (c.1537G>A; p.G513S).
As expected, DNA from the male partner indicated a heterozygous condition for the c.1537G>A mutation within COL4A1 gene.
A couple with a history of HANAC syndrome within the family of the male partner requested consultation from IVF Department of our hospital, to ensure a child-free from the genetic disorder.
Results indicated that out of 12, 9 were heterozygous while 3 were normal or wild type with regard to the COL4A1 mutation [Figure 4].
variants.notes: This is a PGD report for one family. The affected individual is a child in the male partner's family, and the exact relationship to the father is unstated. Inheritance in that child is not described. The total carrier count is left null: the father and the affected child are carriers, plus 12 embryos, but the affected child's genotyping is not explicitly described. The father's clinical status is not described; he is called a 'suspected carrier' and tested heterozygous. No transcript is given. There is no clinical detail beyond the label 'HANAC syndrome'. The variant may correspond to the previously reported HANAC variant, but no prior publication of this family is cited.

extraction.extraction_notes: The paper is an IVF/PGD technical report. It contains a single COL4A1 variant in one family, with minimal clinical phenotype data. Table 1 (embryo characteristics) is referenced, but its contents were not rendered in the provided text.

variants.phenotype_details: Isolated, non-syndromic bilateral autosomal dominant congenital nuclear cataract (disc-shaped lens opacity in pupil area) in 15 affected members of a five-generation Han Chinese family; brain MRI and renal function normal in affected members; no porencephaly, ICH, diabetes or glomerulopathy.
evidence_quotes: The large pedigree (Figure 1) of a five-generation Han family from a rural area in Jiangsu Province in China includes 15 affected and 64 unaffected individuals with typical features of congenital cataract.
All of the affected individuals carry the same COL4A1 mutation.
Brain MRIs and renal function of the affected members were normal.
This mutation was not found in unaffected family members or in 200 unrelated controls.

The entire COL4A1 gene was sequenced and a heterozygous G-to-C transition (c.2345 G > C) was identified in exon 31, leading to the replacement of a highly conserved glycine residue by alanine at position 782 (Gly782Ala) within the triple-helix domain (Figure 4C).
variants.notes: Single five-generation family; proband IV-7. Variant segregates with 15 affected members (carrier count inferred from 'All of the affected individuals carry the same COL4A1 mutation'). Inheritance classified as inherited given multigenerational autosomal dominant segregation; specific parental genotype of proband not explicitly stated. n_tested = 79 family members studied. Linkage HLOD 5.413 at 13q33.3-q33.4. Only in silico (SIFT/PolyPhen) predictions, no functional assays.

extraction.extraction_notes: Additional file 1 (SIFT/PolyPhen predictions) referred to but not provided. Transcript NM_001845 stated in background for COL4A1 gene generally.

variants.phenotype_details: Autosomal dominant familial porencephaly with reduced penetrance; proband IV:21 has a large porencephalic cyst. Unaffected carrier father (III:8) and obligate carriers without subclinical cerebrovascular disease. Renal and ocular examinations normal within the pedigree. Both patient and carrier father showed focal dermal basement membrane defects on EM.
variants.functional_evidence: Patient dermal fibroblasts showed ER retention of COL4A2/COL4A1, enlarged ER, ER stress with activation of all three UPR branches, reduced proliferation and increased apoptosis; mutant protein was degraded via the proteasome, and 4-PBA reduced intracellular COL4A2, ER stress and apoptosis, whereas the unaffected carrier father's cells largely lacked ER retention.
variants.prior_report_reason: The pedigree is described as 'adapted from Fig. 1 in' an earlier publication, indicating the family's clinical phenotype was reported previously (without the COL4A2 variant); the variant itself is reported as novel here.
evidence_quotes: While sequence analysis of patient IV:21, who has a large porencephalic cyst, excluded COL4A1 mutations, it identified a base pair change in exon 28 of COL4A2 (Fig. 1B) that is predicted to substitute a glycine residue of a Gly-X-Y repeat for aspartic acid (G702D) (Fig. 1C).

Sequence analysis of additional family members confirmed segregation of the mutation with the phenotype and that the mutation was absent in 100 unrelated ethnically matched healthy controls, providing strong evidence that COL4A2 G702D represents the causative mutation.
Analysis of dermal biopsies from a patient and his unaffected father, who also carries the mutation, revealed that both display basement membrane (BM) defects.
Renal and ocular examinations did not reveal any kidney or eye defects characteristic of COL4A1 disease within this pedigree.
A pedigree shows familial dominant porencephaly with reduced penetrance (adapted from Fig. 1 in ).
variants.notes: c. notation and transcript not given; protein numbering based on Ensembl ENSP00000353654. Number of carriers and affected individuals in the pedigree not stated in text (pedigree figure not provided). n_tested not stated (single-family candidate gene study; 100 controls screened). Inherited from unaffected carrier father (III:8).

extraction.extraction_notes: Single large family with porencephaly; one COL4A2 variant. Total carrier count and number of family members sequenced are in the pedigree figure, which was not provided. The family's clinical description was previously published (citation stripped); the variant identification is new in this paper.

Mouse-only functional study of the tendon basement membrane. It uses the ENU-induced Col4a1+/Svc mouse (G1064D substitution in the alpha1(IV) chain), which shows a discontinuous tendon basement membrane, reduced laminin and spontaneous tendon adhesions. No human patients or human COL4A1/COL4A2 variants in specific individuals are reported, so no variant records were created.

Whole-exome sequencing study of 117 suspected monogenic CSVD patients, all previously negative for pathogenic variants on a targeted panel that included COL4A1 and COL4A2 (inclusion criterion). No COL4A1 or COL4A2 variants are reported in any individual. These genes appear only as panel genes, in PanelApp gene lists (Supplementary Table 2), in the gene-prioritisation training set and in discussion text. The reported variants are in other genes (ABCC6, LAMB1, LAMC1, APP, MYH11, NOTCH1, SQSTM1 and others). Two of 11 sheets in the supplementary workbook were truncated and not provided, and several tables were filtered. Nothing in the provided text suggests these sheets contain COL4A1 or COL4A2 variants.

Systematic review and meta-analysis of sequencing studies in non-cryptogenic cerebral palsy. It reports no specific COL4A1/COL4A2 variants in specific individuals, and no new patients. Gene-level counts are aggregated from earlier publications: COL4A1 in 12 individuals and COL4A2 in 4 individuals (Supplementary Data S7). The COL4A1 count comes from Van Eyk n=2, Chopra n=1, Fehlings n=4, Santana-Almansa n=2 and Thys n=3. The COL4A2 count comes from Wang n=1 and Van Eyk n=3. These carriers belong to the source studies and should be extracted from those papers, not from this one. The authors also note possible partial cohort overlap between Chopra et al. and Almansa et al. Supplementary Table_1 and Table_6 were truncated: other sheets were not included, and only 4 of 24 rows of the recurrent-genes sheet were kept.

variants.phenotype_details: 4-year-old boy with severe hemophilia A on emicizumab with repetitive spontaneous joint bleeds; ISTH-BAT 5; negative family history. Carrier mother has no bleeding.
evidence_quotes: 4 | M | 4 | COL4A2 | VUS | NM_001846.4 | c.751A>Gp.(Asn251Asp) | - | 6.195e−7 | Repetitive spontaneous joint bleeds in the patient with severe hemophilia A while he was on emicizumab | 5 | Negative | Mother carrier: no bleedingFather normal: no bleeding
Of note, musculoskeletal bleeds were only reported in 1 patient, which involved the known hemophilia A patient.
variants.notes: BDUC cohort (n = 69). Bleeding is likely explained by hemophilia A; the variant was not linked to a COL4A2-type phenotype.

variants.phenotype_details: 2-year-old boy with cutaneous bleeding symptoms and epistaxis; ISTH-BAT 3; positive family history of bleeding, but the variant was absent in affected relatives.
evidence_quotes: 8 | M | 2 | COL4A1 | VUS | NM_001845.6 | c.244G>Ap.(Gly82Arg) | - | 0 | Cutaneous bleeding symptomsEpistaxis | 3 | Positive | Variant absent in several other family members with cutaneous bleeding symptoms. Likely benign

Additional studies, including family cosegregation analyses and further clinical investigations, were undertaken to enable potential reclassification of the VUS findings; however, this was only possible for 1 variant, which was ultimately reclassified as likely benign.
variants.notes: BDUC cohort. The variant did not segregate with bleeding in the family and was reclassified as likely benign. Parental carrier status was not specified.

variants.phenotype_details: 13-year-old boy with cutaneous bleeding symptoms (subgaleal hematoma); ISTH-BAT 3; negative family history.
evidence_quotes: 10 | M | 13 | COL4A2 | VUS | NM_001846.4 | c.4493C>Tp.(Thr1498Met) | - | 0.0000607567 | Cutaneous bleeding symptoms (subgaleal hematoma) | 3 | Negative | No further testing performed.
VUS findings were identified in 8 patients, most frequently in COL3A1, COL4A2, and COL5A1 (Table 3).

variants.phenotype_details: Term-born girl after an uncomplicated pregnancy with delayed motor development and left-sided hemiparesis. Brain MRI at 8 months showed sequelae of a hemorrhagic infarction with marked ventricular dilation. Father carries the variant without a BSVD phenotype.
