extraction.extraction_notes: Retrospective single-center cohort of 44 pediatric patients (33 COL4A1, 10 COL4A2, 1 both); 336 charts screened, 44 included (used as n_tested). Per-patient variant, phenotype and inheritance data are in eTables 2a-c, which were not provided; all variant identities come solely from a model-generated transcription of Figure 4 that was partly illegible, so all records are low confidence and phenotype_systems/inheritance could not be linked to individual variants (colour-coded onset category not read). Panel A = COL4A1 (NM_001845.6), B = COL4A2 (NM_001846.4) per author caption. Protein changes not given, so glycine status of missense variants is undetermined (typed missense_other). Text states 30 distinct COL4A1 and 9 COL4A2 variants, with 4 variants seen in 2 patients each (3 sibling sets); the transcription gives 30 COL4A1 and 8 COL4A2 variants and suggests 5 recurrent COL4A1 variants (c.1241G>A, c.2317G>A, c.2258C>A, c.3611G>C, c.2269_2276del), a discrepancy; recurrent variants recorded as 1 proband/2 carriers, may be 2 unrelated probands. Two COL4A2 patients had variants reported by an international laboratory >2 decades ago without available reports. One sibling pair with sensorineural hearing loss, hematuria, proteinuria, muscle cramps, porencephalic cyst and IVH inherited a COL4A1 VUS from their father (renal disease, muscle cramps), but the specific variant is not identifiable. Authors state none of the patients were previously described.

Retrospective Alport syndrome cohort (179 probands; WES on 168) reporting only COL4A3, COL4A4 and COL4A5 variants (Table S13). COL4A1 is mentioned only in the Discussion, in reference to HANAC syndrome featuring kidney cysts; no COL4A1 or COL4A2 variants are reported in any individual. The supplementary file was truncated (6 of 30 sheets not included), so the remainder of Table S13 was not seen. However, the Methods state that genetic diagnosis was based on COL4A3/COL4A4/COL4A5 variants only.

Retrospective cohort of 29 pediatric-onset intractable epilepsy patients treated with cannabidiol. One male patient (Table 2, patient no. 3) is listed with 'COL4A1'-related epilepsy (a genetic epileptic encephalopathy). He had baseline seizures of 150/month reduced to 9/month, a moderate CBD response at 1 year, and an elevated liver enzyme adverse event managed by valproate reduction. The paper never states the specific COL4A1 variant (no c./p. nomenclature), inheritance, classification or other phenotype details such as neuroimaging. Because no specific variant is reported, no VariantEvidence record was created. A curator may wish to note this COL4A1 patient (n_tested = 29) if the variant becomes available elsewhere.

This is a case-control association study of ANRIL, HNF1A and PAI-1 SNPs in Saudi stroke patients, with whole-exome sequencing (WES) in 10 stroke patients. Table 8 lists four COL4A2 variants: c.297G>A rs4238272, c.3804T>A rs439831, c.3807T>C rs409858 and c.4083T>C rs438758. All four are common synonymous dbSNP polymorphisms reported at 'Freq/10 samples 10, 100%', meaning every WES-sequenced patient carries them. They are reported as population-level frequencies in a cohort, not as candidate causal variants in specific affected individuals, so no variant records were created. No transcript was stated, and the c. numbering is unverified. The COL4A1 c.161C>T (p.Pro54Leu) and COL4A2 p.Glu1123Gly variants are only cited from earlier publications (Hartl et al. and others), with no new individuals in this paper. The paper gives inconsistent cohort sizes: 100 cases with 100-120 controls, and elsewhere 105 cases with 115 controls.

variants.phenotype_details: Female; microscopic hematuria and mild proteinuria found at age 39; declining kidney function at age 48 (eGFR 57), progressing to CKD stage 3b (eGFR 41) over 6 years; biopsy showed diffuse GBM thinning (<200 nm, some <100 nm), interstitial fibrosis/tubular atrophy 25-30%, global glomerulosclerosis; mildly hyperechoic kidneys with bilateral simple subcentimeter cortical cysts; new-onset unilateral left-sided sensorineural hearing loss and tinnitus. No retinal/vascular eye disease, normal brain MRI, no muscle cramps, normal neurological exam.
evidence_quotes: A comprehensive inherited kidney disease gene panel identified a heterozygous 1.9 Mb deletion in chromosome 13q33.3-q34 involving the entire COL4A1 gene and exons 1 to 45 of the COL4A2 gene (Fig. 2).
A 39-year-old female patient was found to have microscopic hematuria and mild proteinuria during a routine examination with her primary physician.

Electron microscopy revealed normocellular glomeruli, absence of electron dense deposits, and diffuse glomerular basement membrane thinning with all measurements below 200 nm and some less than 100 nm (Fig. 1b).
The patient also reported new-onset left-sided hearing loss and tinnitus; she was found to have mild to moderate unilateral sensorineural hearing loss.
Magnetic resonance imaging focusing on the left internal auditory canal was normal; the entire brain was visualized and was unremarkable.
variants.notes: Single CNV spanning entire COL4A1 and exons 1-45 of COL4A2 (also includes MYO16 and IRS2); recorded under COL4A1 because the schema allows one gene per record, but the same deletion affects COL4A2. No genomic coordinates or ISCN nomenclature given. Inheritance not tested: father had hypertension and elevated creatinine, and daughter had microscopic hematuria at age 20, but neither was genotyped. n_tested set to 1 (single case report).

extraction.extraction_notes: Case report of one patient with a contiguous 13q33.3-q34 deletion involving COL4A1 and COL4A2. The truncating COL4A1 variants in Fig. 3 (p.Tyr1625*, p.Glu1539Glyfs*8, p.Gly1210*, p.Gln856*, p.Ala847Leufs*7, p.Gly732fs, p.Gly696Alafs*106, p.Arg396*, p.Gln247*) are previously published literature variants, shown only in a figure transcription, and add no new individuals, so they were not extracted. Supplementary figures (renal ultrasound, ocular imaging) were not provided.

variants.phenotype_details: 74-year-old woman with late-onset, rapidly progressive dementia (memory, executive, instrumental decline; MMSE 22 to 15 to 3/30 over about one year) and behavioral changes (irritability, verbal aggression). MRI showed extensive confluent periventricular and deep white matter hyperintensities, including anterior temporal and orbitofrontal subcortical white matter (CADASIL-like pattern). Two left temporopolar microbleeds were thought post-traumatic. Ventricular dilatation was present. Later course included epileptic seizures. No stroke, ICH or lacunar infarcts. No ophthalmological disease, renal failure or migraine. Elevated CSF NfL.
evidence_quotes: Molecular analysis identified a heterozygous variant in the exon 16 of COL4A2 (NM_001846.4: c.940G>C; p.Gly314Arg).

According to the ACMG/AMP criteria, the p.(Gly314Arg) variant was therefore classified as likely pathogenic, although its causality in the clinical symptoms of this patient cannot be established at this point.
Brain MRI (Fig. 1) revealed widespread confluent hyperintensities on T2-Fluid Attenuated Inversion Recovery images in the periventricular and deep white matter.
We present the case of a 74-year-old Caucasian woman referred to our memory clinic due to progressive cognitive decline.
While there was no known family history of dementia or stroke, her mother experienced sudden death at 50, and her father at 67.
variants.notes: Parental testing was not possible or not reported; both parents are deceased. The authors state that causality is uncertain, so the variant may be fortuitous or a modifier. Dementia is recorded under 'other' because it was not attributed to an imaging correlate with certainty. The microbleeds were considered post-traumatic, so small_vessel reflects the white matter hyperintensities. rs757680081; gnomAD v4.1 frequency 0.001%.

variants.phenotype_details: Case 1 (5 y male): neonatal multifocal myoclonic seizures at 3 days, multiple intracerebral hemorrhages/antenatal hemorrhagic insults, encephalomalacia, Wallerian degeneration, microhemorrhages, superficial hemosiderosis, porencephalic cysts on follow-up MRI at 3 y, new acute lacunar infarct, spastic cerebral palsy, global developmental delay, ataxic gait, bilateral cataracts (IOL at age 4), PFO. Case 2 (3 y male sibling): prenatal intraventricular hemorrhage, periventricular calcifications, ventriculomegaly/posthemorrhagic hydrocephalus requiring VP shunt at 7 months, possible corpus callosum agenesis, partial septum pellucidum agenesis, pontine microhemorrhage, bilateral congenital cataracts (surgery at 6 months), macrocephaly, developmental delay, status epilepticus at 9 months and 2 years. Father (not stated to be tested) has encephalomalacia, intellectual disability, bilateral cataracts and abnormal gait.
evidence_quotes: Genetic testing confirmed a COL4A1 missense mutation (c.2707G > C, p.Gly903Arg).
Genetic testing confirmed a COL4A1 mutation, the same as his brother (Case 1) (Table 1).
The mother is healthy, while the father has a history of encephalomalacia with intellectual disability, bilateral cataracts, and abnormal gait.
Postnatal examination identified bilateral congenital cataracts, which were corrected by lens replacement surgery at 6 months.
A follow‐up brain MRI was performed at the age of 3 years and demonstrated porencephalic cyst formation secondary to old cerebrovascular insults (Figure 3).
variants.notes: Two affected brothers from one consanguineous Palestinian family counted as one proband/family. Parental testing not described; affected father is suggestive of paternal inheritance but carrier status not reported, so inheritance coded unknown. Total carriers = 2 confirmed siblings.

variants.phenotype_details: Homozygous in Case #1, a fetus (30 gestational weeks in text; 20-week-old in Table 1) terminated after prenatal imaging. Findings: intrauterine growth retardation; cortico-subcortical hemorrhagic lesions (left occipital, right frontal); periventricular leukomalacia; multiple periventricular white matter calcifications; left midbrain parenchymal loss; left-sided cerebellar hypoplasia with abnormal foliation and hemosiderin deposits consistent with prior hemorrhagic infarct; vermian and pontine hypoplasia. Heterozygous parents unaffected.
evidence_quotes: In Case #1, a homozygous COL4A2 c.535C>T, p.(Arg179Cys) (exon 8; Figure 2A) was identified, inherited from unaffected heterozygous parents.

This very rare variant (AF‐0.00001449‐gnomAD), absent in homozygous healthy individuals, affects a highly conserved residue (GERP = 5.33) and is predicted to be moderately damaging, classified as likely benign (ACMG Class‐II; BP1, BP4).
Cortico‐subcortical hemorrhagic lesions were noted in the left occipital and right frontal lobes, alongside multiple periventricular white matter calcifications.
Left‐sided cerebellar hypoplasia with abnormal foliation and hemosiderin deposits was consistent with prior hemorrhagic infarct disruption.
variants.notes: Homozygous; parents heterozygous carriers (total carriers 3 inferred from fetus + two parents). Authors classify the variant as likely benign per ACMG yet treat it as causal (hypomorphic allele). Only in silico protein stability modeling (ThermoMPNN, Rosetta, AlphaMissense 0.45) performed, no wet-lab functional work. Gestational age discrepancy (30 weeks in text vs 20-week-old in Table 1). The same variant was previously reported in trans with p.(Gly690Val) in a different patient (PMID 36603335); that individual is cited, not counted here.

variants.phenotype_details: Compound heterozygous (in trans with c.4275dup) in Case #2, a 2-year-old female born SGA at term; neonatal perioral cyanosis and spontaneous pneumothorax; developmental delay and severe speech impairment in first year; left hemiplegia, dystonia, axial hypotonia, spasticity at age 2. This is a large exome sequencing study of 1924 dystonia patients (1895 index patients) screened across 406 dystonia-linked genes. The body text says one index patient carried a presumably pathogenic (likely pathogenic/pathogenic by ACMG) COL4A1 variant: 'only one carrier of a presumably pathogenic variant was found in the remaining 14 uncommon dystonia genes (in ATL1, CHMP2B, COL4A1, ...)'. The COL4A1 genotype-phenotype relationship was classed as inconsistent with the literature ('This included variants in AFG3L2, ATL1, C19orf12, CHMP2B, COL4A1, ...'). The specific variant, the patient's phenotype (presumably dystonia, likely focal or segmental) and the inheritance are given only in Supplementary Table S2. That sheet was truncated out of the supplementary file provided ('3 of 4 sheets in this file were not included'). Only the Table S1 gene-list row for COL4A1 was available. Because the variant identity cannot be read from the supplied text, no variant record was created. A curator should retrieve Table S2 (ACN3-12-1648-s002.xlsx) to extract the single COL4A1 carrier (n_tested = 1895 index patients / 1924 patients). Table S3 (VUS) may also contain further COL4A1/COL4A2 VUS carriers, and it was likewise not provided. No COL4A2 findings are mentioned in the available text.

Cohort study of 1,086 Taiwanese SVD patients (TAG-SVD). 508 patients who were NOTCH3 p.R544C-negative underwent NGS on a 5-gene panel that included COL4A1 (COL4A2 was not on the panel). Two patients were reported with pathogenic or likely pathogenic COL4A1 variants, denominator n=508 on the NGS panel. The specific variants are listed only in eTable 1, which was not provided, so no variant-level records could be created. The text gives only group-level information for the 2 COL4A1 carriers: 50% had a history of stroke, the mean age at first stroke was 50 years, and neither had intracerebral hemorrhage ('Two patients with COL4A1 variant did not suffer from intracerebral hemorrhage.'). Their clinical features are in eTables 2-3, which were also not provided. The figure transcriptions contain no COL4A1/COL4A2 variants.

Cohort of 226 children on ketogenic diet (153 genetically tested). Two patients are reported to carry causative COL4A1 variants, both non-responders to the ketogenic diet. The specific variants are not given in the provided text. Because no specific COL4A1 variant is named, no variant record was created. A curator should check Supplementary Table S3 and the Supplementary Materials for the two COL4A1 carriers. Table 5 row: 'COL4A1 | 2 | 0/2 (0) | 0/2 (0) | 0/2 (0) | 0/2 (0) | 0/2 (0)'.

This is a whole-exome sequencing study of 506 unrelated inherited retinal disease probands. COL4A1 appears in the supplementary PanelApp gene list (MONOALLELIC, Eye Disorders), but that is only a list of genes on the panel. Per-proband variant data are said to be in Supplementary Table 1, which was not provided in parseable form; it may name the variant. No COL4A1/COL4A2 variant record was created because no specific variant is reported in the available text. A curator should check Supplementary Table 1 to confirm the gene (COL4A1 vs COL2A1) and the variant.

WES performed on all patients and parents, so de novo calls counted as confirmed. Mild bilateral white matter abnormalities reported for all patients. No cataracts, kidney abnormalities or elevated CK were found; eye examinations were not performed.

variants.phenotype_details: Multiple kidney cysts, multiple liver cysts and bilateral hydronephrosis; authors state the relationship between the variant and phenotype remains unclear. Age not stated.
evidence_quotes: COL4A1 | NM_001845 (COL4A1): c.3819G>A (p.Trp1273Ter) | Point (nonsense mutation) | PVS1 + PM2 | Likely pathogenic
Another patient was found to have a COL4A1 mutation.
The patient presented with clinical phenotypes of multiple liver and kidney cysts and bilateral hydronephrosis. However, the relationship between the gene mutation and the phenotype remains unclear.

Additionally, tuberous sclerosis complex (TSC) was diagnosed in two cases (0.4%), while autosomal dominant polycystic liver disease (ADPLD), COL4A1-related disease and IFT140-related disease were each identified in one case (0.2%) (Fig. 1, Table 1).
variants.notes: Single COL4A1 case among 702 screened patients with multiple renal cysts; linkage of the Table 3 novel variant to the single COL4A1-related case is inferred (only one COL4A1 case reported). No family studies or parental testing described; transcript version not given. Hydronephrosis and liver cysts placed in 'other'.

extraction.extraction_notes: Retrospective NGS cohort of 702 Chinese patients with multiple renal cysts. Only one COL4A1 variant reported (Table 3, novel, likely pathogenic). Supplementary Tables S3-S6 (full variant lists) were truncated/not provided; supplementary tables shown are gene panel lists only. Figure transcriptions concern PKD1/PKD2 only.

Population screening of whole-genome sequencing data from 15,548 Koreans without neurological disorders across 24 Mendelian stroke genes, including COL4A1 and COL4A2. COL4A1 and COL4A2 results are reported only as aggregate carrier frequencies per 1,000 individuals (Table 2). For COL4A1, the pathogenic clinical frequency was 0 in Koreans, the CADD-predicted frequency 11.77 and the nonsynonymous frequency 19.87. For COL4A2, the pathogenic clinical frequency was 0.06, implying about 1 carrier out of 15,548, with a CADD-predicted frequency of 16.47 and a nonsynonymous frequency of 27.72. No specific COL4A2 variant is named in the provided text. The parsed Supplementary Table 1 is rendered as reversed text and lists rows for ABCC6, ACVRL1, CECR1, CBS, COL3A1, COLGALT1, FBN1, HBB, HTRA1, KRIT1, NF1, NOTCH3 and RNF213, but none for COL4A2. That table appears to show fewer than the 39 pathogenic clinical variants the authors mention, so the COL4A2 variant may exist in the original file but was not available here. Carriers are healthy screened individuals with no phenotype reported. Because no specific COL4A1/COL4A2 variant in a specific individual can be extracted, no variant records were created. A curator should check the original Supplementary Table 1 for the single COL4A2 ClinVar pathogenic or likely pathogenic carrier (denominator n=15,548).

variants.phenotype_details: Female (AA0221-01) with infantile epileptic spasms syndrome, seizure onset at 1 month, focal seizures and spasms, bilateral but markedly asymmetric imaging abnormality, FCDI on histopathology. Left temporoparietooccipital disconnection at 0.8 years, Engel class III, with resolution of the bilateral epileptic encephalopathy and fewer seizures. The authors call it a blended phenotype with a co-occurring 6p25.2 deletion (TUBB2A/TUBB2B) and say imaging showed 'imaging features of both entities'; the specific COL4A1-related imaging features are not described.
evidence_quotes: Germline pathogenic variants were identified in 27/59 (46%) children, in TSC2 (x19), DEPDC5 (x2), CDKL5 (x2), NPRL3 (x1), FGFR1 (x1), TSC1 (x1), and one child with both a TUBB2A/TUBB2B deletion and a pathogenic variant in COL4A1 (x1).
One individual had a blended phenotype as a result of a COL4A1 variant and a 6p25.2 deletion that included TUBB2A and TUBB2B.
One individual had a dual diagnosis of COL4A1-related disorder and a 6p25.2 deletion with imaging features of both entities.
This individual underwent a left temporoparietooccipital disconnection, with resolution of a bilateral epileptic encephalopathy and reduction in seizure frequency.
variants.notes: Variant, sex, age at onset, surgery and histopathology come from Supplementary Table 1 (row AA0221-01, heterozygous). No transcript was stated. Parental testing is not described for the COL4A1 variant, so inheritance is unknown. The variant was detected in brain-derived DNA and is described as germline. The phenotype is confounded by the co-occurring TUBB2A/TUBB2B deletion. The COL4A1 imaging features are not specified, so only 'other' is listed. n_families is set to 0 because the carrier was found by cohort screening. The paper says four genetic diagnoses were previously published but does not say which, so prior reporting of this child cannot be excluded.

extraction.extraction_notes: This is a cohort of 59 children with IESS and focal MCD who underwent epilepsy surgery. Brain tissue was tested by panel sequencing or exome sequencing. COL4A1 c.634G>A p.(G212S) is the only COL4A1/COL4A2 variant reported, and the text says it was found both through ES seqr analysis and through clinical testing. The paper states that four of the genetic diagnoses were previously published but does not identify them. All other variants in the paper are in non-COL4 genes and were not extracted.

Cross-sectional cohort of 129 adults with genetic developmental and epileptic encephalopathies (42 genes) seen at one centre. The cohort includes two individuals with COL4A1-related DEE and one with COL4A2-related DEE. Tables and supplementary material mention these individuals: epileptic encephalopathy, ASD, aggressive behaviour, quadriparesis/hemiparesis, referral for ophthalmological screening, and age bands 20-39. However, no specific COL4A1 or COL4A2 variant (c. or p. nomenclature) is given anywhere in the provided text or supplementary extracts. Inheritance is also not given per individual. No variant-level records were created. The supplementary PDF was parsed with most rows filtered out ([kept N of M rows]), so a variant list may exist in material not provided to me. Inspecting Supplementary Table 2 or other supplementary tables may reveal the specific variants.

variants.phenotype_details: Autosomal dominant intermittent exotropia (IXT) in pedigree F1. Affected: father F1-I1 (onset unclear) and twin-aged daughters F1-II1 and F1-II2 (onset age 5 years).
variants.reported_classification: Novel; candidate/potential pathogenic gene for concomitant exotropia
evidence_quotes: F1 | China | COL4A2 | 13 | rs192250572 | 0.0022 | NM_001846.2 | c.1328C > G(p.P443R) | Missense | AD | Heterozygote | Yes | Novel
Distinct variants of COL4A2 were present in three pedigrees, and distinct variants of SYNE1 were present in two pedigrees.
variants.notes: Variant reported to cosegregate with exotropia in a two-generation AD pedigree (affected father and children), but the proband is identified only by an arrow in Fig. 2, so the proband's inheritance is recorded as unknown. The number of carriers was not stated explicitly. Exotropia was assigned to the ocular system, although it is not a classic COL4A1/2 ocular feature. Variant has an rsID (1000 Genomes AF 0.0022) despite being labelled 'Novel'.

extraction.extraction_notes: The study performed WES/Sanger sequencing on 47 individuals from 10 Chinese exotropia pedigrees; n_tested is set to 47. COL4A2 variants were found in pedigrees F1, F8 and F9 (two variants at codon 1419 in F9). All variants are described as cosegregating under an AD model, but individual carrier genotypes were not tabulated and probands are marked only in Fig. 2 (not provided), so inheritance is coded as unknown. No COL4A1 variants were reported. COL4A2 was not included in the 220-sample sporadic capture panel. No functional work was done. The Fig. 4 transcription is consistent with Table 3.

variants.phenotype_details: 5-year-old male; bilateral cystic dysplastic kidneys progressing to ESKD (peritoneal dialysis from 6 months, kidney transplant at 5 years); stroke and seizure at 6 months during surgery (attributed to hypertension); brain microbleeds (punctate microhemorrhages) attributed to COL4A1 small vessel disease; agenesis of the corpus callosum; hypotonia; global developmental delay, non-verbal; left-eye cataract surgery at age 3; atonic bladder after transplant (proposed new finding); hypothyroidism considered incidental. Also carried biallelic CFTR variants considered non-consequential.
evidence_quotes: Rapid exome testing was performed on the patient with COL4A1-related disorder, which identified that he was heterozygous for a de novo p.G888R pathogenic variant in the COL4A1 gene consistent with COL4A1-related disorder, as well as biallelic cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator (CFTR) variants.
The mother and father of the patient did not harbor the p.G888R variant in the COL4A1 gene.
This patient is a 5-year-old male with COL4A1 collagen mutation with bilateral cystic dysplastic kidneys and global developmental delay.
Neurologic assessment revealed the diagnosis of agenesis of the corpus callosum with brain microbleeding due to COL4A1 collagen disease affecting the small vessels of the brain (Fig. 2).
Cataract surgery on the left eye was done at the age of three.
variants.notes: Only protein-level notation given; no transcript or c. notation. Both parents tested negative; parentage confirmation not explicitly stated. Stroke was attributed by authors to hypertension during surgery. Table 1 lists two prior literature cases of G888R (Meuwissen 2015; ClinVar/Landrum 2016) which are not new individuals and are not counted.

extraction.extraction_notes: Two-case series; only Case 1 involves COL4A1. Case 2 (OFD type 1) had no genetic testing and is not relevant. Table 1 summarises previously published G888R cases, not counted.

This is primarily a functional and mechanistic study using Col4a1+/SVC (G1064D) and Col4a2+/em2Wtsi (exon 18 deletion) mice, a CRISPR-engineered COL4A1 G755R and COL4A2 exon 18 deletion in the HBEC cell line, and hiPSC-derived endothelial cells. The COL4A1 G755R and COL4A2 G702D hiPSC lines come from patients with Gould syndrome that the paper says were 'generated as previously described'. These patients are therefore previously reported, and no new clinical data on them are given here. In those lines the variants increased basal and acetylcholine-stimulated endothelial Ca2+. Seven LINCHPIN patients with sporadic ICH carrying unspecified 'rare coding COL4A1/COL4A2 variants' were analysed histologically (n=7, COL4-ICH group, from the authors' prior sequencing study). However, the specific variants are not named in the text or in Supplemental Table S1, which gives only cohort-level demographics. The 18 SVD patients were selected for common non-coding risk alleles, but no specific SNPs or individual genotypes are reported. No records were created because no new individuals with specified COL4A1/COL4A2 variants are reported.

This paper concerns compound heterozygous PKHD1 variants (c.3592_3628+45del and c.11207T>C, p.Ile3736Thr; NM_138694.4) in two fetuses with ARPKD. COL4A1 is mentioned only as one of several genes included in a STRING protein-protein interaction network analysis. No COL4A1 or COL4A2 variants are reported in any individual.

This is a targeted NGS cohort study of 181 stroke genes in 10,428 Chinese ischaemic stroke/TIA patients (CNSR-III). The body text gives only aggregate COL4A data: 'COL4A2 microangiopathy caused by heterozygous COL4A2 mutations (52.5%, 21/40)' had a positive genetic diagnosis. It also states that more than 90% of COL4A1/COL4A2 mutation carriers had no haemorrhage, or had only microbleeds with other features of cerebral SVD. Individual-level variants are listed in supplementary eTable 3 (759 individuals, each with one P/LP variant), with transcript, c./p. notation, ClinVar/ACMG class and diagnostic category. However, the parsed supplement provided here stops partway through the embolic-stroke section (last row shown is KRAS). No COL4A1 or COL4A2 rows from eTable 3 or eTable 4 were present in the input, so no variant-level records could be extracted. The COL4A1 count is not stated in the body. Of the ~40 COL4A2 carriers, the number of distinct variants and their identities are not available. A curator should consult the full supplementary PDF (svn-2022-002158supp001.pdf, eTable 3/4). Denominator if extracted later: n_tested = 10,428. Carriers were found by screening, with no family studies or segregation (the authors state that familial segregation and de novo status could not be obtained).

variants.phenotype_details: Term male neonate (Patient 1). Prenatal microcephaly and polyhydramnios detected one month before delivery. Brain MRI on day 9 showed volumetric brain reduction with simplified cortical convolutions, polycystic glio-malacic lesions (left parietal/occipital, right parietal-mesial), hemosiderin deposits suggesting prior haemorrhage in right posterior paraventricular region, and thinning of the corpus callosum; lesions presumed antenatal in origin. Day 17 episode of hypertonus and gaze deviation with right focal EEG abnormalities. Later limb hypertonus, axial hypotonia, dysphagia requiring PEG/jejunostomy. At 7 years: severe neurodevelopmental delay, spastic tetraparesis, relational and language disorders. Patent foramen ovale. Ocular, audiological and renal assessments normal. Also carries paternally inherited 16q24.3 microduplication and heterozygous MTHFR C677T. Carrier mother's phenotype not described.
evidence_quotes: Trio analysis identified the heterozygous missense variant c.2705C>G (p.Pro902Arg) of the COL4A1 gene (NM_001845) in maternal segregation in our patient.
The variant was not known in the scientific literature and was reported in the reference population database (gnomAD AF: 0.0004351; dbSNP: rs146134172; ClinVar ID: 80023).
A follow-up at 7 years of age showed that the infant developed severe neurodevelopmental delay, spastic tetraparesis, and relational and language disorders.
variants.notes: Non-glycine missense variant present in gnomAD (AF 0.0004351); maternally inherited, mother's phenotype not reported. Patient also has a paternal 16q24.3 microduplication (KBG syndrome considered and excluded by authors) and MTHFR heterozygosity. No formal ACMG classification given. n_tested set to 0 as no screened cohort size is stated (two clinical cases only).

variants.phenotype_details: Term male neonate (Patient 2). Day 7 of life: jaundice, vomiting, irritability; bilateral grade II-III intraventricular haemorrhage with ventricular dilatation, posterior fossa haemorrhage, small parenchymal haemorrhage in right cerebellar hemisphere, haemorrhage in skull-base cisterns and left extra-axial site; electrical seizures; progressive ventricular dilatation requiring ventricular drain then ventriculo-peritoneal shunt. Left pyelectasia and megaureter; bovine aortic arch and foramen ovale. Ocular and audiological assessments normal; renal function normal. Normal neurodevelopment at 3 years. Heterozygous MTHFR C677T. Carrier mother's phenotype not described.
variants.reported_classification: In silico bioinformatic prediction tools indicated that the variant was pathogenic.
evidence_quotes: Trio analysis identified heterozygous missense variant c.413C>G (p.Pro138Arg) of the COL4A1 gene (NM_001845) present in the newborn and in his mother.
CUS showed asymmetric dilatation of the lateral ventricles with moderate (grade II–III) bilateral intraventricular hemorrhage (IVH) and dilatation of the third ventricle.
The variant was neither known in the scientific literature nor reported in the reference population database (gnomAD, HGMD).
At the follow-up carried out at 3 years of age, the patient’s neurodevelopment was normal.
variants.notes: Non-glycine missense; maternally inherited, mother's clinical status not described. Classification statement reflects in silico predictions rather than a formal ACMG class. Pyelectasia/megaureter placed under 'other' (urinary tract malformation, not HANAC features). n_tested set to 0 as no screened cohort size is stated.

extraction.extraction_notes: Paper reports two new term neonates with ICH and COL4A1 variants (both maternally inherited non-glycine missense). Table 2 is a literature review of 33 previously published cases (e.g., p.G1580R, p.Gly749Ser, p.Gly1384Ser, c.4150+1G>A, etc.); these were cited from earlier papers without new individuals and were not extracted. Table 2 contains apparent transcription errors in cited variants (e.g., 'c.2317G4A'). No supplementary material or figure transcriptions provided.

Systematic review of genetic causes of pediatric hemorrhagic stroke mimicking non-accidental head injury. COL4A1/COL4A2 are discussed only in general terms (gene function, phenotype spectrum, citation of Hausman-Kedem et al. family with a COL4A2 deletion). No specific variants are reported in specific individuals, and no new patients are described. Supplementary Table S1 (quality assessment) was not provided and is not expected to contain variant data.

This is a case report of a COL4A5 frameshift variant (NM_000495.5: c.1095dup p.(Leu366ValfsTer45)) in a family with Alport syndrome and polycystic kidney disease. No COL4A1 or COL4A2 variants are reported in any individual. COL4A1 is mentioned only in passing, in the discussion of HANAC syndrome. Table S1 was referenced but not provided.

variants.phenotype_details: Adult-onset autosomal dominant CSVD: recurrent pontine and subcortical ischemic lesions/lacunes (mean onset 50 ± 9 years; 9 of 19 with onset <50 years; e.g., proband F1-8 pontine stroke at 39 years), vascular leukoencephalopathy/white matter hyperintensities, microbleeds (more frequent in F3-F7), intracerebral hemorrhage in F2-10, F2-15, F5-5, F5-10; cognitive impairment/dementia and gait disturbance in several patients.
variants.functional_evidence: Patient fibroblasts (F1-8, F2-12) showed ~10.6-fold increased COL4A1 mRNA and ~2.8-2.9-fold increased COL4A1 protein, and long-read RNA-seq (F1-8, F2-12, F8-16) showed the inserted allele largely abandons the two distal canonical polyadenylation signals (~5% vs ~87% on the wild-type allele) in favour of proximal PASs.
evidence_quotes: Among 246 probands (141 females [57.3%]; median [IQR] age at referral, 56 [49-64] years), 7 patients of French ancestry carried the insertion.
In these 7 patients’ families, 19 family members with CSVD carried the insertion.
PCR analysis detected the insertion in this patient (F8-16) and her relative F8-12.
Second, this insertion was co-segregating with the affected phenotype in all 7 families.
Intracerebral hemorrhage was observed in patients F2-10, F2-15, F5-5, and F5-10.
variants.notes: 7 carrier probands (F1-F7) were found among 246 screened CSVD probands in the case-control study; an 8th proband (F8-16, with carrier relative F8-12) was identified after the study by targeted PCR and is outside the 246 denominator. A position of c.*1311 appears only in the Figure 5 transcription (model-generated), so hgvs_c is left blank; no transcript is stated. Inheritance is recorded as unknown because parental carrier status is not explicitly reported, although the paper reports autosomal dominant family histories and co-segregation with affected relatives in all 7 families. The total carrier count is ambiguous: the abstract says 19 family members carried it, while the supplementary eTables list 21 affected individuals for F1-F7, plus 2 in F8. The insertion was absent in 467 French controls and in 10,847 gnomAD-SV genomes.

extraction.extraction_notes: Single variant paper: COL4A1 3′UTR AluYa5 mobile element insertion. Genealogical trees (Figure 1, eFigure 1) were not available as text. The eTables give clinical features of the carriers. No HGVS nomenclature is given in the author text.

Cohort of 136 Mexican patients with Marfan syndrome and related connective tissue disorders sequenced on the 174-gene Illumina TruSight Cardio panel. COL4A2 appears only once, in the Introduction, in a general list of genes associated with Marfan-like syndromes. No specific COL4A1 or COL4A2 variant is reported in any individual in the provided text or tables. Reported variants concern FBN1, TGFBR2, TGFB1, TGFB2 and COL5A2. Per-patient variant data are referred to in supplementary material (S3 Dataset, Table S2), which was not provided, so any COL4A1/COL4A2 panel findings there could not be assessed.

Systematic review of the genetics of hydrocephalus; it reports no new patients. COL4A1 and COL4A2 appear only as rows summarizing prior publications. Table 1 cites Verbeek et al., 2012 (COL4A2 c.4165G>A p.G1389R and c.3206delC, familial porencephaly). Table 10 cites Van der Knaap et al., 2006 (a COL4A1 mutation, variant unspecified). These individuals were reported in the earlier papers and add no new carriers here, so no variant records were created.

extraction.extraction_notes: Retrospective cohort of 68 children undergoing epilepsy surgery; 49 had genetic testing (WES/array CGH). Two COL4A1 glycine variants reported in Table 1 only, with no inheritance data. Figure S1 not provided. n_tested set to 49 (genetically tested patients).

variants.phenotype_details: Proband (III-1): migraine without aura; lacunar-type acute infarction of left internal capsule posterior limb at 32 y; patchy periventricular WMHs; multiple microbleeds; multiple cerebral aneurysms (lateral basilar artery, SCA 10x10x12 mm treated with coiling, small ICA C3 aneurysm); vertebrobasilar dolichoectasia; hematuria with normal renal function; mild cognitive decline (MoCA 23); no RAT. Mother (II-1, carrier): cerebellar ischemic infarction at 48 y, diffuse WMHs, a few lacunar infarctions, right ICA aneurysm; hypertension. Grandfather (I-1, untested) had ischemic stroke at 54 y.
evidence_quotes: ES revealed a novel heterozygous variant in exon 42 of the COL4A1 gene (c.3734G>A, p.Gly1245Asp).
Using Sanger sequencing, we detected the same variant in the proband’s mother (Figure 2).

Brain MR angiography (MRA) and computed tomography angiography (CTA) revealed multiple CAs, including the lateral side of the basilar artery (BA) and the superior cerebellar artery (SCA), as well as vertebrobasilar dolichoectasia (Figure 1).
Urinalysis indicated hematuria, although renal function was normal.
Brain MRI at the age of 48 revealed diffuse WMHs and a few lacunar infarctions. MRA of the brain at that time revealed a right ICA aneurysm (Figure 2).
variants.notes: Transcript not stated. Inherited from affected mother (mother tested positive by Sanger; father not described). Grandfather with stroke not genotyped. Paper elsewhere refers to the mother as 'Proband#2' but she is the same family; counted as one proband/family. Lacunar infarction and microbleeds/WMH counted as small_vessel; aneurysms and dolichoectasia as cerebrovascular/other (large vessel).

extraction.extraction_notes: Case report plus literature review. The literature-review variants (53 variants, 76 patients) are listed only in Supplementary Tables S1-S5, which were not provided; Table 2 mentions previously published variants (Gly498Val, Gly417Arg, Pro648Ala, Gly720Asp) with citations only—these are prior reports and not extracted. Only the novel family variant COL4A1 p.Gly1245Asp is recorded.

ADPKD familial variability cohort (Irish Kidney Gene Project). COL4A1 is mentioned only once, in the Figure 1a legend: 'The non-ADPKD phenotypes of 8 probands (PKHD1 (n = 3), MAP2K2 (n = 2), PRKCSH (n = 1), and COL4A1 (n = 1)) were excluded.' This means a single COL4A1 proband from the 522-person registry (313 families) was excluded. No specific COL4A1 variant, phenotype or inheritance information is given, and the variant does not appear in Supplementary Table S1. Supplementary Table S1 lists only PKD1, PKD2 and IFT140 variants. No COL4A2 variants are reported. Because no specific COL4A1 or COL4A2 variant is described, no variant record was created.

Narrative review of SCAD genetics. COL4A1 and COL4A2 are mentioned only as prioritized genes at GWAS risk loci (meta-analysis of 1917 SCAD cases) and as part of an aggregate collagen-gene rare-variant burden enrichment (COL4A1 among 10 collagen genes). No specific COL4A1/COL4A2 variants are reported in specific individuals, so no variant records were created.

variants.phenotype_details: Described only as a 'symptomatic patient' with COL4A1 SVD-related mutation; no clinical details given in this paper.
variants.functional_evidence: Patient hiPSC-derived mural cells showed reduced extracellular collagen IV, increased migration and apoptosis, MMP upregulation and a paracrine detrimental effect on endothelial tight junctions and barrier function, all reversed by CRISPR isogenic correction and partially rescued by MMP inhibition (doxycycline, marimastat).
variants.prior_report_reason: The hiPSC line derives from a patient whose variant is cited to earlier publications (citations elided in text); patient fibroblasts were previously studied, so this individual is not newly reported.
evidence_quotes: Two hiPSC lines with typical SVD-associated SNPs in COL4A genes were used in this study: a COL4A1G755R with a G>A substitution in exon 30 of COL4A1 gene resulting in a change from a glycine to arginine at position 755 from a symptomatic patient and a COL4A2G702D with a G>A replacement in exon 28 of COL4A2 gene, resulting in a change from a glycine to aspartic acid at position 702 from the asymptomatic father of a patient (Table S1) (; ).
There was a significant reduction in collagen IV staining in the ECM of the disease COL4A1/A2 mutant lines compared with the controls, as seen in patient fibroblasts (Figure 1D) ().
variants.notes: Functional iPSC study; individual previously reported elsewhere. No c. notation or transcript given; protein change taken from 'G755R'. Do not count as a new proband.

variants.phenotype_details: hiPSC line derived from the asymptomatic father of a patient; the affected child's phenotype is not described in this paper.
variants.functional_evidence: Carrier-derived hiPSC mural cells showed reduced extracellular collagen IV, increased migration and apoptosis, MMP2/MMP9/MMP14 upregulation and paracrine disruption of endothelial tight junctions/barrier, corrected by isogenic CRISPR repair and partially rescued by MMP inhibitors.
variants.prior_report_reason: Line from the asymptomatic father of a previously reported patient; 'it has been shown that the father's fibroblasts lack some of the properties seen in the patient's fibroblasts', indicating prior publication of this family.
evidence_quotes: First, the COL4A2 hiPSC line was generated from the asymptomatic father of the patient.
Previously, it has been shown that the father’s fibroblasts lack some of the properties seen in the patient’s fibroblasts.
variants.notes: Family previously reported; father is an asymptomatic carrier (child is the affected proband, presumably inherited from father but not detailed here). No c. notation or transcript given.

extraction.extraction_notes: Functional hiPSC disease-modelling study using cells from two previously reported individuals (citations elided in provided text); no new patients. Records included only to capture functional evidence; both flagged as prior reports and should not be counted as new probands. Table S1 (line details) not provided.

variants.phenotype_details: PADMAL. F1-IV-2: right lower-limb hemiparesis from brain infarction at 39, recurrent infarctions, stepwise cognitive impairment at 45, bilateral white matter hyperintensities, pontine oval infarcts ('raisin bread sign'), bedridden before 57, died at 59; autopsy showed hyalinized vessels and thickened media tunica with COL4A1 accumulation, pyramidal tract atrophy. F1-IV-6 (relative): infarction with hemiparesis, anaesthesia and dysarthria at 35, recurrent infarctions, pyramidal signs, hyperreflexia. F2-II-3 (family history of young-onset infarction) and F3-II-2 (sporadic): raisin bread sign, multiple subcortical small infarctions, white matter hyperintensities; no microbleeds or stenosis. Cognitive dysfunction and mood disturbance in two patients.
evidence_quotes: We detected heterozygous COL4A1:c.*33T > A in these patients, while the variant was absent in the controls (Fig. 1D and E, Supplementary Fig. 1A).
COL4A1:c.*33T > A was detected by Sanger sequencing using the genomic DNA of F2-II-3 and F3-II-2 (Supplementary Fig. 1B and C).
Although one CVD patient (F2-II-3) had a familial history of young-onset brain infarction, the other CVD patient (F3-II-2) did not.
She had hemiparesis on her right lower extremity at the age of 39 and was diagnosed with a brain infarction without any vascular risk factors.
These patients also had characteristic small oval infarctions in the pons, and multiple small infarctions in the subcortical hemispheric area and white matter hyperintensities (Fig. 2C and D).
variants.notes: Three families: Family 1 (two affected carriers, F1-IV-2 proband and F1-IV-6) and two unrelated patients (F2, F3) found among a 40-patient juvenile CVD cohort after selection by MRI 'raisin bread sign'. n_tested=40 refers to the cohort only (Family 1 ascertained separately); only selected cohort patients were sequenced. Parental testing not described for any proband; F1-IV-6's affected father was not genotyped. Individual IDs inconsistent in text (F2-IV-8/F3-III-2 in methods vs F2-II-3/F3-II-2 in results). Sanger results for other Family 1 relatives (F1-III-5, III-8, III-9, IV-7) not explicitly reported beyond 'absent in the controls'. Variant previously reported in literature but these families appear new. Transcript not stated.

extraction.extraction_notes: Single recurrent COL4A1 3'UTR variant in three Japanese families. Clinical details in Supplementary Tables 1-3 and Supplementary Figures were not provided. WES also found shared variants in GCM2, HECTD2, COL4A2 (intronic) and ING1, judged benign/unrelated; the COL4A2 intronic variant was not specified and not recorded.

Narrative neuroimaging review of monogenic cerebral small vessel disease. The paper includes illustrative imaging cases: Fig. 1 shows a 3-year-old boy with a COL4A1-related disorder (porencephaly, calcification, microbleeds, cataract). Fig. 2 shows a 5-year-old boy with a COL4A2-related disorder (cystic encephalomalacia, right hemiparesis). Neither case is given a specific variant, so no variant-level records were created.

Case report of three sisters with cystic kidney disease. The only mention of COL4A1 is as one of 43 genes on the cystic kidney disease NGS panel. No COL4A1 or COL4A2 variant was reported in any sister. The reported variants are PKD1 c.11803del, p.(Ala3935Profs*10), found in two sisters, and TTC21B c.1593_1595del, p.(Leu532del), a VUS found in one sister. Neither gene is in scope.

Narrative review of Alport syndrome (COL4A3/COL4A4/COL4A5). COL4A1 and COL4A2 are mentioned only as members of the type IV collagen family. No specific COL4A1/COL4A2 variants are reported in any individual.

Korean multicenter cohort of 725 adults with ≥3 renal cysts, screened with an 89-gene ciliopathy panel. COL4A1 is listed only as a genotype found in 0.2% of the 560 typical ADPKD patients, which is likely 1 patient. The paper gives no specific variant, no HGVS, no individual phenotype and no inheritance data. COL4A2 is not mentioned. Because no specific COL4A1/COL4A2 variant is reported, no variant record was created. Relevant sentence: 'The other genotypes responsible for the typical ADPKD phenotype were found to include COL4A5 (1.1%), TSC1 (0.5%), HNF1β (0.4%), AVP (0.4%), AHI1, ALG8, COL4A1, COL4A3, DYNC2H1, EYA1, HSPA6, LRP5, NEK8, PRKCSH, TSC2, and UMOD (all 0.2%).' Figure 2 may contain more detail but was not provided as text. It is also unclear whether the COL4A1 finding was classified as pathogenic, a damaging (DM) variant or a VUS.

Neuropsychological case-control study of 20 sporadic cSVD patients, 20 CADASIL (NOTCH3) patients and 20 controls. COL4A1 and COL4A2 are mentioned only as part of a 7-gene NGS panel that was used to exclude monogenic causes in the sporadic cSVD group. No COL4A1 or COL4A2 variants are reported in any individual.

variants.phenotype_details: Male proband of Venezuelan/South American origin (family OFT-00816) diagnosed with bilateral topographic keratoconus at age 11 (RE stage 2, LE stage 1-2, duck pattern); also atopy, eye rubbing, obesity; no family history of KC. Variant inherited from mother, whose phenotype is not described as affected. Proband also carries heterozygous variants in HSPG2, COL23A1, ARG1 and DUXA (oligogenic model proposed).
evidence_quotes: COL4A2 | NM_001846.3:c.3635-3C>T | VUS | Het | AD | Maternal

Several mutations in heterozygosis in genes involved in the structure of the corneal layers were detected in the patient: a missense variant (p.(Arg3362Cys)) in the HSPG2 gene coding for perlecan; a variant affecting the splicing region (c.3635-3 C>T) in the COL4A2 gene coding for the α2 chain of collagen IV; a missense variant (p.(Asp176Tyr)) in the COL23A1 gene; and a variant (p.(Ile129Thr)) in the ARG1 gene involved in the correct deposition of collagen (20).

Male of Venezuelan origin diagnosed with bilateral topographic KC at age 11. The patient suffered from atopy, a history of obesity and an eye-rubbing habit whilst lacking a positive family history of KC.
variants.notes: Splice-region intronic variant (-3), no splicing analysis reported. Phenotype is non-syndromic keratoconus (corneal), not a typical COL4A2 phenotype; mapped to 'ocular' as the closest token. Mother is a carrier (maternal inheritance) but family has no reported KC history, so the mother is presumably unaffected. Proposed as part of oligogenic background; causality not established. Table 2 lists ethnicity as South American; text says Venezuelan.

extraction.extraction_notes: Whole-exome sequencing of 24 unrelated pediatric keratoconus probands (63 participants including parents). Only one COL4A1/COL4A2 variant reported: COL4A2 c.3635-3C>T in family OFT-00816. Other collagen IV variants (COL4A3, COL4A4) are outside scope. Pedigree figure (Figure A1) not provided.

variants.phenotype_details: Family SCAD-03 (affected sister pair): II.1 SCAD at 43 y with FMD and coronary tortuosity; II.2 SCAD at 45 y with migraine headaches. The variant co-segregated with SCAD under an autosomal dominant model with incomplete penetrance. No multisystem connective tissue disorder was found on genetics evaluation of the proband.
variants.reported_classification: Top candidate gene in family; HGMD deleterious classification CM1818194
evidence_quotes: A particularly notable finding in our study was the identification of collagen genes as top candidates for F-SCAD in five families (SCAD-09, -03, -07, -14, -15), each harboring a rare missense variant leading to substitution of a highly conserved amino acid: COL3A1 (Arg446Cys), COL4A1 (Pro530Ser), COL4A2 (Gly151Ser and Gly413Arg), and COL5A2 (Gln902Pro).
Co-segregation with disease required that a variant was present in all affected family members and obligate carriers.
variants.notes: The assignment of this variant to family SCAD-03 is explicit only in the Figure 1 transcription. It is consistent with the order of families and variants in the Discussion text. gnomAD MAF is 0.03%. The transcript is not stated. Carrier count and parental genotypes are not itemized; the individual genotypes are shown only in the pedigree figure. SCAD is listed under 'other' because no listed system token fits.

variants.phenotype_details: Family SCAD-07: proband III.1 had SCAD at 41 y with FMD, emotional stress and a tiny cerebral aneurysm. Sister III.2 had SCAD at 37 y with FMD and coronary tortuosity. Maternal aunt II.3 had a cerebral aneurysm and an intracranial artery aneurysm at 65 y; her carrier status is not stated in the text.
evidence_quotes: Moreover, two families had distinct heterozygous missense variants in COL4A2, which encodes the collagen type IV alpha 2 chain (SCAD-07 and SCAD-14; Figure 1, Table 2).

Moreover, brain imaging performed in all but one affected family member (SCAD-09 proband) revealed subtle vascular disease in only one individual with a tiny cerebral aneurysm (SCAD-07 proband), whose maternal aunt also had a cerebral aneurysm by history.
variants.notes: The text places COL4A2 variants in SCAD-07 and SCAD-14 but does not say which variant is in which family. The pairing of G413R with SCAD-07 comes from the Figure 1 transcription. A cerebral aneurysm was mapped to 'cerebrovascular' as a judgement call. The number of carriers, including whether the aunt was genotyped, is not stated.

variants.phenotype_details: Family SCAD-14 (affected mother-daughter pair): I.2 had SCAD at 59 y and again at 61 y (recurrent), with FMD. II.1 had SCAD at 32 y with physical exertion as a trigger.
evidence_quotes: Moreover, two families had distinct heterozygous missense variants in COL4A2, which encodes the collagen type IV alpha 2 chain (SCAD-07 and SCAD-14; Figure 1, Table 2).

Families were comprised of two affected mother–daughter pairs (SCAD-12, 14), two affected sister pair–parent trios (SCAD-13, 15), one affected sibling trio (SCAD-06), six affected sister pairs (SCAD-01, 02, 03, 04, 05, 07), one affected sibling pair–daughter trio (SCAD-10), and three families with distantly-related affected relatives (SCAD-08, 09, 11).
variants.notes: The pairing of G151S with SCAD-14 comes from the Figure 1 transcription. The CADD score was 24.8, the 75th percentile. Which mother-daughter member is the proband is not stated in the text, so inheritance in the proband is recorded as unknown. The variant co-segregated in both affected members.

extraction.extraction_notes: This is a WGS study of 15 familial SCAD probands (n_tested=15) with relatives; 31 affected individuals and 16 unaffected parents were sequenced. Three COL4A1/COL4A2 candidate variants were prioritized as top family candidates rather than as ACMG pathogenic variants; only the NOTCH1 and KCNK3 variants were called likely pathogenic. The variant-to-family mapping for the COL4A1/COL4A2 variants depends partly on the Figure 1 transcription. No transcripts are given, no functional work was done, and no individual-level genotypes are given in the text.

Exome/panel sequencing cohort of 275 polymicrogyria families. The text states: 'We also identified 6 families with variants in the COL4A1 or COL4A2 gene.' The specific COL4A1/COL4A2 variants and individuals are listed only in eTable 2 in Supplement 2, which was not provided. The supplied supplements are Supplement 1 (methods and gene panels), Supplement 3 (group authors) and Supplement 4 (data sharing statement). No COL4A1/COL4A2 variant is named in the provided text, so no variant records could be created. A curator should obtain eTable 2 (Supplement 2) to extract the 6 COL4A1/COL4A2 families; the denominator is n_tested = 275 families.

variants.phenotype_details: 35-year-old Mexican female, born prematurely at 7 months; first ischemic stroke 4 years before evaluation (~age 31) with right hemiparesis and dysarthria; MRI posterior pattern leukodystrophy, acute lacunar infarct in left caudate body; recurrent acute right frontal and parietal lacunar ischemic strokes 3 years later; elevated CPK (595 U/L) with normal EMG; reduced left carotid flow; normal renal function. Mother had probable left cerebral infarction with chronic right hemiplegia (untested).
evidence_quotes: a genetic complete exome sequencing (CentoXome GOLD) test was ordered, and a change in direction mutation in COL4A1 (variant coordinates; Chr13 [GRCh37]: g.110828842C>T; NM_001845.4:c.2987G>A; p.(Gly996Asp) and Exon 36) was found (Table 1).
The brain 1.5TMR scan showed a posterior pattern of leukodystrophy and acute lacunar infarction in the body of the left caudal nucleus.

Her brain MRI (Figure 1), FLAIR, and T2 sequences showed posterior leukodystrophy, acute right frontal and parietal lacunar ischemic strokes, and chronic lacunar infarction in the left body of the caudate nucleus and she was hospitalized again to receive IV methylprednisolone in the bolus with recovery to the baseline.
There is an unclear history of probable cerebral stroke in her mother; however, genetic studies have been offered to her relatives to confirm and results are yet to come.

In our patient, we only found an elevated CPK levels as systemic manifestation; however, a muscle biopsy was not performed because the electromyography was normal and other studies were not relevant for the management.
variants.notes: Inheritance unknown: relatives offered testing, results pending; mother has possible stroke history. Paper once erroneously refers to 'COL4A4' in discussion, but variant is clearly COL4A1. Lacunar infarcts listed under small_vessel; recurrent ischemic stroke also under cerebrovascular.

extraction.extraction_notes: Single case report; exome sequencing on one patient. Text contains typo 'COL4A4' referring to the same COL4A1 finding.

Population-based cohort of 109 children with polymicrogyria in Stockholm; 90 had genetic testing. The body text states that 'one additional individual with presumed vascular aetiology had a pathogenic variant in COL4A1 and therefore was classified as genetic', but the specific variant (cDNA/protein change), inheritance and individual phenotype are not given in the provided text. Variant details are presumably in Supplementary Table 1, which was not provided. No record was created because no specific COL4A1 variant is named. A curator may wish to retrieve Supplementary Table 1 to capture this one COL4A1 carrier: presumed vascular PMG, polymicrogyria (cerebrovascular), with a denominator of 109 cohort / 90 genetically tested. The authors also mention a planned follow-up paper on the genetic results.

variants.phenotype_details: Muslim Arab male with dysplastic kidneys (CAKUT); kidney failure at 5.5 y; no consanguinity
evidence_quotes: 21–115 | Muslim Arab male with dysplastic kidneys. Kidney failure at 5.5 y; no consanguinity | CAKUT | COL4A1 | c.1807C>Tp.Pro603SerNM_001845.6 | Het | 25.2 | 0.0019% | LP | PM2, PP3, PM1, PP5PP2
We detected diagnostic single-gene etiologies in 36 of the 79 participants (45%), encompassing 21 distinct monogenic disorders (Table 2, Figure 1).
variants.notes: Heterozygous non-glycine missense found by exome screening of a national pediatric dialysis cohort (n=79). Inheritance and segregation not reported for this individual. Classified LP by authors (criteria include PP5). The kidney phenotype is CAKUT, which is not a classic HANAC presentation. It is listed under renal_hanac only because the kidney failure is attributed to the variant.

variants.phenotype_details: Jewish male with CAKUT and intellectual disability; kidney failure at 14 y; no consanguinity; ring chromosome 13
evidence_quotes: 21–315 | Jewish male with CAKUT and Intellectual disability; kidney failure at 14 y; no consanguinity | CAKUT | COL4A1 deletion | chr13 deletion:110,152,323-110,214,025ring chromosome 13 | Het | NA | | LP |
Nonetheless, using the exome data, we were still able to detect medium and large size gene deletions in 6 patients.
variants.notes: Heterozygous deletion involving COL4A1 in the context of a ring chromosome 13, called from exome data. Genome build presumably hg38, since reads were aligned to hg38. The extent of COL4A1 involvement and of other genes is not specified. Intellectual disability may reflect the ring chromosome rather than COL4A1. Inheritance not reported.

extraction.extraction_notes: Nationwide exome sequencing of 79 Israeli children on dialysis. Two COL4A1 findings are listed in Table 2, both attributed by the authors to CAKUT. The paper gives no inheritance or segregation details for either COL4A1 case. Supplementary Table S1 (gene panel) and Supplementary Figure S1 were not provided.

Whole-genome sequencing study of 10,241 Chinese ischemic stroke patients (STROMICS). The only COL4A2 mention is a GWAS stroke-risk locus, discussed as allele-frequency comparisons: 'the risk allele of the two loci (COL4A2 and SH3PXD2A) showed lower frequencies in STROMICS compared to the reference populations.' This is an association polymorphism, not a variant reported in specific affected individuals, so no record was created. The specific variant ID is not given in the text; it may appear in Supplementary Table S9, which was not provided. No COL4A1 variants are reported. ClinVar P/LP variants are listed in Supplementary Table S22, which was not provided. That table could include COL4A1/COL4A2 carriers, but the main text describes individual-level analysis only for NOTCH3.

Systematic review of Axenfeld-Rieger syndrome literature. COL4A1 is mentioned only at the gene level, summarised from previously published studies (Coupry 2010, Meuwissen 2015, Nandeesh 2020, Rodahl 2013, Saffari 2020, Shah 2012, Sibon 2007). No specific COL4A1/COL4A2 variants are named, no new patients are reported, and no primary data were collected.

variants.phenotype_details: Pontine autosomal dominant microangiopathy and leukoencephalopathy (PADMAL) with recurrent brainstem infarctions; T1 sagittal and T2 axial MRI showed fused infarctions in the pons at age 43 (age at imaging); white matter lesions (inclusion criterion). Age at onset not individually stated.
evidence_quotes: We identified a heterozygous c.*34G>T mutation in the 3′ untranslated region of the COL4A1 gene in the patient with PADMAL, three other mutations in the coding region of COL4A1 and two mutations in COL4A2 (Supplementary Table 6).

Intracranial haemorrhage was found in 2 patients (Fig. 2D) and recurrent brainstem infarctions were found in one patient with pontine autosomal dominant microangiopathy and leukoencephalopathy (PADMAL, Fig. 2E and F).
(E and F) T1 sagittal and T2 axial images showed fused infarctions (arrows) in the pons in a 43-year-old patient with pontine autosomal dominant microangiopathy and leukoencephalopathy (PADMAL).
A consecutive series of 309 adult patients clinically suspected of gLEs were recruited from the Department of Neurology, Beijing Tiantan Hospital, between January 2014 and December 2021.
variants.notes: Transcript not stated; ACMG classification and segregation/inheritance not given in main text (may be in Supplementary Table 6, not provided). Found by WES screening of a 309-patient cohort; no family study described, so n_families set to 0. Family history not described in main text.

extraction.extraction_notes: Six patients with COL4A1/2-related disorders were identified among 309 adults sequenced by WES (201 diagnosed). Only one variant (COL4A1 c.*34G>T, PADMAL patient) is named in the main text. The other five variants (three COL4A1 coding variants, two COL4A2 variants) and per-patient phenotypes (ICH in 2, HANAC with muscle cramps in 2, intracranial aneurysm in 1, eye/kidney/heart involvement; COL4A2 patient aged 66 with ICH and microbleeds in Fig. 2D) are listed only in Supplementary Table 6, which was not provided; records for these could not be created because the variants are not specified.

variants.phenotype_details: Patient-level phenotype for this variant is not given; reported only at group level for 3 COL4A1 (BSVD1) patients: mean age at onset 39.3 ± 3.1 years; ataxia (3), ischemic stroke (2), cognitive decline (1), parkinsonism (1), limited eye movement; prominent frontoparietal and periventricular WMHs (3), multiple lacunar infarcts in all cases, microbleeds (2).
evidence_quotes: COL4A1 | E16‐17 del | ‐ | AD | — | — | NA | NA | NA | LP (PS2 + PM2 + PP4)
Moreover, three patients with mutations in COL4A1 were identified, with an average age at onset of 39.3 ± 3.1 years.
Multiple lacunar infarcts were observed in all cases.
A total of 129 patients, suspected of having possible genetic leukoencephalopathy, were ultimately enrolled in the study.
variants.notes: Exon 16-17 deletion listed among novel LP variants (Table 1); exact breakpoints, transcript and number of carriers not stated (assumed 1 proband). De novo status inferred only from the ACMG PS2 code; parental testing not described in the text, so recorded as assumed. Paper also states 'no pathological CNVs were identified', which is inconsistent with an exon deletion. Phenotypes are group-level for the 3 COL4A1 patients; small_vessel listed because WMHs and lacunar infarcts were present in all 3; stroke (2/3) could not be attributed to this carrier. n_families set to 0 because carrier was found by cohort screening and no family study was described.

extraction.extraction_notes: Three COL4A1 (BSVD1) patients were diagnosed in a 129-patient WES cohort, but only one COL4A1 variant (novel E16-17 del) appears in the body text. The other COL4A1 P/LP variants are in Table S1 (known variants) and COL4A1 VUS in Table S2, which were not provided. Per-patient clinical data are in Tables S3/S4 (not provided). The COL4A1/2 figure in the cross-population comparison (2.1% of 438 Chinese cases) is literature-aggregated and not extracted.

This paper reports an MBTPS2 variant (c.516A>C, p.Glu172Asp) in a fetus with X-linked osteogenesis imperfecta. It reports no COL4A1 or COL4A2 variants. COL4A1/COL4A2 come up only as a transcript-level downregulation and as type IV collagen protein deposition measured in fibroblasts with MBTPS2 variants. The paper describes no specific COL4A1/COL4A2 variants in any individual.

variants.phenotype_details: Male neonate (prenatal detection, born 38w4d): microcephaly, scattered multifocal hemorrhagic/ischemic infarcts, ex-vacuo dilatation, diffuse mild polymicrogyria, dysgenesis of corpus callosum, inferior vermian hypoplasia, possible calcification; frequent subclinical seizures requiring multiple agents; bilateral optic nerve hypoplasia (concern for septo-optic dysplasia), left posterior polar cataract with microspherophakia; cardiac: moderate muscular VSD, hypoplastic aortic arch/suspected coarctation, mild-moderate hypoplastic left ventricle, PDA, fenestrated atrial septum (authors note cardiac findings not previously associated with COL4A1); mild left renal calyceal dilatation. Also copy-neutral absence of heterozygosity on chromosome 11.
evidence_quotes: XomeDxXpress Clinical Exome Sequence Analysis showed a de novo heterozygous variant at c. 2771 G>A of the Col4a1 gene.

Prenatal ultrasound showed multiple fetal anomalies, including microcephaly, scattered multifocal hemorrhagic/ischemic infarcts, ex-vacuo dilatation, polymicrogyria, moderate ventricular septal defect (VSD), and a narrowed aortic arch.
An ophthalmology evaluation showed small, hypo-plastic optic nerves of both eyes, concerning for septo-optic dysplasia. The left eye showed a posterior polar cataract with microspherophakia.
Postnatal renal ultrasound showed mild calyceal dilatation of the left kidney.

The cardiac findings in our patient, namely aortic coarctation and VSD, have not previously been associated with Gould Syndrome or a Col4a1 variant and potentially convey the presence of multiple disorders.
variants.notes: No protein change or transcript stated; variant_type set to 'other' because the amino acid consequence is not given (likely missense but not stated). Called de novo without explicit description of parental testing of the variant (parents apparently tested for the chromosome 11 AOH region), so counted as assumed. Renal calyceal dilatation not classed as HANAC feature; placed under other. A coexisting chromosome 11 copy-neutral AOH region may contribute to phenotype (esp. cardiac).

extraction.extraction_notes: Single neonatal case report. Variant given only as cDNA 'c. 2771 G>A' without transcript or protein annotation. The SNP association with arterial stiffness mentioned in Discussion is cited from another study and not extracted.

This is an Epilepsy Currents commentary on Bedrosian et al. 2022 (Epilepsia, PMID 35687047). It mentions only that one of 50 surgical epilepsy patients with FCD carried a germline COL4A1 mutation. No specific variant, nomenclature or individual-level phenotype is given, and the patient belongs to the cited original study, not to new individuals reported here. No variant records were created; the original Bedrosian et al. paper should be curated instead.
