extraction.extraction_notes: Cohort of 85 children with PVHI/PVI (Estonian Pediatric Stroke Database) screened by exome (60), TruSight One Expanded panel (23) or single-gene testing (2). Six COL4A1/COL4A2 P/LP variants extracted from Table 2 (patients 1-6); COL5A1, NOTCH3, MT-TL1, F2, SERPINC1 variants excluded as non-target genes. One additional COL4A2 variant of unknown significance (one patient with presumed antenatal PVI) is listed only in Supplementary Table 3, which was not provided; it could not be extracted. Transcripts not stated (hg19 alignment). Discussion mentions '2 families with a presumed antenatal periventricular venous infarction child with COL4A1 pathogenic variants', but Table 2 shows maternal inheritance for patient 4 (presumed antenatal) and patient 5 (antenatal); minor inconsistency.

Narrative review of the genetics of cerebral small vessel disease. COL4A1/COL4A2 appear only in general terms: monogenic disease descriptions, and GWAS or candidate-gene associations at 13q34 with white-matter hyperintensities and ICH. No specific COL4A1/COL4A2 variants are reported in specific individuals, and no new patients or functional data are presented.

Whole-exome sequencing gene-burden study of 387 Saudi ischemic stroke patients versus about 20,230 Saudi Human Genome Project controls. COL4A2 appears only as a gene-level burden signal in Table 2, with no individual variants named in the body text: 27 heterozygous and 1 homozygous cases versus 217 heterozygous and 9 homozygous controls; dominant-model P = 2.70E-07, recessive-model P = 0.435679. COL4A1 is not mentioned. Supplementary Tables S1 (rare impactful variants) and S2 (full burden results) are referred to but were not provided. These may list specific COL4A2 variants. Even so, the paper presents them only as aggregate burden and polygenic-risk-score inputs, not as candidate causal variants in specific individuals with phenotypes. For that reason no variant-level records were created.

variants.phenotype_details: Original German PADMAL family: 6 carriers clinically and radiologically affected, 3 radiologically affected only, 3 carriers unaffected (at risk). Radiological: pontine lacunes followed by supratentorial white matter lesions and atrophy of pons and medulla. Clinical onset mean 52 (SD 10) years, radiological onset mean 52 (affected) / 36 (radiologically only). First symptoms dysarthria (3), vertigo (2), ataxia (2), hemiparesis (1); further symptoms tetraparesis (2), mutism (2), dementia (3); stroke history. Death mean age 67 (6th-8th decade). No cerebral haemorrhage or porencephaly.
variants.prior_report_reason: This is the original PADMAL family (Colmant and Hagel); authors state the work complements previously published clinical, radiological and pathological data of this family and completes their previous reports.
evidence_quotes: The anonymized pedigree (Fig. 2) shows that genotypes were available for 17 family members excluding married-in individuals of whom 6 were clinically and radiologically affected, and 3 were only radiologically affected.
Three individuals were clinically and radiologically unaffected but carried the causative COL4A1 variant and were therefore defined as at risk.
Red “v” stands for heterozygous COL4A1, NM_001845.6:c.*31G > T carriers and wt for individuals who are homozygous wildtype.
First, it shows the co-segregation of a COL4A1 3’UTR variant with the disease in the family for which the name Pontine Autosomal Dominant Microangiopathy with Leukoencephalopathy (PADMAL) was coined.
In all but one clinically affected individual, the first symptom (dysarthria, vertigo, ataxia) was most likely related to a brainstem stroke.
variants.notes: Variant lies in the miRNA-29-binding site of the COL4A1 3'UTR. Family previously published (variant likely first reported in an earlier publication). Total carriers 12 derived from 6+3+3 genotyped carriers described. Inheritance coded as inherited because the family shows autosomal dominant co-segregation; the proband is not individually identified and the pedigree is anonymized. n_tested set to 0 because the variant was not found by cohort screening (17 family members genotyped); 874 sporadic stroke patients screened carried no variant in the binding site.

extraction.extraction_notes: Single family study plus screening of 874 sporadic stroke patients (225 Muenster, 649 Rostock) for variants in the COL4A1 miRNA-29-binding site; no variants were found in the sporadic patients. Pedigree figure (Fig. 2) not provided as text; individual-level data omitted by authors for anonymity.

Whole-genome re-sequencing of 8 members of one Chinese pedigree with type 2 diabetes and interstitial lung disease. COL4A1 is never mentioned. COL4A2 appears only in Table 2, a list of structural variants shared by at least 7 of the 8 sequenced subjects. That table lists an intrachromosomal translocation (ITX) breakpoint chr13:111076796 (COL4A2) to chr13:41271120 (FOXO1/MIR320D1). COL4A2 is also named as a node in the protein-protein interaction analysis. The SV was present in at least 7 of 8 subjects, including healthy relatives, and the paper does not specify which individuals carry it. The authors state that its role in disease is unclear, and they do not propose it as a candidate cause of any phenotype. No COL4A-related phenotypes (cerebrovascular, renal, ocular, muscle) are reported. The variant the authors prioritise is MUC5B rs2943512, which is not relevant to COL4A1 or COL4A2. No record was created because no COL4A1/COL4A2 variant is reported in specific affected individuals as a candidate cause. The genome build is not stated; coordinates appear to be hg19.

This paper reports COL4A4 variants only: c.595-1G>A (splice) in pedigree 1 and c.1715G>C (p.Gly572Ala) in pedigree 2, both in families with familial hematuria. It reports no COL4A1 or COL4A2 variants. COL4A1 and COL4A2 are mentioned only in passing in the Discussion, as members of the type IV collagen gene family. No records were created.

variants.phenotype_details: UK Biobank population carriers (aged 40-69 at recruitment). No individual-level phenotypes reported. Compared with other COL4A1/2 carriers, p.Gly332Arg carriers did not differ in risk of any outcome (any stroke OR 1.72, ICH OR 5.72, vascular dementia OR 25.46, all non-significant; no migraine-with-aura cases). Pooled COL4A1/2 carriers (n=336) had increased ICH risk (OR 3.56), not significant after FDR correction.
evidence_quotes: The most common variant in COL4A1/2 was p.Gly332Arg, found in 174 individuals.

The COL4A1 p.Gly332Arg variant was found in 172 individuals. Compared with other COL4A1/2 carriers, p.Gly332Arg carriers did not differ in their risk of any of the clinical outcomes assessed (Table 2).
For COL4A1/2, 336 heterozygous carriers were found (1 in 1353); 11 unique variants were identified (eFigures 4 and 5 and eTable 5 in the Supplement).
variants.notes: Carrier count is internally inconsistent: 174 in Results and Table 2 header (N1 = 174) versus 172 in the 'Location of Variants' section. Carriers were identified by exome screening of a population biobank, not ascertained as patients. Relatedness among carriers is not stated per variant. No inheritance data are given. The paper states only variants classified pathogenic or likely pathogenic by ACMG were included; the specific class for this variant is in eTable 5, which was not available. No c. notation or transcript is given in the provided text.

extraction.extraction_notes: This is a UK Biobank exome screening study (n = 454,756) of 336 COL4A1/2 carriers of 11 unique pathogenic or likely pathogenic triple-helix variants. Only COL4A1 p.Gly332Arg is named in the author text. The other 10 COL4A1/2 variants and their carrier counts are listed in supplementary eTable 5, but that table was truncated out of the provided supplement: 10 of 17 sheets were not included, and parsing stopped at the HTRA1 table. These variants therefore could not be extracted. Phenotype data are aggregate associations only (ORs/HRs), with no individual-level carrier phenotypes. NOTCH3 and HTRA1 variants were ignored.

Case-control association study of keratoconus (257 cases, 253 controls) genotyping common SNPs in COL4A3 (rs55703767, rs10178458) and COL4A4 (rs2229814, rs2228555) only. No COL4A1 or COL4A2 variants are reported; COL4A1/COL4A2 are mentioned only in passing as negative findings in prior studies. All variants are association polymorphisms reported with genotype frequencies and odds ratios, not candidate causal variants in specific individuals, so no records were created.

variants.phenotype_details: Adult-onset severe CSVD (inclusion required severe symmetrical WMHs Fazekas grade 3/III plus lacunar infarcts, dPVS, external capsular lesions or microbleeds); group 1 patient (onset of neurological symptoms/signs <=55 years) without family history. Individual-level clinical details not given in main text.
evidence_quotes: One patient had a mutation in the 3'-untranslated region of COL4A1 (c.*33T>A), which was previously reported.
Per the ACMG criteria, 14 mutations in HTRA1, ABCC6 and TREX1 corresponded to pathogenic/likely pathogenic mutations, and 2 mutations in COL4A1/A2 corresponded to uncertain significance.
variants.notes: Variant previously reported in the literature (not necessarily this patient). Found by WES among 63 undiagnosed patients out of 106 in the cohort; no transcript stated; no parental testing described. Individual phenotype details likely in supplementary tables not provided.

variants.phenotype_details: Adult-onset severe CSVD (severe WMHs Fazekas 3/III plus lacunar infarcts, dPVS, ECL or microbleeds per inclusion criteria); group 1 patient (onset <=55 years) with positive family history in first-degree relatives. Individual details not given in main text.
evidence_quotes: Another patient had a novel mutation in COL4A2 (p.Gly1176del).
Per the ACMG criteria, 14 mutations in HTRA1, ABCC6 and TREX1 corresponded to pathogenic/likely pathogenic mutations, and 2 mutations in COL4A1/A2 corresponded to uncertain significance.
Hence, it is unclear whether deletion of a single amino acid (glycine) can cause CSVD.
variants.notes: In-frame single glycine deletion in the triple-helical Gly-X-Y region; authors question pathogenicity. Family history positive in a first-degree relative but no segregation testing described. Found by WES among 63 undiagnosed patients out of 106; no CNV found on cn.MOPS. No transcript stated.

extraction.extraction_notes: Cohort of 106 Japanese patients with adult-onset severe CSVD (75 group 1, 31 group 2); after NOTCH3/HTRA1/TREX1 testing, WES was performed on 63 undiagnosed patients. n_tested set to the full cohort of 106. Individual clinical data for COL4A1/COL4A2 carriers likely in online supplemental tables (not provided). Other genes (NOTCH3, HTRA1, ABCC6, TREX1) not extracted.

Database-construction paper (NCGR) that collates published genetic findings in neonatal encephalopathy with suspected HIE and cerebral palsy. It reports no new patients. The only specific COL4A1 variant named is NM_001845:c.2263G > A, described as previously reported in a patient with CP due to birth asphyxia; the source studies are cited but the reference list is not in the provided text. Other COL4A1 variants are said to be catalogued in Supplementary Tables 1-7, which were not provided. No COL4A2 variants are mentioned. Because no new individuals are reported, no variant records were created.

variants.phenotype_details: Female neonate; microcephaly (HC -3.41 SD); severe early jaundice on Day 1 requiring exchange transfusion; bilateral ventricular enlargement, periventricular calcification, ischemic changes on CT; multiple hemorrhagic infarcts with intraventricular perforation and cerebellar atrophy on MRI (Day 10); elevated CK (4050 U/L) that later improved; recurrent anemia requiring two red-cell transfusions; seizures from neonatal period, West syndrome with hypsarrhythmia at 6 months; developmental delay at 10 months. Echocardiography, abdominal ultrasound and ophthalmologic exam were normal.
variants.reported_classification: considered to be a pathological variant
evidence_quotes: we performed a genetic investigation of the patient using next generation sequencing and identified a heterozygous missense mutation in the COL4A1 gene (p. Gly586Asp, chr13: 11018625).
We also examined the parents' genes and found no abnormalities in the COL4A1 gene, indicating that the mutation was de novo.
A simple brain MRI was performed on Day 10 and showed multiple hemorrhagic infarcts with intraventricular perforation and cerebellar atrophy (Figure 2).
Blood tests at the time of admission showed an elevated level of CK (4050 U/L) and hyperbilirubinemia (13.7 mg/dL [234.3 μmol/L]).
She was diagnosed with West syndrome and is being managed with multiple antiepileptic drugs and ACTH therapy.
variants.notes: No transcript or c. notation given; genomic coordinate chr13:11018625 given without genome build (likely hg38 based on value, but not stated). Parental testing described as examining parents' COL4A1 genes with no abnormalities; parentage confirmation not mentioned. Elevated CK in a neonate listed under muscle as reported; may be confounded by neonatal context.

extraction.extraction_notes: Single case report of a de novo COL4A1 glycine substitution. Cohort figures (Tomotaki, Meuwissen) are cited from prior literature and not extracted.

This paper reports biallelic KIF26A variants in 5 families with congenital brain malformations. It does not report any COL4A1 or COL4A2 variant. COL4A1/COL4A2 appear only as a negative screen: for patient B01 (Family B, bilateral schizencephaly), the authors state 'Sequencing for COL4A1 and COL4A2 variants was normal'. No COL4A1/COL4A2 variant-level data were extracted.

UK Biobank population-based exome study (199,313 unrelated exome-sequenced participants after QC; 200,603 before exclusions). It screened for 260 literature- or ClinVar-derived putative pathogenic variants in CTSA, TREX1, HTRA1, COL4A1 and COL4A2. In the UKB it found 17 COL4A1 variants (481 carriers) and 5 COL4A2 variants (336 carriers). No CTSA or TREX1 variants were present. Per-variant identities, carrier counts and phenotypes are given only in supplementary eTables 2-4 (links.lww.com/NXG/A541), which were not provided. Tables 1 and 2 were also not rendered beyond their captions. Only two specific variants are named in the body text: COL4A2 c.3448C>A and c.5068G>A. These are described only by their frequency in Black participants (1.2% and 4.7%, respectively). Together they drive the finding that 190 of 336 COL4A2 carriers were of self-reported Black ethnicity. No transcript, per-variant carrier count, denominator for Black participants, or individual phenotype is given for them. They behave like ancestry-enriched polymorphisms reported with population frequencies, so no records were created. Phenotype analyses are gene-level collapsed burden and association tests based on ICD-10 and Read codes, not individual-level case data. COL4A1 carrier status was associated with phenotypes-of-interest (OR 1.29, p=0.006), driven by cataract, migraine and stroke. Proportions of carriers with any phenotype-of-interest in hospital and death records: COL4A1 20% (95/481), COL4A2 4% (15/336). If a curator obtains the eTables, per-variant records could be built with n_tested=199,313 and n_families=0.

variants.phenotype_details: Paediatric cataract, central posterior cortical with dots; family with inherited paediatric cataract; variant segregates with disease. No extra-ocular features reported for this family.

A known COL4A1 p.(Gly720Asp) change was determined to be disease-causing in family CRCH38 (figure 1D).
Classification of the COL4A1 p.(Gly720Asp) change as likely pathogenic, in family CRCH38, was greatly assisted by its previous observation in a family with a congenital cataract phenotype.
Genome sequencing was performed on the DNA of an affected individual (proband) from each of 37 families with European ancestry.
variants.notes: Variant previously described (Sibon et al) in a different family; this Australian family CRCH38 is new. Segregation marked 'Yes' but pedigree details (number of affected carriers, parental status) are in figure only, not provided; direct parental carrier status not stated in text, so inheritance left unknown although family is described as inherited cataract with segregation. MIR184 n.52T>C also found in this family, deemed benign/VUS.

extraction.extraction_notes: Gene-panel genome sequencing study of 37 Australian families with paediatric cataract; only one COL4A1 variant reported. Pedigree (figure 1D) and supplementary tables S1-S4 not provided, so number of carriers in CRCH38 unknown.

Systematic review of published monogenic cSVD cases (390 COL4A1 and 41 COL4A2 carriers aggregated from prior literature). No new individuals are reported, and no specific variants are listed in the provided text. Per-variant data may be in Supplementary Data S1/Tables S1-S4, which were not provided. Only aggregate phenotype frequencies are given.

Review of genotype-phenotype correlations for COL4A3, COL4A4 and COL4A5 in Alport syndrome. COL4A1 and COL4A2 are mentioned only in the general description of collagen IV network structure. No COL4A1 or COL4A2 variants are reported in any individual. The specific variants discussed (COL4A5 p.Gly624Asp, COL4A3 p.Leu1474Pro) are in other genes and are cited from prior literature and databases.

variants.phenotype_details: Found in the male partner of couple 14 with unexplained recurrent spontaneous abortion (3 miscarriages at 7, 8 and 10 weeks); no carrier phenotype reported beyond the couple's pregnancy losses.
evidence_quotes: Herein, mutations of COL4A2 (c.4808 A>C; p.H1603P) were found in URSA patients, supporting the role of COL4A2 in placentation.
variants.notes: WES of 30 URSA couples (60 individuals; plus 9 control couples). Table 1 places the variant in the male partner of couple 14; the text says it came 'from mother and/or father'. Only in silico predictions (CADD 24.8, SIFT deleterious, PolyPhen probably damaging, located in C4/NC1 domain) and Sanger validation. Table 2 lists inheritance mode as 'AD' (gene-level annotation, not segregation). Phenotype is couple-level recurrent miscarriage, not a classical COL4A2 phenotype.

variants.phenotype_details: Carried by partners in URSA couples 11 (female), 13 (likely male), 19 (male) and 20 (female); couples had 2-4 miscarriages.
variants.notes: Table 1 only; column alignment of the rendered table is ambiguous (row 13 assignment to male partner uncertain). Not among the 22 variants retained as strongly associated with URSA in Table 2. Possibly a recurrent/common variant in this population; no allele frequency given.

variants.phenotype_details: Carried by partners in URSA couples 13, 16, 20, 22 (male partners) and 29 (female partner); couples had 2-5 miscarriages.
variants.notes: Table 1 only; column alignment ambiguous. Recurrence in 5 of 60 individuals suggests a common polymorphism; not retained in Table 2 of strongly associated variants.

variants.phenotype_details: Female partner of URSA couple 21 (2 miscarriages at 8 and 12 weeks).
evidence_quotes: After mutation filtering, a total of 971 maternal and 954 paternal pathogenic or possible pathogenic variants were identified (Table 1).
variants.notes: Table 1 only; not retained among the 22 strongly associated variants in Table 2.

extraction.extraction_notes: Whole-exome sequencing of 30 couples with unexplained recurrent spontaneous abortion (60 individuals) plus 9 control couples. Only COL4A2 p.H1603P was highlighted as a strongly associated candidate (Table 2, Sanger-validated, in silico predictions only). Other COL4A2 variants (P443R, K701R, M1419T) appear only in Table 1 among preliminary-filtered variants; the rendered Table 1 columns are misaligned so assignment to female/male partner is uncertain. Phenotype is recurrent pregnancy loss at couple level, not a classic COL4A1/COL4A2 disorder; no cerebrovascular, renal, ocular or muscle phenotypes reported. No inheritance/segregation testing; 'AD' in Table 2 is a gene annotation. No COL4A1 variants reported.

Input contained only the title and an empty 'Footnotes' section; no abstract, body text, tables or supplementary data were provided. The title (familial intracranial aneurysm, whole-exome and mitochondrial DNA sequencing; likely an editorial/commentary) does not indicate any specific COL4A1/COL4A2 variants in specific individuals. Nothing extractable; full text should be checked by a curator if relevant.

variants.phenotype_details: Dystonia; age at WES 25 years, latency from symptom onset 2 years; no family history; no diagnosis assigned.
variants.reported_classification: V (VUS) for both finding and interpretation
evidence_quotes: 7 | | | | | | + | 25 | 2 | V | V | COL4A1 p.(Glu1539Gly) | . | NO | Heterozygous | NO
Of the 54 patients in which WES was obtained,14 (25.9%) presented pathogenic variants and 18 (33.3%) VUS.
variants.notes: Table-only data. No c. notation or transcript given. 'V' in the table appears to denote VUS. Heterozygous, no family history; parental testing not described for this patient (TRIO done in 7 of 32 patients with findings, cases not all specified), so inheritance unknown. Patient found by WES in a movement-disorders clinic cohort (54 WES of 2948 clinic patients); no family studied. Non-glycine missense outside typical Gly-X-Y pattern; no cerebrovascular/imaging findings reported.

extraction.extraction_notes: Single COL4A1 variant reported in Table 1 (patient 7) of a 54-patient WES movement-disorder series. Denominator: 54 patients sequenced (out of 2948 clinic patients). No COL4A2 variants. Note that the Supplementary Table 1 patient numbering is inconsistent with Table 1 numbering but does not involve the COL4A1 patient.

This case report describes a single autosomal-dominant Alport syndrome family carrying a novel heterozygous COL4A3 variant (c.G3566A, p.G1189E). The paper reports no COL4A1 or COL4A2 variants in any individual. COL4A1 and COL4A2 appear only in general background discussion of type IV collagen genes, so no records were created.

This is a whole-genome sequencing study of 35 familial pancreatic cancer patients from 27 Danish families. Table 2 lists COL4A2 (together with COL4A2-AS2, NM_001846.3) as harbouring 3 private heterozygous protein-truncating variants (PTVs). The text says these genes, other than RICTOR, carry PTVs each observed in only one patient. Supplementary Table S2 adds only gene-level rows: 'COL4A2 | COL4A2-AS2; chr13; first PTV position 111109129 (hg19); 3 PTVs' and a separate 'COL4A2; chr13; 111158678; 1 PTV'. The per-variant annotation with HGVS nomenclature, patient IDs and consequence types is in Table S3, which was not provided. Individual COL4A2 variants therefore cannot be identified, apart from one genomic start position, or attributed to specific patients. No COL4A1/COL4A2-related phenotype is reported; the only phenotype is pancreatic adenocarcinoma, and no cerebrovascular, renal, ocular or muscle findings are described. COL4A2 was not among the nominally associated genes in the ProxECAT analysis (Table S4). The authors note that COL4A2 also appeared among PTV genes in their earlier study of first-degree relatives (Tan et al.). For these reasons no variant records were created. A curator with access to Table S3 could extract the 3–4 COL4A2 PTVs found among n_tested=35, each in a single unrelated patient, with inheritance unknown.

This paper reports four novel COL4A5 variants (c.1424-4C>G, c.2777G>T p.(Gly926Val), c.4529-2A>T, c.1552G>A p.(Gly518Arg)) in three Chinese X-linked Alport syndrome families. It reports no COL4A1 or COL4A2 variants. COL4A1/COL4A2 appear only in a general discussion of type IV collagen chain structure. No records were created.

variants.phenotype_details: Found in the Newfoundland family segregating autosomal dominant progressive bilateral sensorineural hearing loss; the hearing loss is attributed by the authors to ATP11A, and this COL4A1 variant was excluded from the disease interval by recombination in unaffected relatives. No COL4A1-type (cerebrovascular, renal, ocular, muscle) phenotype reported.
variants.functional_evidence: RT-PCR of patient B-cell RNA (carriers III-1, III-5, III-7) showed a single normal ~280 bp amplicon identical to controls, indicating no splicing disruption, consistent with in silico predictions.
evidence_quotes: Two candidate splicing variants, one novel: ATP11A (NC_000013.11:chr13:113534963G>A; ENST00000415301.1:ATP11A-203:c.*11G>A; Fig. 4a) and one rare: COL4A1 (NC_000013.11:g.110174539dupT; NG_011544.2:g.137617dup; NM_001845.6:c.3326-7dupT; Fig. 4b) were both absent in NL population controls.
In silico tools predict that COL4A1 c.3326-7dupT does not disrupt splicing, which we confirmed by RNA analysis (Fig. 4c).

Furthermore, during the transcriptional analysis, we recruited two unaffected family members (PID III-4 and V-2) that harbored key cross over events and reduced the disease interval to 769 kb, excluding the COL4A1 c.3326-7dupT (Fig. 1).
c RT-PCR analysis of the COL4A1 c.3326-7dupT variant revealed a single ~ 280 bp amplicon in unaffecteds (controls) and COL4A1 c.3326-7dupT carriers (PID III-1, III-5, and III-7).
variants.notes: Incidental positional candidate in a hearing-loss linkage study; authors excluded it as the cause (recombination) and showed normal splicing. Named carriers include III-1, III-5 and III-7 (III-5 is the proband's father), but total carrier count and the proband's own genotype are not explicitly stated, so inheritance recorded as unknown and total carriers null. Supplementary Table S3 lists it as rs532261610, MAF 0.37%, Impact Medium. 'Other' phenotype reflects hearing loss in the family, not attributed to COL4A1.

extraction.extraction_notes: Paper is about ATP11A in autosomal dominant non-syndromic hearing loss. The only COL4A1/COL4A2 variant reported in individuals is COL4A1 c.3326-7dupT, a rare intronic positional candidate in the Newfoundland family that was excluded by recombination and showed no splicing effect. Supplementary Table S3 also lists COL4A1 c.84+17003G>A (rs187157903, MAF 0.60%) among rare variants in the linked interval with no further discussion; not extracted as it was not analyzed or attributed to any individual phenotype.

Cohort of 120 idiopathic cerebral palsy families (118 trios, 2 quartets) studied by WES/WGS/CMA. The body text says de novo COL4A1 mutations were found in two unrelated CP patients, CP_008_1 and CP_033_1. Both had spastic CP, epilepsy and severe intellectual disability, and CP_008_1 also had severe microcephaly and congenital blindness. Quoted: 'Another recurrent gene in this cohort was COL4A1 (OMIM: 120130), in which we identified DNMs in two CP patients (CP_008_1 and CP_033_1).' The specific variant nomenclature (c./p.) is given only in Supplementary Tables 3 and 4, which were not provided. For that reason no variant-level records were created, since as_written and HGVS could not be filled. Parental testing was trio-based, with de novo defined as absent in both parents and parentage confirmed by PLINK. A curator with access to Supplementary Tables 3/4 should add two COL4A1 records: n_tested=120, n_probands=1 each, inh_de_novo_confirmed likely. The phenotype systems would likely be other (CP, epilepsy, ID, microcephaly) plus possibly ocular for the congenital blindness in CP_008_1; COL4A1-specific neuroimaging is not described. The figure transcription concerns TYW1 only.

Case report of a single patient with ADPKD (two PKD1 missense variants), compound heterozygous SLC12A3 variants (Gitelman syndrome) and 47,XXY Klinefelter karyotype. No COL4A1 or COL4A2 variants are reported in this patient. COL4A1 is mentioned only in passing in the Discussion, citing a prior report of 'dual sequence variants in PKD2 and COL4A1', with no new individuals or specific variant given. The NGS panel (380 kidney genes) may have included COL4A1/COL4A2, but no variants in them were reported.

variants.phenotype_details: Male, 21.01 years at enrollment; non-cryptogenic CP (perinatal stroke as risk factor); spastic quadriplegic CP, dystonia, epilepsy, ID, cortical visual impairment; cystic encephalomalacia in right parietal region likely prior right PCA territory infarct; cerebellar calcification versus prior cerebellar hemorrhage; cerebral and cerebellar atrophy, small brainstem, thin corpus callosum; posterior embryotoxon; optic pathway hypoplasia or atrophy; patent ductus arteriosus, hypoplastic isthmus of aortic arch, bicuspid aortic valve; hypospadias, cryptorchidism, inguinal hernia; intrauterine growth restriction.
evidence_quotes: 21 | Trio | 21.01 | M | Non‐cryptogenic | spastic quadriplegic | COL4A1 | NM_001845.4:c.443G > A (p.Gly148Glu) | De novo | Heterozygous | Yes | Likely pathogenic

For the individual with the COL4A1 variant, in addition to spastic quadriplegic CP, epilepsy, ID, previous infarct, cerebellar hemorrhage, and cerebral atrophy, there were extra‐neurological symptoms concerning for a genetic syndrome, including posterior embryotoxon, optic pathway hypoplasia, patent ductus arteriosus, bicuspid aortic valve, hypospadias, and cryptorchidism, consistent with COL4A1‐related disorder (OMIM #175780).
We included 50 probands in this analysis (20 females, 30 males).
variants.notes: Trio WES with clinical confirmation by GeneDx; called de novo in trio analysis (both parents sequenced); parentage not discussed. Additional phenotype details from supplementary Table S1.

Case report of a man with X-linked Alport syndrome and kidney cysts. The only variant reported is COL4A5 c.358G>A (p.Gly120Ser), which is outside the scope of this database (COL4A1/COL4A2 only). Case report of a Japanese mother and son with familial retinal arteriolar tortuosity (FRAT). Both underwent NGS with the Ion AmpliSeq Inherited Disease Panel (328 genes including COL4A1), and the authors state that no pathogenic variants were found, including in COL4A1. No specific COL4A1 or COL4A2 variant is reported in any individual. COL4A1 is mentioned only in the context of prior literature (e.g., Zenteno et al.). The authors note that a COL4A1 variant missed by the panel (coverage, mosaicism, CNV, regulatory regions) cannot be excluded. The proband had transient mild CK elevation and renal pelvic dilatation, but no variant was identified.

COL4A1 is mentioned only as a gene on the extended PKD panel (8 of 18 tested patients received the extended panel). All reported diagnostic findings were in PKD1 (7 truncating, 3 non-truncating, 5 VUS missense) and PKD2 (1). The remaining 2 patients were negative. No COL4A1 or COL4A2 variants were reported. Specific variants are listed in Supplementary Table 1, which was not provided, but the body text accounts for all 18 results without any COL4A1/COL4A2 finding.

variants.phenotype_details: Found in two unrelated participants of a population-based sample from the Ivanovo region (aged 25-64). No phenotype was reported for these carriers. evidence_quotes: The full set of 242 targeted genes also contained 69 novel PTVs in 48 genes (Table 4 and Supplementary Table 3), all being singletons, except for the two doubleton cases: the frameshift variant ENSP00000347507.3:p.Lys1173ArgfsTer41 in the ACMG59 gene MYH7 and the stop gain variant ENSP00000364979.4:p.Arg1063Ter in the non-ACMG gene COL4A1.

The most PTV-depleted gene in this list is the collagen type IV alpha 1 chain COL4A1 with only six PTVs observed in gnomAD. The novel protein-truncating variant Arg1063Ter in this gene is observed in two participants.
We also checked 17 carriers of 18 novel truncating variants in non-ACMG59 genes and did not discover any remarkable genotype–phenotype associations.

Supplementary Table 1 also lists one novel PTV in COL4A2 (1 carrier), plus COL4A1/COL4A2 ClinVar VUS and novel missense counts. The specific identities of these variants are in Supplementary Table 3, which was not included (the supplementary file was truncated: 2 of 4 sheets missing), so no COL4A2 record was created. extraction.extraction_notes: Whole-genome sequencing of 150 unselected singleton CP cases from the Australian CP Biobank. Five COL4A1/COL4A2 P/LP variants were reported in Table 1. Individual clinical and imaging details are in Supplementary Table 1, which was not provided, so the phenotype is recorded only as CP ('other'). The text says COL4A2 accounted for three cases, but one passage lists 'COL4A1 and COL4A2 (two individuals each)' among missense variants plus a COL4A2 LoF/splice; this is consistent with 5 total. The Discussion mentions 7 total COL4A1/2 individuals across prior Biobank studies (n=604 tested for COL4A1, 333 for COL4A2); only the 5 new from this study are extracted. The PubTator-flagged COL4A4 variant was excluded.

This is a WGS study of 61 unaffected first-degree relatives of familial pancreatic cancer patients from 27 Danish families. COL4A2 appears only as a gene-level hit in a ProxECAT rare-variant burden test against gnomAD controls (p=1.37e-06, FDR 2.64e-04). It also appears in a core matrisome pathway enrichment. The text mentions one rare COL4A2 missense variant (13:111155578, Ref/Alt G/A, hg19) and one unspecified splice region variant. These are not attributed to specific individuals in the provided text, and no carrier count, phenotype or HGVS nomenclature is given. Per-variant details are said to be in Supplementary Table S5, which was not provided. The carriers are unaffected relatives studied for cancer risk, not individuals with a COL4A1/COL4A2-related disease. Because the variant is reported as part of a gene-burden association analysis rather than as a candidate cause in specific affected individuals, no variant record was created.

This paper is a NOTCH3 study of CADASIL patients (54 probands, 38 with NOTCH3 variants). COL4A1 and COL4A2 appear only as genes screened by targeted NGS in patients carrying NOTCH3 variants outside the EGFr region. The authors report that no potential pathogenic mutation was identified in them (data unpublished). The paper reports no specific COL4A1 or COL4A2 variants in any individual.

The input is labelled full text, but only the title, the abstract and a data-availability statement were provided. The body text was not supplied. The abstract reports a Japanese family with a novel COL4A1 variant, including a patient with recurrent epistaxis and glioblastoma. The variant is not named anywhere in the provided text: no c. or p. notation and no transcript. The number of carriers, the inheritance and the phenotypes of other family members are also not given. No variant record was created because no variant designation is available to extract. The paper does likely contain variant-level data, so a curator should retrieve the full article and the HGV Database entry (10.6084/m9.figshare.hgv.3006) to get the variant and the family details.

variants.phenotype_details: 23-year-old male; neonatal mild hypotonia, postaxial polydactyly, mild motor delay, drug-resistant epilepsy from age 3, mild leukoencephalopathy on MRI at age 3; at age 23 acute right basal ganglia haemorrhage with left hemiparesis and dysarthria, lacunar subacute ischaemic lesions, progressive subcortical leukoencephalopathy, microbleeds and left superficial hemosiderosis; moderate intellectual disability, mitral prolapse, mild LVH; hyperhomocysteinaemia with heterozygous MTHFR C677T and LAC positivity. Authors interpret lesions as compatible with cerebral vasculitis.
evidence_quotes: The results confirmed the presence of de-novo 13q22-q34 duplication (41.7 Mb, 72,365,975-114,077,122x3) including GPC5 (OMIM 602446) and GPC6 (OMIM 604404), COL4A1 (OMIM 120130) and COL4A2 (OMIM 120090), PROZ (OMIM 176895), GAS6 (OMIM 600441), GPR180 (OMIM 607787), STK24 (OMIM 604984), TNFSF13B (OMIM 603969) and NALCL (OMIM 611549) genes.
Several years later, at the age of 23, he abruptly presented with drop attack, dysarthria, and left hemiparesis.

Subcortical leukoencephalopathy was also visible with lacunar subacute ischemic lesions in the left frontal-orbital subcortical area and bilaterally in the white matter at the level of the corona radiata (Figure 1a–c).
The Susceptibility weighted imaging (SWI) sequence also highlighted the presence of some microbleeds and left superficial hemosiderosis in the cerebral sulci at the brain convexity (Figure 2d).

Authors do not discuss COL4A1/COL4A2 as causal; they attribute phenotype to vasculitis, PROZ/GAS6/TNFSF13B, hyperhomocysteinaemia and LAC. Same CNV recorded under COL4A2.

evidence_quotes: The Affymetrix CytoScanHD SNP‐array showed an apparently de novo intragenic duplication of >99 kb (156 probes), containing exon 5–28 of the COL4A2‐gene (coordinates of estimated minimally duplicated region: chr13: 111,030,406–111,129,816 bp [build GRCh37]).
This duplication was not present in leucocyte DNA of the parents.

The brain MRI, performed at day three showed diffuse hemorrhagic lesions throughout both hemispheres, predominantly in the periventricular white matter, but also in the basal ganglia, and microbleeds in the mesencephalon and cerebellum (Figure 1g–j).
The serum creatine kinase was repeatedly elevated (±1,257 U/L, as had been reported in COL4A1 mutations before).
On follow‐up she also developed subcutaneous vascular malformations, myoclonic epilepsy, and cerebral palsy.

Exome/genome sequencing study of 384 UK SCAD survivors plus 92 validation cases, with 13,722 UK Biobank controls. COL4A2 appears only as a gene prioritized from the collapsing analysis (manual review and mantis-ml) for future validation. No specific COL4A1 or COL4A2 variant is reported in any individual in the provided text. Collapsing-analysis details (Table VIII and Tables VI/VII in the Data Supplement) were referenced but not provided, and may list qualifying variants. The pathogenic and likely pathogenic variants reported involve PKD1, COL3A1, SMAD3, TGFB2, LOX, MYLK and YY1AP1, not COL4A1 or COL4A2.

Alport syndrome podocyte study. The three patients carry variants only in COL4A3 (c.1937dup, c.4803del) and COL4A5 (c.2777del, c.2546G>A), not in COL4A1 or COL4A2. The paper mentions COL4A1/COL4A2 only as transcripts measured by RT-qPCR, which were increased in AS patient 1 podocytes. No COL4A1/COL4A2 variants are reported in any individual.

This is a keratoconus twin family study using WES, RNA-seq, qRT-PCR and western blot. No COL4A1 or COL4A2 sequence variants were reported in any individual. COL4A1 and COL4A2 appear only as differentially expressed (downregulated) genes in the proband's corneal fibroblasts (Table S3, qRT-PCR, Collagen IV western blot). The only type IV collagen variant reported is in COL4A3 (NM_000091.4:c.4607T>C, p.Ile1536Thr; maternal; did not cosegregate). COL4A3 is outside the scope of this database, so no record was created for it.

Whole-exome sequencing study of 21 cases (20 unrelated families; C01 and C09 are brothers) with corneal neuralgia after LASIK/PRK. The text states that low-frequency (AF<0.05) COL4A2 variants were found in 4 cases (C08, C09, C18, C21), and that C21 carried a homozygous COL4A2 missense variant. The specific COL4A2 variants are listed only in Table 3. Only the caption of Table 3 was provided, with no rows, and the supplementary tables (http://links.lww.com/PR9/A65) were not provided. As a result, no variant names, HGVS notation or zygosity per case (apart from the homozygous call in C21) could be extracted, and no records were created. These are low-frequency candidate variants in a neuropathic pain cohort and are not linked by the authors to any COL4A-typical phenotype; no cerebrovascular, renal or other COL4A2-associated phenotypes were reported. The authors only mention in passing that COL4A1/2 have been linked to migraine. A curator with access to Table 3 should check whether the COL4A2 rows (C08, C09, C18, C21; denominator 21 sequenced) merit records.

variants.phenotype_details: 7-year-old girl with an 11.56 Mb 13q33.1-q34 deletion (about 30 OMIM genes, including COL4A1 and COL4A2). Features: facial dysmorphism, hypotonia, psychomotor developmental delay, intellectual disability, epilepsy (first grand mal seizure at 6 years), muscular VSD and PDA that resolved spontaneously, failed hearing screening/BAEP, reduced anogenital distance, congenital left hip dislocation, persistent microscopic hematuria, left renal hypoplasia with hydronephrosis, thin left renal artery, and grade I left vesicoureteral reflux. No brain imaging and no ophthalmological findings were reported.
evidence_quotes: Compared with the Database of Genomic Variants (DGV), a de novo 11.56 Mb deletion ranging from 13q33.1 to 13q34 (Chr13:103542220–115,106,996) was found.

This study reports a patient with a de novo 11.56 Mb deletion ranging from 13q33.1 to 13q34 (Chr13:103542220–115,106,996) which is a chromosome region containing about 30 OMIM genes, including eight OMIM morbid genes: SLC10A2, LIG4, COL4A1, COL4A2, ING1, F7, F10 and GRK1.

The patient suffered from a reduced anogenital distance, hematuria and left renal hypoplasia in addition to the common clinical features of mental retardation, facial abnormalities, and congenital heart diseases.
We postulated that the underlying renal abnormality associated with 13q deletion might be the cause of hematuria.
variants.notes: This is a large contiguous-gene deletion (11.56 Mb, about 30 OMIM genes), not an intragenic COL4A1 variant. The same CNV is recorded again under COL4A2. The genome build is not stated. 'De novo' is stated, but no parental testing is described. The authors do not attribute the renal or other phenotypes specifically to COL4A1; the hematuria is attributed to the underlying renal abnormality.

extraction.extraction_notes: Paper also reports COL4A4 and COL4A5 variants (not extracted, out of scope). Two additional NMD-ADPKD patients with HANAC-causing COL4A1 mutations were previously reported in separate case reports; their variants are not specified here and they were not extracted. Supplementary methods/tables referenced (S1, S3, S17, S18) were not provided. No transcripts stated for any variant.

variants.phenotype_details: Heterozygous carrier was a participant in the minimal-SVD group (lowest quartile of WMH burden, no MRI brain infarcts) of a population-based cohort aged 65+; no affected phenotype reported. The authors note the MRI protocol lacked gradient echo imaging, so microbleeds or haemorrhages could not be detected.
evidence_quotes: We also observed two minimal-SVD participants carrying a heterozygote genotype at one glycine residue altering missense variant in COL4A1 [NM_001845.4 (COL4A1): c.3158G > A (p.Gly1053Asp), participant level depth coverage = 125× and Phred scaled genotype quality = 99], and one nonsense (stop gained) variant in COL4A2 [NM_001846.2 (COL4A2) c.3766C > T (p.Arg1256Ter), participant level depth coverage = 77× and Phred scaled genotype quality = 99].

Intriguingly we observed two missense variants in COL4A1 and COL4A2 in 3C-Dijon participants with minimal SVD, with typical characteristics of SVD causing mutations, although they have not been described previously in SVD families.
variants.notes: The variant was found by WES screening of 512 extreme-SVD participants (259 extensive, 253 minimal) from the 3C-Dijon cohort. The carrier had minimal SVD, which suggests low penetrance or undetected haemorrhagic features. The call was not Sanger-validated. No family or parental data are given.

variants.phenotype_details: Heterozygous carrier was a participant in the minimal-SVD group (lowest quartile of WMH burden, no MRI brain infarcts) of a population-based cohort aged 65+; no affected phenotype reported.
evidence_quotes: We also observed two minimal-SVD participants carrying a heterozygote genotype at one glycine residue altering missense variant in COL4A1 [NM_001845.4 (COL4A1): c.3158G > A (p.Gly1053Asp), participant level depth coverage = 125× and Phred scaled genotype quality = 99], and one nonsense (stop gained) variant in COL4A2 [NM_001846.2 (COL4A2) c.3766C > T (p.Arg1256Ter), participant level depth coverage = 77× and Phred scaled genotype quality = 99].

Intriguingly we observed two missense variants in COL4A1 and COL4A2 in 3C-Dijon participants with minimal SVD, with typical characteristics of SVD causing mutations, although they have not been described previously in SVD families.
variants.notes: The discussion loosely calls both variants 'missense', but the results section describes this one as a nonsense (stop gained) variant. It was found by WES screening of 512 extreme-SVD participants and was not Sanger-validated. No family or parental data are given.

extraction.extraction_notes: The paper is an extreme-phenotype WES association study in the 3C-Dijon cohort (n=512 sequenced). The COL4A1/COL4A2 association SNP rs2275842 (Table 2) and gene-based SKAT-O results (Table 3) were excluded as association data. The COL4A2 GWAS intronic SNPs mentioned in the discussion were also excluded. Other protein-modifying COL4A1/COL4A2 variants are shown in Supplementary Figs 3-4, which were not provided. Only the two individually described carriers were extracted.

variants.phenotype_details: Patient 26, aged 17 at last follow-up: moderate learning difficulties, left hemiparesis, no epilepsy, normal EEG; MRI showed bilateral fronto-parietal polymicrogyria and schizencephaly, periventricular nodular heterotopia and white matter loss. Polyhydramnios prompted surgical delivery.
evidence_quotes: In one family, the parents tested negative, but both the proband (no. 26) and his sister (not included in the study) carried the same mutation; parental mosaicism is assumed but not proven.
Patient 26 (COL4A1 p. G1169S), aged 17 at last follow-up, had moderate learning difficulties and left hemiparesis.
variants.notes: Both parents tested negative but an affected sister also carries the variant; the authors assume parental mosaicism, so the variant is neither a confirmed de novo nor shown inherited. It is coded inh_unknown. The sister's phenotype is not described. The transcript is stated generally for COL4A1 in the paper.

variants.phenotype_details: Patient 28, aged 16: severe language impairment with dysarthria, left spastic hemiparesis, right fronto-parietal schizencephaly, no seizures. Also agenesis of the right kidney, bilateral ptosis, left eyelid hemangioma, right cataract and bilateral retinal atrophy.
evidence_quotes: Patient 28 (COL4A1 p.G1207V), aged 16 years at last observation, had severe language impairment with dysarthria, language automatism, and left spastic hemiparesis.
He had agenesis of the right kidney and a severe ocular dysmorphism with bilateral ptosis, hemangioma of the left superior eyelid, right cataract, and bilateral retinal atrophy.
variants.notes: Inheritance for patient 28 is not given in the main text; it may be in a Dryad table that was not provided. Renal agenesis is listed under other rather than renal_hanac.

variants.phenotype_details: Patient 34: focal epilepsy with onset at 5 years, presenting as status epilepticus; behavioral problems; normal neurologic examination; nonspecific white matter lesions and an arachnoid cyst on MRI.
evidence_quotes: The 5 mutations in the C-terminal domain were all missense and were all associated with a severe syndromic picture, except the variant p.C1551Y, found in patient 34, with focal epilepsy and behavioral problems, normal neurologic examination, nonspecific white matter lesions, and an arachnoid cyst on MRI.
Status epilepticus was the presenting symptom in 4 patients (nos. 3, 19a, 23a, and 34).
variants.notes: Located in the C-terminal (NC1) region. Inheritance is not stated in the main text.

variants.phenotype_details: Patient 8 (adult): developmental delay, moderate cognitive impairment, autism, normal neurologic examination; drug-resistant focal seizures from 11 years; extensive supratentorial white matter loss and abnormalities, initially attributed to perinatal infection. Patient 9: drug-resistant focal seizures from 10 months, microcephaly, hypotonia at birth; periventricular white matter loss, thin corpus callosum and cerebellar atrophy.
evidence_quotes: The COL4A1 p. G601S variant is newly described, identified in 2 new patients (nos. 8 and 9).
Patient 9 had onset of focal drug-resistant seizures at age 10 months; neurologic examination showed microcephaly and hypotonia at birth.
variants.notes: Patients 8 and 9 are assumed unrelated because they have separate case numbers; the paper does not state their relationship. Inheritance is not given in the main text.

variants.phenotype_details: Patient 24, died at 6 years: bilateral porencephaly, intractable epilepsy (West syndrome at 6 months, treated with corpus callosotomy then functional hemispherectomy), profound global developmental delay, microphthalmia, congenital cataracts. Also severe intrauterine growth retardation and microcephaly.
evidence_quotes: Among the new patients, we found a similar phenotype in a child who died at 6 years of age (no. 24) and had bilateral porencephaly, intractable epilepsy, profound global developmental delay, microphthalmia, and congenital cataracts.
Patient 24, diagnosed with West syndrome at 6 months, underwent corpus callosotomy at 20 months.
variants.notes: The variant was previously reported de novo in an unrelated patient; only the new patient (no. 24) is counted here. Inheritance for patient 24 is not stated.

variants.phenotype_details: 3-year-old girl: surgical delivery for suspected prenatal hydrocephalus; microcephaly, severe cognitive impairment, drug-resistant epileptic spasms. Her paternal grandmother died of a ruptured cerebral aneurysm.
evidence_quotes: In our series of new cases, the same mutation was found de novo in an affected 3-year-old girl.
The child developed microcephaly, severe cognitive impairment, and drug-resistant epileptic spasms.
variants.notes: Called de novo, but parental testing is not described in the text, so it is coded de_novo_assumed. The case number is not given; she may be patient 32 (suspected hydrocephalus), but that is not stated. The earlier published paternally inherited family is not counted.

variants.phenotype_details: Italian family (cases 33a–33e) with very varied phenotypes. 33b and 33d have epilepsy; 33d is an adult with epilepsy onset at 6 years and a normal neurologic examination. 33a has periventricular leukoencephalopathy. 33c had acute germinal matrix hemorrhage on fetal MRI and extensive leukoencephalopathy at 8 days. 33c and 33e are described as asymptomatic carriers.
evidence_quotes: Five members carried mutation COL4A1 p. G1369R and presented with very varied clinical phenotypes.
(C) Acute germinal matrix hemorrhage on fetal brain MRI (arrows) and consequent extensive leukoencephalopathy on postnatal brain MRI (*) at 8 days of life (patient 33/c).
The pedigree in figure 4 also highlights that asymptomatic carriers (nos. 33/c and 33/e) can precede severe phenotypes.
variants.notes: Multigenerational family counted as one proband. The proband is not explicitly identified; inheritance is inferred from carriers spanning generations. The family is described as from Italy (5 from the same family). 33/c is called an asymptomatic carrier yet has fetal hemorrhage on figure legend, which is inconsistent.

extraction.extraction_notes: Most variant-level data (tables 1, 2, 3a/b and figure e-1 on Dryad, doi.org/10.5061/dryad.gj58t0v) were not provided, so only variants named in the main text with new patients are extracted. The cohort has 46 new patients, 44 after exclusions; 44 is used as n_tested. The 55 previously published patients are a literature review and are not counted. p.G720D and p.G749S are listed among recurrent mutations, but the text describes only previously reported families for them. It is ambiguous whether the p.G749S patient with prenatal hemorrhage is new, so neither variant has a record. p.G562E is mentioned from a published case only. Patients 1 and 2 carry mutations in the transcription initiation region but their variants are not named in the text. The 3 new COL4A2 mutations are not named in the main text. Immunohistochemistry on patient 1's resected tissue is reported, but that patient's variant is not named.

The paper is a cohort of 50 children with encephalopathy and intracranial calcification, screened with a 59-gene NGS panel that included COL4A1 and COL4A2. The text states that two patients had a clinical and radiological picture suggesting a collagen IV-related disorder, and that one of them was genetically confirmed. Fig. 2 describes this patient as having COL4A1-related leukoencephalopathy: ex vacuo enlarged lateral ventricles, lacunar infarctions in the right basal ganglia, small subependymal and subcortical white matter calcification, and right cerebellar hemisphere hypoplasia. The specific COL4A1 variant, the patient number and the inheritance are reported only in Table 2. Only Table 2's caption was rendered in the provided text; its rows were not. As a result, no variant-level record could be created without guessing the variant. A curator should consult Table 2 of the original article to retrieve the COL4A1 variant (n_tested = 50) and its segregation data. The other patient suspected of a collagen IV disorder had no pathogenic COL4A1/COL4A2 mutation.

This case report describes missense variants in COL4A5 (c.C3940>T, p.P1314S) and COL4A6 (c.C3538>T, p.P1180S) in a family with cerebrovascular fibromuscular dysplasia. The paper reports no COL4A1 or COL4A2 variants in any individual. COL4A1/COL4A2 are mentioned only in passing, in the context of angiopathy literature. No records were extracted.

variants.phenotype_details: Proband PP50cat (Cambodia, male): pediatric cataract, age at diagnosis unknown; family with AD cataract. The COL4A1 variant did not segregate with cataract; a MIP p.(Arg33Cys) variant segregating in the family was considered causal.
evidence_quotes: AD | COL4A1 | chr13:110864795 | c.356C>G | p.(Pro119Arg) | 5.27 | No | 0 | 0 | ProbD | T | US

Variants were also detected in COL4A1 and NSDHL (Table 1), but did not segregate with cataract status in other family members, thus the MIP variant is the most likely cause of the disease in this family.
variants.notes: Variant did not segregate with cataract in the family; authors attribute disease to MIP variant. Transcript taken from supplementary gene list (Table S1). Ocular phenotype listed because carrier proband has cataract, but authors consider variant non-causal. Absent from ExAC/gnomAD.

variants.phenotype_details: Proband SR12cat (Cambodia, male): pediatric cataract, age at diagnosis unknown; multiplex family. Variant did not segregate with disease.
evidence_quotes: SR12cat had variants in two genes, TDRD7 and COL4A1. Both variants are also reported in ExAC at low frequencies and neither segregated with the disease in the family (Figure 2g).
variants.notes: Variant did not segregate with cataract; authors state it is unlikely to be causal. Present in ExAC/gnomAD at low frequency. Transcript from supplementary Table S1.

extraction.extraction_notes: 51-gene cataract panel in 33 probands from Bhutan, Cambodia and Sri Lanka. Two rare COL4A1 missense variants reported, both non-segregating and judged not causal by authors (ACMG 'US'). Variants in other genes not extracted. Pedigree details (Figure 2) not provided as text; number of tested relatives/carriers not stated.

variants.phenotype_details: Sound-color (auditory-visual) synesthesia segregating across three or more generations in family 11. Participants were selected to have no neurological, ophthalmological or psychiatric disorder; no typical COL4A1 phenotypes are reported.
variants.reported_classification: Rare variant segregating with sound-color synesthesia; candidate gene (axonogenesis)
variants.prior_report_reason: The paper says the families were originally included in a 2009 microsatellite linkage study of 43 auditory-visual synesthesia families. That study did not report this variant.
evidence_quotes: We identified rare genetic variants that fully cosegregate with synesthesia in each family, uncovering 37 genes of interest.
Furthermore, COL4A1 (family 11) encodes an alpha subunit of type IV collagen, which binds αβ integrin heterodimers to promote axonal growth and branching.
For each family, we obtained exome sequences from four or five verified synesthetes across three generations plus at least one nonsynesthetic family member.
variants.notes: The variant is given only as a genomic position (likely GRCh37) with no c./p. notation, so the substituted residue is unknown; missense_other is assigned provisionally and it may involve a glycine. The variant is one of 37 segregating variants in three families and was not singled out as causal. The phenotype is a nonpathological trait (synesthesia), not a COL4A1 disease. Inheritance is listed as inherited because the variant cosegregates across three generations. The exact number of carriers in family 11 and the total number of individuals sequenced are not stated.

extraction.extraction_notes: This is a whole-exome sequencing study of 3 multigenerational synesthesia families. Its only COL4A1 finding is a rare missense variant at 13:110866346 G/A segregating in family 11, among 37 candidate variants. No COL4A2 variants are reported. No functional work was done on the variant; expression data (GTEx, Human Protein Atlas, BrainSpan) are gene-level only. Pedigrees are shown in Fig. 1, which was not provided as text. The supplementary PDF was filtered: page 1 kept 3 of 81 rows, so the Sanger validation details are not visible.

variants.phenotype_details: Patient P21: intractable early-onset epilepsy classified as infantile spasms, onset before 3 years of age. The cohort inclusion criteria required no structural lesion on brain MRI, so no cerebrovascular or small-vessel findings are implied. No individual clinical details are given.
evidence_quotes: P21 | COL4A1 | AD | NM_001845.4 | c.2897G > A | p.Gly966Glu | Heterozygosity | Likely pathogenic | PS2, PM2, PP2, PP3, PP4 | de novo
A total of 74 unrelated pediatric patients with EOE without a known cause were recruited from the epilepsy clinic in Severance Children’s Hospital from March 2015 to May 2016.
A parental study was scheduled to detect de novo occurrence for the candidate pathogenic, likely pathogenic, and VUS variants in all available trios.
Infantile spasm | 51 | 16 | 35 | 31.4 | BRAT1 (1), CDKL5 (2), COL4A1 (1), DNM1 (1), GNAO1 (2), KCNQ2 (2), MECP2 (1), STXBP1 (3), WWOX (1), CNV (2)
variants.notes: The variant is listed as de novo in Table 1, and the ACMG criterion PS2 was applied; PS2 implies confirmed maternity and paternity. Parental testing via trio Sanger sequencing is described only generically in the Methods, not specifically for P21. The infantile spasm phenotype is inferred from the gene count in Supplementary Table S4. Inclusion criteria excluded patients with structural MRI lesions, which is notable for a COL4A1 carrier. No per-patient clinical description is provided. n_families is set to 1 on the basis of the trio parental study, not a documented pedigree.

extraction.extraction_notes: This is a targeted 172-gene NGS panel study of 74 unrelated Korean patients with intractable early-onset epilepsy. Only one COL4A1 variant is reported (P21) and no COL4A2 variants are reported. The cohort excluded patients with structural lesions on brain MRI. Per-patient phenotype data are not provided beyond the syndrome-level counts in Supplementary Table S4.

Whole exome sequencing case-control association study of raised atherosclerotic lesions in the PDAY autopsy cohort (359 cases, 626 controls; 985 total). The only COL4A1/COL4A2 variants reported are common polymorphisms tested for association: COL4A2 rs72657934 (intron 20, p=7.36E-06), and COL4A1 rs1562173, rs3742207 (Gln1134His), and rs16975492. These are reported with MAF, beta and p-values, not as variants in specific affected individuals, so per instructions no variant records were created. Rare-variant gene-based analyses did not highlight COL4A1/COL4A2. The rsID for the missense variant is given inconsistently in the text (rs3742207 vs rs3742007), and the Methods mention rs4773144 as the top hit.

Candidate-gene association study of 15 common polymorphisms in 2,609 Spanish rheumatoid arthritis patients (subclinical atherosclerosis assessed in 1,258). The only COL4A1/COL4A2 variant is the common intergenic/association SNP COL4A1-COL4A2 rs4773144 (A/G). It is reported only with association statistics (CV events OR 1.01, 95% CI 0.78-1.30, P=0.93; cIMT P=0.89; carotid plaques OR 0.95, P=0.62), and no association was found. No specific variants are reported in specific affected individuals, so no variant records were created.

This paper is about Alport syndrome genes COL4A5, COL4A3 and COL4A4. It is an aggregate analysis of LOVD database variants. COL4A1 and COL4A2 are mentioned only in Table 1, as 'COL4A1-like'/'COL4A2-like' chain family designations. No COL4A1 or COL4A2 variants are reported in any individual. All primary variant data are said to be in the LOVD databases, which were not provided.

This paper studies Alport syndrome and familial benign haematuria in a Hungarian cohort of 14 families and 3 individuals, plus 66 controls. It reports variants only in COL4A3, COL4A4 and COL4A5, sequenced with an AmpliSeq NGS panel. COL4A1 and COL4A2 were not sequenced. They are mentioned only in the introduction, as the collagen IV chains of the fetal glomerular basement membrane. No COL4A1 or COL4A2 variants are reported in any individual, so the variants list is empty.

This paper reports a novel COL4A4 splice variant (c.1459+1G>A, NM_000092.4) in a Chinese family with thin basement membrane nephropathy. COL4A3 was also screened and no variant was found. COL4A1 and COL4A2 were not screened, and no variants in them are reported; they are mentioned only in background discussion of collagen IV chains. The paper therefore contains no COL4A1/COL4A2 variant-level data.

This paper reports variants in COL4A3, COL4A4 and COL4A5 (Alport syndrome genes): COL4A3 G695R and L1474P, COL4A3 S1147F, COL4A4 P1587R, COL4A5 G1030S and G1161E. It also reports variants in SALL2, MYH9, LAMA5, PLCE1, NPHS1, CAPN12, ACTN4 and APOL1. No COL4A1 or COL4A2 variants are reported in any individual. COL4A1 and COL4A2 were not among the 19 genes on the multiplexed panel (Table S3). They may have been in the 292-gene panel (Table S1, not provided), but no COL4A1/COL4A2 variant was reported. COL4alpha1 appears only as immunohistochemistry staining (strong glomerular expression in the index patient), not as a genetic variant.

variants.as_written: An adenine to guanine transition (A3046G) in exon 36 substituted a methionine residue for a valine residue within the triple helical domain at amino acid number 1016 (p.M1016V)
variants.phenotype_details: Patient 1, diagnosed with Walker-Warburg syndrome: lissencephaly (severe cobblestone-type cortical malformation), hydrocephalus, Dandy-Walker malformation, optic nerve hypoplasia, hypotonia with congenital muscular dystrophy; MRI also showed diffusely abnormal white matter, thin brainstem, enlarged tectum, severe cerebellar hypoplasia, enlarged posterior fossa.
variants.functional_evidence: In stably transfected HT1080 cells the secreted/intracellular COL4A1 ratio for M1016V was reduced but variable and not statistically significant (n=9).
variants.prior_report_reason: Figure S4 states patient 1's MRI images are modified from Figure 1 in Kanoff et al. (1998) Pediatr Neurol, indicating the patient's clinical features were previously published (without COL4A1 genotype); patient is LP93-014 from the Dobyns database.
evidence_quotes: To test this, we performed direct sequence analysis of genomic DNA from a cohort of 27 patients with CMD (see Table S1 for primers).

The first mutation was identified in a patient diagnosed with WWS that had lissencephaly, hydrocephalus, Dandy-Walker malformation, optic nerve hypoplasia and was hypotonic with CMD (see Figure S4 and Text S1 for clinical details).

An adenine to guanine transition (A3046G) in exon 36 substituted a methionine residue for a valine residue within the triple helical domain at amino acid number 1016 (p.M1016V) and was not detected in 282 control chromosomes (Figure 8A).
Overall, the ratio of secreted/intracellular COL4A1 for the COL4A1M1016V mutation was reduced, however the results were variable (n = 9) and did not reach statistical significance.
variants.notes: No transcript stated; c. notation derived from 'A3046G' and consistent with codon 1016. Parental testing not described. Not a glycine substitution (Y-position methionine). COL4A2 not sequenced. Patient's clinical/imaging data previously published by Kanoff et al. 1998.

variants.as_written: A cytosine to guanine transversion (C3946G) in exon 44 substituted a glutamine residue for a glutamate residue within the triple helical domain of the protein at amino acid number 1316 (p.Q1316E)
variants.phenotype_details: Patient 2, unspecified CMD with ocular and cerebral involvement (Figure S4 describes a less severe MEB phenotype): mild gyral abnormalities/diffuse cobblestone-type cortical malformation, hydrocephalus (moderately enlarged lateral ventricles), retinal dysplasia, seizures, elevated CK, diffuse abnormal white matter signal, thin brainstem with flat pons. Carrier father apparently unaffected (non-penetrance).
variants.functional_evidence: In stably transfected HT1080 cells Q1316E clearly impaired COL4A1 secretion with intracellular accumulation of monomeric and heterotrimeric COL4A1 (p<0.001), similar to the G562E positive control.
evidence_quotes: The second mutation was identified in a patient with unspecified CMD with ocular and cerebral involvement.
The patient had mild gyral abnormalities, hydrocephalus, retinal dysplasia, seizures and elevated CK (see Figure S4 and Text S1 for clinical details).
Although this cytosine to guanine transversion was not detected in 286 control chromosomes, it was present in the paternal DNA.
Here, we observed non–penetrance of the COL4A1Q1316E mutation in the father of the affected child.

In contrast, and similar to the established COL4A1G562E mutation, the COL4A1Q1316E mutation clearly impaired COL4A1 secretion leading to intracellular accumulation (p<0.001), supporting the hypothesis that the COL4A1Q1316E mutation is pathogenic.
variants.notes: No transcript stated; c. notation derived from 'C3946G' and consistent with codon 1316. Inherited from an apparently unaffected father. Diagnosis described as unspecified CMD in main text but as MEB phenotype in Figure S4 legend.

extraction.extraction_notes: Mostly a mouse study (Col4a1 delta-ex40) plus screening of 27 CMD/MEB/WWS patients (negative for known dystroglycanopathy genes) by COL4A1 Sanger sequencing. Two common non-synonymous SNPs, silent and intronic variants are in Tables S2-S4 (not provided) and were not extracted. COL4A2 not sequenced. COL4A1 G562E used only as a functional assay positive control (no new patients), not extracted. Clinical details in Text S1 not provided.

Narrative review of hereditary connective tissue diseases in young adult stroke. The section on COL4A1/COL4A2 (Type IV collagen-related small vessel disease, HANAC) summarizes the prior literature only. It names no specific variants and reports no new individuals, so no variant records were created.

Perspective/review article on stroke genetics. COL4A1 is mentioned only generally (porencephaly, infantile hemiparesis, adult-onset small vessel disease with microbleeds), citing prior work. The paper reports no specific COL4A1/COL4A2 variants and no individual patients.

Methodological simulation study plus a candidate-gene association analysis of maternal/fetal genotype incompatibility in pre-eclampsia (324 case and 602 control mother/offspring pairs, Chile). The only COL4A2 variants reported are common intronic polymorphisms (rs2296849 and rs421177, plus COL4A2_633876793), given with incompatibility-model p-values and odds ratios. They are association SNPs, not variants found in specific affected individuals, so no variant records were created. None of these results was significant after FDR correction. No COL4A1 variants are reported.

variants.phenotype_details: Proband fetus (third pregnancy): Grade IV left periventricular germinal matrix hemorrhage at 23+4 weeks with progression to severe ventriculomegaly (15.96 mm) by 28 weeks, fetal growth restriction (EFW 0.2nd percentile); aberrant right subclavian artery and echogenic intracardiac focus at 16 weeks; terminated at 29 weeks. Carrier mother (33 y): childhood-onset left lower-limb claudication, left clubfoot, limb asymmetry, left upper-limb weakness; MRI right periventricular encephalomalacia with chronic right corticospinal tract Wallerian degeneration; persistent microscopic hematuria; 1.2-cm right renal simple cyst; retinal arteriolar tortuosity and A-V nicking; early-onset preeclampsia. Prior (second-pregnancy) fetus had similar Grade IV GMH but was not tested for the variant.
evidence_quotes: WES identified a heterozygous missense variant, COL4A1 (NM_001845.6) c.4249G>C (p.Gly1417Arg), in the fetus and mother; the father was wild‐type.
Fetal MRI at 23+4 weeks confirmed Grade IV left periventricular germinal matrix hemorrhage with mild ventriculomegaly (10.47 mm; Figure 4).
Renal: Persistent microscopic hematuria (urine occult blood 2+, RBC 15–20/HP) without proteinuria. Renal ultrasound demonstrated a 1.2‐cm simple cyst in the lower pole of the right kidney.
Funduscopy (Figure 6) revealed enhanced arteriolar reflexes, arteriovenous nicking, and localized retinal arteriolar tortuosity—all documented before the onset of preeclampsia.
ACMG/AMP classification—PM1 (critical functional domain), PM2_Supporting (absent from population databases), and PP3 (computational evidence)—yielded a VUS (Table 2).
variants.notes: Proband is the fetus of the third pregnancy; variant maternally inherited (mother heterozygous, father wild-type). Mother's own de novo status not assessable. n_tested=3 reflects the trio WES. The second-pregnancy fetus with similar hemorrhage was not tested for the variant. Functional validation stated to be ongoing; no results reported. 'Other' system reflects fetal growth restriction, cardiac/vascular ultrasound markers in the fetus, and maternal preeclampsia.

extraction.extraction_notes: Single-family case report. Mother also carries an incidental ~1.33 Mb 17p12 deletion (PMP22, HNPP) not inherited by the fetus; not recorded as a COL4A1/COL4A2 variant. Fetal autopsy declined.

Single case report of a 4-year-old girl with Gould syndrome. She had a 'de novo pathogenic change in the COL4A1 gene', but the paper never names the specific variant (no c./p. notation, no transcript), so no variant record was created. Parental testing is not described, so the de novo status would be 'assumed' rather than confirmed. Reported phenotype: periventricular white matter calcifications found incidentally on head CT at 9 months; mild developmental delays; colonic varices without portal hypertension, with hematochezia and symptomatic anemia at 4 years; abnormal mesenteric venous structures on CT angiography and TRICKS MRI. Ophthalmology follow-up is mentioned without findings; renal function and renal ultrasound were unremarkable; there was no cerebral hemorrhage. She also has oculocutaneous albinism, attributed to a separate gene mutation. If the variant is identified elsewhere, a curator could add a record: COL4A1, 1 proband, inheritance de novo assumed, phenotype systems small_vessel (questionable: white matter calcifications) and other (GI varices, developmental delay).

Methodology and preliminary-results paper for the Italian ALIGNED rare cerebrovascular disease network. This is a case report of a 41-year-old male with porencephaly and secondary psychosis. COL4A1 is mentioned only in general background, as a cause of familial porencephaly. No genetic testing was reported for the patient, and no specific COL4A1 or COL4A2 variant is described.

Narrative review of cerebral small vessel disease pathophysiology. Tables 2 and 3 (pathogenic variants in the population; common-variant associations) were not rendered beyond their captions and summarize prior literature and association data. No variant-level data on individuals is reported.

Retrospective study of 19 refractive surgery candidates (methods text says 18 patients/36 eyes; results say 19) who had AvaGen polygenic keratoconus risk testing. COL4A1 is reported only at the gene level: the test flagged it in 16 (84.2%) patients. No specific COL4A1 or COL4A2 variants (c./p. notation or rsIDs) are given for any individual. The flagged variants are polygenic risk-score markers rather than candidate causal variants, so no variant records were created. Gene distribution figures (Figures 4-5) were not provided as text.

Single case report of a male infant (born at 34 weeks) with fetal-diagnosed porencephaly, hemolytic anemia, jaundice, hydrocephalus, seizures, and later left ventricular outflow tract stenosis with mitral regurgitation and systolic anterior motion. The paper states only that he had 'a mutation in collagen type IV alpha 1 chain (COL4A1)' found by postnatal genetic analysis. No specific variant (c./p. notation) is given, so no VariantEvidence record was created. The authors say this patient's metabolic and muscular complications were described in a previous report (citation not rendered in the provided text). The same individual and variant are likely in that earlier publication, which a curator could check for the variant identity. The cardiac phenotype (LVOTS, abnormal papillary muscles, MR/SAM) is new information about this patient.

variants.phenotype_details: 20-year-old man with congenital porencephalic cyst (left sylvian fissure/inferior basal ganglia), congenital right hemiparesis and epilepsy since birth. evidence_quotes: He tested positive for a heterozygous mutation of the COL4A1 gene although his parents tested negative.

A 20-year-old man with a past medical history of epilepsy, congenital right hemiparesis, and congenital porencephalic cyst presented to the emergency department with witnessed generalized tonic-clonic seizures, three episodes at home and one in the emergency department.
A brain CT scan showed an intracerebral hemorrhage with porencephalic cyst and superior sagittal sinus thrombosis despite negative thrombophilia work-up.
The de novo mutation of the COL4A1 mutation in our patient could have contributed to the co-occurrence of both states.
variants.notes: The specific variant is not reported: no cDNA or protein change, transcript, or testing method is given. The paper states only that the patient carries a heterozygous COL4A1 mutation and that both parents tested negative. Parentage was not discussed. Without variant identity, this record cannot be matched to other reports.
